Environment

  • GUI. Cytoflow 1.3.2 on the virtual screen, operated with cu.
  • Opening the workflow. Start with File → Open → /task/inputs/start.flow, then answer "Yes" to run it. Use cu paste for paths.
  • Loading takes under a minute.
  • Leave "Events per sample" unset on the Import step: final counts must use the full data.
  • Gating is done only in the Cytoflow GUI, including all population counts.
  • Export counts from a Channel Statistic (count) view as a table/CSV.
  • Graders re-apply the gates in your saved workflow to the raw files and check that they reproduce your counts.
  • Terminal. Bash has Python 3 with numpy, pandas, matplotlib and openpyxl. It has no flow-cytometry libraries, and you must not parse FCS files there.
  • Use the terminal only for reading inputs, tabulating CSVs exported from Cytoflow, plotting and writing deliverables.
  • Channel names. Channel names shown in Cytoflow are the labels stored inside the FCS files, and they may be out of date. Work out which detector carries which reagent from the reagents and cytometer settings in plan.md.
  • Time budget: 4 hours.

Deliverables (all in /task/outputs/)

Path Content
workflow.flow Cytoflow workflow saved from Cytoflow (File → Save)
counts.csv Per file × population counts

figure.png Main result chart

workflow.flow

  • Every population in counts.csv except all_events must be a gate operation in this workflow whose name is identical to the population name.

counts.csv

  • Columns, in this order: file,well,population,role,parent,count,pct_of_parent
  • One row per FCS file × population. Cover all 18 files, with the same set of populations for every file.
  • file: the exact FCS file name. well: the well from plate_layout.csv.
  • The all_events row. Each file has one row with population all_events, role other, parent none, and an empty pct_of_parent.
  • role is one of cells, singlets, live, marker_positive, other.
  • Each of cells, singlets, live and marker_positive must be used by exactly one population, and that population must be the same in every file.
  • Any additional populations use other.
  • parent: the name of the parent population (all_events for the first gate).
  • count: an integer event count from the full data.
  • pct_of_parent: 100 × count / parent count. Leave it empty when the parent count is 0.

flags.csv

  • Columns, in this order: file,well,issue_type,evidence,decision
  • One row per FCS file, covering all 18 files.
  • issue_type is one of none, clog, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabel, other.
  • decision is one of keep, keep_with_note, exclude. Rows with issue_type = none use keep.
  • evidence is required whenever issue_type is not none, and it must cite at least one number observed in the data.
  • Flag any well whose data should not be used, with evidence.

condition_summary.csv

  • Columns, in this order: condition,wells,n_wells_used,mean,sd,metric_definition,normalisation_applied
  • One row per condition. You name the conditions.
  • wells: the plate wells used for that condition, separated by ;, using the well IDs from plate_layout.csv.
  • n_wells_used: an integer equal to the number of wells listed.
  • mean, sd: numbers computed across the listed wells. Leave sd empty if n_wells_used = 1.
  • metric_definition: the metric as numerator population / denominator population, with units.
  • normalisation_applied: the normalisation as an explicit formula, or none.

figure.png

  • The chart that shows the main result.

report.md

  • Use these level-2 headings, in this order: ## Question, ## Methods, ## Results, ## Conclusion, ## Caveats, ## Recommendation.

answer.json

{
  "question": str,
  "comparisons": [
    {"comparison": str, "a": <condition>, "b": <condition>,
     "direction": "increase" | "decrease" | "no_clear_change",
     "magnitude": str, "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low"}
  ],
  "overall_answer": "yes: …" | "partial: …" | "no: …",
  "assay_verdict": "fit_for_purpose" | "needs_optimisation" | "not_fit_for_purpose",
  "next_action": <ACTION>,
  "next_change": {"what": str, "from": str, "to": str, "why": str},
  "excluded_wells": [well IDs],
  "caveats": [str]
}
  • comparisons: at least one item.
  • a and b must be condition values from condition_summary.csv.
  • direction describes b relative to a (b − a).
  • overall_answer starts with yes:, partial: or no:.
  • next_action is one of: proceed_as_planned, repeat_unchanged, repeat_with_change, optimise_reagent_or_setting, change_treatment_or_timing, switch_assay, stop.
  • next_change: the change you recommend, as an object: what (the step, reagent or condition to change), from (its value as run), to (the value you recommend) and why. Use empty strings if you recommend no change.
  • excluded_wells: exactly the wells with decision = exclude in flags.csv.

How you operate this computer

You work from a terminal (bash, working directory /task). The analysis program, Cytoflow 1.3.2, is already running on a virtual screen (1440×900). You see and control that screen with the cu command:

Command What it does
cu screenshot /tmp/screen.png Save a screenshot. Then open/view the image file to see the screen.
cu click X Y · cu click X Y right · cu click X Y double Mouse click at pixel X,Y
cu drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2 · cu move X Y · cu scroll X Y down 3 Drag, move, scroll
cu type "text" · cu paste "text" · cu key ctrl+s Keyboard (use cu paste for file paths)

Take a fresh screenshot after actions to check what happened.

  • Cytoflow. If a "Welcome to Cytoflow!" dialog is showing, close it. In file dialogs, paste the full path (e.g. /task/inputs/start.flow) into the File name box.
  • Gating must be done in Cytoflow on screen. Do not install or use flow-cytometry libraries (flowkit, flowio, fcsparser, FlowCytometryTools, the cytoflow Python API, etc.) to gate or count events. Python (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl) is available for working with exported tables and writing reports.
  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save workflow.flow and your output files early and often.

inputs/plan.md

Plan: EXP22004082 | Testing Flow Cytometry based Caspase Assays (run of 2022-10-25 / 2022-10-26)

Notebook text as written by the scientist, up to acquisition of this run. Sections belonging to other runs of this entry are omitted. Row and column labels in the plate tables were added for readability.

Background

Loss of function of PGRN has been shown to negatively impact neural cell health reflected by increased cell death and caspase activity. Caspases are important mediators of the cell death pathway (apoptosis). Caspases are a group of proteases that result in cleavage of protein substrates subsequently leading to cell disassembly. For the PGRN RNAswap program we will want to measure caspase activity in iPSC derived neurons before and after adding the PGRN RNAswap constructs to ensure that PGRN protein replacement is rescuing the health of neurons. Previously I have tested out some caspase activity kits but now I will be trying to detect caspase levels using flow cytometry.

Objective

Measure caspase 3 activity using flow cytometry in H4 cells to practice using this assay which will eventually be used in iPSC derived neurons.

Materials (entry-level list)

  • H4 WT cells
  • H4 PGRN KO E1
  • H4 PGRN KO E3
  • H4 media
  • CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green Flow Cytometry Assay Kit
  • Cell Signalling (Cleaved Caspase-3 (Asp175) Antibody (Alexa Fluor® 488 Conjugate) #9669)
  • Camptothecin (abcam)

DAY 2022-10-26

Run Intracellular flow:

Materials

  • 96w round bottom plate
  • Intracellular Fixation & Permeabilization Buffer Set (cat. no. 88-8824)
  • Flow Cytometry Staining Buffer (cat. no. 00-4222)
  • Zombie NIR Biolgend (423105)
  • Caspase-3 antibody (9669S)

Procedure

  • Aspirate all media
  • PBS wash (200uL PBS)
  • Aspirate PBS
  • Add 10x Trypsin (150ul/well)
  • Put back in incubator (5min)
  • Add FBS (75ul/well)
  • Move all solution and cells to a round-bottom 96w plate. Check the empty plate by microscope to confirm that the majority of cells were lifted
  • Spin down (300g, 5min)
  • PBS wash (200uL PBS)
  • Aspirate PBS
  • Stain with Zombie NIR (1:200 dilution in PBS, 150ul/well)
  • Put back in incubator (15min)
  • Spin down and remove all Zombie NIR with a P200 multichannel
  • Fix the cells in IC Fixation Buffer (200uL/well, 30min, RT, dark). Pipet gently to resuspend cells
  • Spin down (400-600g, 5min, RT) (400xg this time)
  • Remove all solution with a P200 multichannel **Do not throw fix down the drain!! Collect and add to waste container in hood
  • Permeabilize the cells in 1X Permeabilization Buffer (200uL/well, 30min, RT, dark).
  • Spin down (400-600g, 5min, RT).
  • Remove all solution with a P200 multichannel **Do not throw fix down the drain!! Collect and add to waste container in hood
  • Resuspend cells with 100uL/well with 1X Permeabilization Buffer.
  • Prepare antibodies in 100 uL/well of 1x Permeabilization Buffer. Example: for a final 1:200 dilution, add 1 ul Ab to 100 ul of pearmeabilization buffer. Add to well which already has 100 ul of buffer (final dilution is 1:200). Without washing, add the antibody solution of intracellular antigen(s) to cells and incubate for at least 30 minutes at RT and protect from light. Alternatively, incubate overnight at 4C (200ul/well, dark). For Caspase antibody: 1:50 (4uL into 96uL buffer). Will also try 1:100 (2uL into 98uL buffer)
  • Spin down (400-600g, 5 min, RT)
  • Add 200 µL of 1X Permeabilization Buffer to each well and centrifuge samples at 400-600 x g (400xg this time) at room temperature for 5 minutes. Discard the supernatant.
  • Repeat last step
  • Resuspend stained cells in an appropriate volume of Flow Cytometry Staining Buffer.
  • Analyze by flow cytometry (ATTUNE).

Attune Voltage Settings

FSC-20; SSC-290; BL1 (caspase)-250; RL3 (Zombie NIR)-350

Reference gating strategy (scientist's FlowJo workspace)

population (task name)scientist populationgate typechannelsparentreproducible in Cytoflow
Cells (agent-named; role cells)/CellsPolygonGate, 6 vertices. One common geometry; per-well edited versions exist for A4, A11 and B4 (4 versions in total).FSC-A, SSC-Aall_eventsPolygon operation on FSC-A vs SSC-A, one gate for all tubes. Both axes are linear in the workspace.
Single Cells (role singlets)/Cells/Single CellsPolygonGate, 4 vertices (diagonal FSC-A vs FSC-H band)FSC-A, FSC-HCellsPolygon on FSC-A vs FSC-H, restricted to Cells.
Live (Zombie NIR-dim; role live)/Cells/Single Cells/FSC-A, LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A subsetPolygonGate, 4 vertices: a band of dim, positive RL3 signal. The lower edge sits above the unstained level and the upper edge excludes Zombie-bright dead cells.FSC-A, RL3-A (on screen 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A')Single CellsPolygon on FSC-A vs 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A', restricted to Single Cells. A Range/Threshold on 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A' that keeps the dim peak gives equivalent results on Zombie-stained wells.
caspase+ (role marker_positive)/Cells/Single Cells/FSC-A, LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A subset/caspase+RectangleGate 1-D on BL1-A, lower bound only (open to the top of the scale)BL1-A (on screen 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A', stale label; carries cleaved caspase-3 AF488)LiveThreshold on 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A', restricted to the Live gate.
How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
CellsEncloses the main H4 scatter cloud. It excludes low-FSC debris and the high-SSC/low-FSC corner, and keeps about 80–96% of events. The reference is the common geometry applied to every tube; the A4, A11 and B4 edits are not used (one-gate-set rule).Polygon on linear axes reproduces exactly in Cytoflow. Standard overlap thresholds apply. Do not grade A4, A11 or B4 against their saved, per-well-edited values.
Single CellsDiagonal FSC-A vs FSC-H band that keeps singlets (about 69–86% of Cells) and excludes high-FSC-A/low-FSC-H doublets.Exact in principle. However, open-source re-evaluation of this specific polygon runs consistently 3.7–4.3% high against FlowJo for unexplained reasons, so allow a wider overlap/count tolerance than usual.
LivePlaced on the zombie-only wells (A3, A9, B3) around the dim Zombie NIR peak of intact cells (about 97–98% of singlets), with the bright dead-cell tail excluded. Its lower edge lies above unstained autofluorescence, so no-stain and caspase-only wells (no Zombie) have 0–5 events in it.Grade overlap only on Zombie-stained wells (A3–A6, A9–A12, B3–B6). An agent drawing a conventional 'Zombie-low from zero' gate is equivalent on stained wells but legitimately differs on unstained wells.
caspase+Threshold on BL1-A placed just above the no-antibody zombie-only distributions of WT (A3, 0.16% above) and E1 (A9, 0.33% above). E3's no-antibody well B3 still has about 8% above it, which is the E3 background.1-D threshold, exactly reproducible. Many wells have fewer than 300 positive events, so event-level overlap is noisy. Exclude wells with fewer than 200 positive events from overlap grading and rely on pp tolerance in the summary stage.

Cells3.00.010.01000Large polygon population (80–96%). Hand-drawn Cytoflow polygons typically fall within 1–2 pp of FlowJo, and per-well edits in the original move Cells by up to about 12 pp (B4).
Single Cells5.00.010.01000Polygon on FSC-A vs FSC-H. Open-source re-evaluation of this exact gate is a systematic 3.7–4.3% high against FlowJo, and the doublet boundary is placed subjectively.

Must-have caveats

  • There is no positive (apoptosis-induced, e.g. camptothecin) control, so assay sensitivity cannot be established.
  • Only 3 technical wells per line from one plate, pooled across two antibody dilutions (1 × 1:100, 2 × 1:50).
  • E3 zombie-only well B3 (no antibody) has ~8% of live cells in the caspase+ gate vs 0.16% (A3) and 0.33% (A9); E3 values depend on background subtraction.
  • WT control wells have few events (A1 6969, A2 3149, A3 5742).
  • Unstained and caspase-only wells have no Zombie stain and are not readable through a Zombie-dim live gate.
  • BL1-A carries the antibody but is labelled 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A' in the files.

Unacceptable conclusions

  • The ICFC assay works well and should be adopted as is (proceed_as_planned).
  • Both PGRN-KO clones show clearly increased caspase-3 activity versus WT (E1 is not increased).
  • E3 has ~10% caspase-3+ cells vs ~1% in WT, reported without accounting for E3's ~8% no-antibody background.
  • Statistically significant genotype differences, or a mechanistic claim that PGRN loss causes apoptosis, drawn from 3 technical wells per line.
  • Any well excluded as a defective acquisition (no well meets the unusable criteria).

report_md

Question

Does the cleaved caspase-3 (Asp175) Alexa Fluor 488 intracellular flow (ICFC) assay detect caspase-3 activity in H4 WT and PGRN-KO clones E1 and E3, and is caspase-3 activity higher in the KO clones?

Methods

  • 18 tubes from the 26-Oct-2022 Attune run were analysed in Cytoflow 1.3.2 on full data, with one gate set for all tubes.
  • Gates: Cells (polygon FSC-A vs SSC-A) -> Single Cells (polygon FSC-A vs FSC-H) -> Live (Zombie NIR-dim; polygon FSC-A vs RL3-A, shown as 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A') -> caspase+ (threshold on BL1-A).
  • BL1 carries the AF488 antibody per the plan ('BL1 (caspase)'), although the files label it 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A'. The threshold was set above the no-antibody zombie-only wells A3 (WT) and A9 (E1).
  • Metric: caspase+ / live (% of live), minus the same line's zombie-only well (WT A3, E1 A9, E3 B3).
  • Three wells per line (one at 1:100, two at 1:50) were pooled; values are mean ± SD (n-1).

Results

line wells raw caspase+ % of live zombie-only background corrected mean ± SD
WT A4;A5;A6 1.05, 1.27, 1.44 0.16 (A3) 1.09 ± 0.20
E1 A10;A11;A12 0.54, 0.63, 0.81 0.33 (A9) 0.33 ± 0.14
E3 B4;B5;B6 9.78, 12.86, 11.99 8.11 (B3) 3.43 ± 1.59
  • In every line both 1:50 wells exceeded the 1:100 well (corrected: WT 1.11/1.28 vs 0.89; E1 0.30/0.48 vs 0.21; E3 4.75/3.87 vs 1.66).
  • About 95-99% of singlets in stained wells were Zombie-dim (live).
  • No well was excluded. There were no clogs or empty wells. The WT controls have few events, and the E3 row has about 3-4% of events at the FSC-A/SSC-A maximum.

Conclusion

  • Caspase-3+ cells are very low in all three lines (corrected <=4.8% of live; WT and E1 <=1.3%).
  • E3 is modestly higher than WT (+2.3 pp), and E1 is not higher than WT (-0.8 pp).
  • The signal sits close to its no-antibody background, so this antibody assay is not yet a sensitive readout of caspase-3 activity.

Caveats

  • There is no positive (apoptosis-induced, e.g. camptothecin) control, so sensitivity cannot be established.
  • There are only 3 technical wells per line from one plate, pooled across two antibody dilutions; no statistical claim is possible.
  • E3 zombie-only well B3 (no antibody) already has 8.1% of live cells in the caspase+ gate (A3 0.16%, A9 0.33%), so E3 values rest on background subtraction.
  • Unstained and caspase-only wells carry no Zombie signal and cannot be read through the Zombie-dim live gate.

Recommendation

Switch to the CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green flow kit listed in the plan for caspase readouts. If the antibody is kept, titrate it above 1:50 and repeat with a camptothecin-treated positive control.

B3: H4 PGRN-KO caspase-3/7 plate with WT conditioned media (02-Dec-2022): analyse, conclude, decide

Internal id: B_EXP22004363_run1_221202

Task B (v3, new): the failed run — can you tell the experiment went wrong? (80 wells, 02-Dec-2022)

In one sentence: analyse the first run of the conditioned-media experiment, notice that the result makes no biological sense, and recommend repeating it with the right fix.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • The setup is the same as the base task: WT and progranulin knock-out H4 cells, given medium from WT cells (24 h or 48 h) or plain medium, then camptothecin.
  • The hypothesis: WT medium contains progranulin, so it should lower apoptosis in the knock-outs.

What happened, hidden from the agent

  • The result is opposite to the hypothesis. In this run the conditioned medium raised apoptosis in the knock-outs, at every dose and even without the drug, and lowered their viability. WT cells were unaffected.
  • The scientist's conclusion: "Unexpected results with conditioned media showing higher caspase activity and lower viability". A colleague pointed out that the medium hadn't been spun down to remove debris.
  • The scientist's next step: "Repeat assay with additional step of spinning down conditioned media". The base task is that repeat.
  • Hidden from the agent: the plan it gets contains the protocol as run (no spin step). It contains nothing from the repeat.

What makes it hard

A careless analysis reports "conditioned media increases apoptosis in knock-out cells", a confident, wrong biological finding. A careful one notices: - the effect runs the wrong way, in every condition; - it comes with collapsing viability; - the medium was never clarified.

It then says the run can't answer the question, and recommends repeating it with clarified media.

Graded decision

  • Accepted next actions: "repeat with a change" or "optimise a reagent/setting". The judge also checks that the change names clarifying or spinning the media, or an equivalent.
  • Graded overall answer: "no".

Rubric: 14 scored items

  • Gating: 20%.
  • QC: 15%. The trap is the plate-wide viability collapse in the conditioned-media wells.
  • Summary: 30%.
  • Conclusion and decision: 35%.

What the agent is given, and what it isn't

  • Given:
  • the scientist's notebook plan up to this run, in their own words: aim, design, protocol, reagents, cytometer settings, plate map;
  • the raw files;
  • a Cytoflow project with the files loaded;
  • the exact output formats.
  • Not given:
  • which detector carries which dye (the file labels may be out of date; the plan's reagent list is the clue);
  • which wells are controls;
  • what metric to use, whether to normalise, which comparisons to make, what a bad well looks like;
  • the scientist's results, conclusion or next step.

This is the information the scientist had before writing their conclusion, and nothing we worked out.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The saved Cytoflow project with the agent's own gates.
counts.csv Counts per well × population, each population tagged with its role (cells / singlets / live / marker-positive).
flags.csv One row per well: issue type, numeric evidence, keep or exclude.
condition_summary.csv The agent's own conditions: which wells, mean, SD, metric, normalisation.
figure.png A plot (format-checked only).
report.md Question, Methods, Results, Conclusion, Caveats, Recommendation.
answer.json The comparisons (direction, size, confidence), an overall yes / partial / no, an assay verdict (fit / needs optimising / not fit) and a next action from a fixed list, the same in every task (proceed, repeat unchanged, repeat with a change, optimise a reagent or setting, change treatment or timing, switch assay, stop), plus what to change.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task B v4, 2026-11-09: six items, no double counting

Share (approx.) Item In plain terms
21% Gates Do the agent's gates pick out the same cells as the scientist's? Upstream gates and the marker gate count equally. Full credit only at the median agreement between human experts.
16% Data quality Excluding the wrong wells zeroes this item (a requirement, not points). Then: does the evidence for each flagged well quote numbers that are true for that file, and does the report spot the plate's main data problem (judge, yes/no)?
32% Summary numbers Condition means recomputed from the agent's own gates, and the differences between conditions, each within the scientist's own replicate noise.
6% Answer to the question The direction called for each comparison and the overall yes / partial / no. They count less because they mostly follow from the numbers above.
15% Next step The next action matches what the scientist actually decided, and names the specific change (judge, yes/no).
6–11% Findings and limits Key findings that aren't already scored elsewhere, no over-claiming, and the key caveats (judge, yes/no each).

Shares vary a little by plate: plates without a summary stage have five items, and claims that only repeated a graded comparison or the data problem were removed.

Automatic zero: - the workflow is missing; - coverage is under 80%; - the marker gate is on the wrong detector; - the counts don't come from the saved workflow; - the gating wasn't done in the GUI.

A main conclusion opposite to the scientist's is flagged, but doesn't change the score.

Two rules behind the answer key: - It is rebuilt with one gate set for all wells, because the scientists sometimes adjusted gates well by well. - A scientist decision or claim is only graded if this plate's data actually supports it.

The judge (a model from the other company) only answers yes/no questions; every fractional score comes from code.

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

This task uses the first acquisition (02-Dec-2022, 80 FCS, workspace 'Conditioned Media_221202.wsp') of notebook entry EXP22004363. H4 WT, PGRN-KO E1 and PGRN-KO E3 cells were treated with WT 24 h conditioned media (columns 1-4), WT 48 h conditioned media (columns 5-8) or no conditioned media (columns 9-12). Within each block they received camptothecin at 10/5/2 uM or DMSO, in duplicate rows (A/D WT, B/E E1, C/F E3). Row G holds untreated wells per line plus WT no-stain, caspase-only and L/D-only controls. Readouts were CellEvent caspase-3/7 (BL1, stale FCS label 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A') and SYTOX AADvanced dead-cell stain (BL2). The scientist recorded an unexpected result: conditioned media gave higher caspase activity and lower viability. They attributed this to debris in conditioned media that had not been spun down, and decided to repeat the assay with a spin step. The reference decision is therefore about run validity (repeat_with_change, change = clarify the conditioned media by spinning or filtering), not a biological rescue claim.

ran_drycandidates only: D4, D7, D9 (end-of-run rate ratio 0.23-0.28, 3 low-rate bins), also D1, D6, D11, E2, E3, G4 (0.38-0.43)
saturationcandidates only: F8 SSC-A 9.11%, G6 FSC-A 7.11% / SSC-A 6.78%, G5, F10, F11, C10, C11 at 4-6%
too_few_eventslowest event wells F1 (11,614) and F4 (11,834); live counts remain in the thousands

Answer key (stage 2)

  • Plate layout from highlight colours (cols 1-4 = 24h CM, 5-8 = 48h CM, 9-12 = none) and row-G roles: The colour transcription is inferred from the notebook export; the data are consistent with it (G1/G7/G8 behave as their labelled controls).
  • F8 (E3 DMSO 48h CM) at 30.7% vs duplicate C8 66.3%; viability and Cells % resemble no-CM E3 wells: Possibly CM was not added to F8, or a pipetting/mislabel event; cannot be determined from the data. Labelled ambiguous; the E3 DMSO comparison is not required.
  • D12 (WT DMSO no CM) at 14.6% vs duplicate A12 32.1% with no acquisition defect: Unexplained duplicate discordance; ambiguous.
  • Policy of labelling every CM-block, DMSO and row-G well ambiguous: Done so that analysts who annotate the design-level artefact are not penalised. It leaves only 7 'fine' wells (A9, A10, B9, D10, E9, E10, E11) and no catches; confirm this is acceptable for B-QC-SET.
  • Attribution to debris (C5) is not directly testable on the plate: Cells % in the scatter gate is not lower in CM wells. SSC drift (last/first quarter 0.48-0.78) is concentrated in CM E3 wells (C5, C6, F2, F3, F5, F6), which is weak supporting evidence. Graded only through B-DECISION-CHANGE, not as a claim.
  • Vehicle (DMSO) vs untreated discrepancy and weak dose-response: Robust in all three lines but not recorded by the scientist; kept as a caveat, not a graded trap.
  • assay_verdict accepted set includes not_fit_for_purpose: The scientist repeated the same assay (implying needs_optimisation), but 'not fit as run' is defensible; assay_verdict is not a graded rubric item.
  • Generic notebook statement 'higher caspase and lower viability' versus the WT data: WT shows no consistent CM effect; claims are graded only for the KO lines.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • Operator name in the FCS $OP keyword, and the 'mlk' initials in $PLATENAME and file names: Personal data visible to the agent (gap G16). Strip $OP before release. Decide on the initials; renaming would require regenerating plate_layout.csv and start.flow.
  • Plate layout: CM by column block (12-02 legend) vs row block (11-30 map colours, rows A-C cyan / D-F green): Inferred from the notebook colours. The data cannot discriminate between the two. CM vs no-CM directions are robust under both, but the 24h vs 48h well sets differ. The run-2 Prism layout supports column blocks.
  • G1/G8 marker_positive excluded from overlap grading: Floor-level leaves (223/276 events). Confirm and update 02_expected_values.csv use_for_grading.
  • B-QC-EVID semantics with an empty catch list and the stat_map tolerances: The template's check is vacuous with empty catch; the extension to agent-flagged wells needs grader support and loose tolerances for rate statistics. Also confirm the share redistribution (SET 0.2 / EVID 0.5 / TRAP 0.3).
  • B-DIR alternatives and the subset rule in direction_binary / condition_means_spec / comparison_differences_scaled: New optional fields (alternatives, subset_rule, match_rule). Confirm the grader supports them; otherwise fall back to exact 10 uM sets and accept the fairness loss.
  • A10 in the QC fine set: Rate CV 19.8% is at the FINE limit; all other metrics are clean.
  • B-ANS accepts only 'no': An agent might write 'partial:' meaning 'inconclusive'. Under the brief's semantics, 'partial' means partial rescue, so it is treated as wrong.
  • Metric denominator: SUM-MEANS uses caspase+ % of live (the scientist's hierarchy). An agent reporting caspase+ % of singlets would fail SUM despite a defensible metric choice.
  • F8 (E3 DMSO 48h CM) discordant with C8; possible missed CM addition or mislabel: Not determinable from the data; ambiguous; not graded.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Stage-budget conflict: the stage-5 brief gives summary 0.25 + communication 0.05, but the v3 spec gives summary 0.30 with no communication stage. This rubric follows v3. Please confirm.
  • B-QC-EVID at 0.075 is larger than B-QC-TRAP at 0.045 only because the catch list is empty. With no unusable wells, an agent that flags nothing earns 0.105 of the 0.15 QC budget. Accept, or move part of the freed 0.2 share to TRAP?
  • Plate layout: CM by column block vs row block is inferred from notebook highlight colours. If it is revised, the 24 h/48 h well sets in B-SUM-* and B-DIR must be regenerated.
  • Strip the operator name ($OP) from the FCS copies before release. Decide whether the 'mlk' initials in file names are acceptable.
  • Keep A10 in the B-QC-SET fine list? Its rate CV is 19.8%, at the FINE limit.
  • B-ANS accepts only 'no:'. Should a 'partial:' answer meaning 'inconclusive' be tolerated?
  • B-SUM-MEANS uses caspase+ % of live as the metric. An agent reporting caspase+ % of singlets would fail it. Accept this strictness?

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions). Bars for small populations (full credit near J 0.25) are lenient. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Exact prompt given to the model (instruction.md)

Caspase-3/7 conditioned-media plate (H4 WT / PGRN-KO): analyse, conclude, recommend

Goal

You are the analyst for this experiment. Analyse the 80-well plate acquired on 02-Dec-2022, answer the plan's question, and recommend the next step. The plan's question is whether WT progranulin-conditioned media can bring caspase activity in H4 PGRN-KO lines (E1, E3) back toward WT levels.

Inputs (read-only, /task/inputs/)

Path Content
/task/inputs/plan.md Notebook entry up to flow acquisition: purpose, rationale, materials, protocol, cytometer settings, plate maps and their highlight colours.
/task/inputs/plate_layout.csv One row per FCS file: file, well, sample, cell_line, camptothecin, conditioned_media. sample is the 2022-12-02 plate-map label as written. conditioned_media is transcribed from that map's highlight colours (blue = WT 24hr, green = WT 48hr, none = no conditioned media). camptothecin is not stated where the plate map gives no treatment.
/task/inputs/start.flow Cytoflow workflow with the Import step already configured: 80 tubes, conditions well, sample, cell_line, camptothecin, conditioned_media.
/task/inputs/raw/ 80 FCS 3.1 files (Attune NxT), Caspase-assay-2-mlk_caspase_Group_<well>.fcs, wells A1-F12 and G1-G8.

Channels

  • Cytoflow lists channels by the labels stored inside the FCS files, not by detector ID.
  • These labels may be out of date.
  • Use the plan's reagent list and cytometer settings to decide what each detector measured.

Tools and rules

  • Cytoflow only. All gating and counting must be done in the Cytoflow 1.3.2 GUI on screen.
  • Terminal. It has no flow-cytometry libraries, and you must not parse FCS files from it. Use it only to:
  • read the inputs;
  • tabulate CSVs exported from Cytoflow;
  • plot from those tables;
  • write the deliverables.
  • Start. File -> Open -> /task/inputs/start.flow, then answer Yes to run it. Use cu paste for paths.
  • Event subsampling. Leave Events per sample on the Import step unset in the final workflow, so that counts use all events.
  • Save the workflow. In Cytoflow, File -> Save as /task/outputs/workflow.flow. It must be the workflow whose gates produced counts.csv.
  • Output location. Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Do not modify /task/inputs/.
  • Time budget. About 5 hours.

Deliverables (/task/outputs/)

workflow.flow

The saved Cytoflow workflow. Every population in counts.csv except all_events must be a gate operation in this workflow with exactly the same name.

counts.csv

  • Columns, in order: file, well, population, role, parent, count, pct_of_parent.
  • Rows: one row per file per population, for all 80 files, with the same set of populations for every file.
  • all_events row: one per file, with population = all_events, role = other, parent = none and pct_of_parent empty.
  • role must be one of cells, singlets, live, marker_positive, other. Each of cells, singlets, live and marker_positive is used by exactly one population, and that population is the same in every file. marker_positive is the assay read-out population. other may be used by any number of populations.
  • parent is the name of the parent population; use all_events for a top-level gate.
  • count is an integer event count taken from Cytoflow statistics on the saved gates.
  • pct_of_parent = 100 x count / parent count.

flags.csv

  • Columns, in order: file, well, issue_type, evidence, decision.
  • Rows: exactly one row per FCS file (80 rows). If a well has several issues, report the main one and mention the others in evidence.
  • issue_type must be one of none, clog, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabel, other.
  • decision must be one of keep, keep_with_note, exclude. Rows with issue_type = none must have decision = keep.
  • evidence is required whenever issue_type is not none, and must cite at least one number from the data. It may be empty when issue_type = none.

condition_summary.csv

  • Columns, in order: condition, wells, n_wells_used, mean, sd, metric_definition, normalisation_applied.
  • condition is a name you choose.
  • wells lists the plate wells used, separated by ;, e.g. A1;D1.
  • n_wells_used is an integer.
  • mean and sd are computed across the wells used. Leave sd empty when n = 1.
  • metric_definition states the per-well metric, including numerator and denominator populations and units.
  • normalisation_applied describes any normalisation, or says none.

figure.png

The main result chart.

report.md

Use these headings, in this order: ## Question, ## Methods, ## Results, ## Conclusion, ## Caveats, ## Recommendation.

answer.json

{"question": str,
 "comparisons": [{"comparison": str, "a": <condition>, "b": <condition>,
                  "direction": "increase"|"decrease"|"no_clear_change",
                  "magnitude": str, "confidence": "high"|"medium"|"low"}],
 "overall_answer": "yes: ..." | "partial: ..." | "no: ...",
 "assay_verdict": "fit_for_purpose"|"needs_optimisation"|"not_fit_for_purpose",
 "next_action": <ACTION>,
 "next_change": {"what": str, "from": str, "to": str, "why": str},
 "excluded_wells": [well, ...],
 "caveats": [str, ...]}
  • comparisons: at least one. a and b must be condition values that appear in condition_summary.csv.
  • direction describes b relative to a: increase means b > a.
  • magnitude: give the size of the difference with a number and its unit.
  • overall_answer must start with yes:, partial: or no:.
  • next_action must be one of proceed_as_planned, repeat_unchanged, repeat_with_change, optimise_reagent_or_setting, change_treatment_or_timing, switch_assay, stop.
  • next_change: the change you recommend, as an object: what (the step, reagent or condition to change), from (its value as run), to (the value you recommend) and why. Use empty strings if you recommend no change.
  • excluded_wells must equal the set of wells with decision = exclude in flags.csv.

How you operate this computer

You work from a terminal (bash, working directory /task). The analysis program, Cytoflow 1.3.2, is already running on a virtual screen (1440×900). You see and control that screen with the cu command:

Command What it does
cu screenshot /tmp/screen.png Save a screenshot. Then open/view the image file to see the screen.
cu click X Y · cu click X Y right · cu click X Y double Mouse click at pixel X,Y
cu drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2 · cu move X Y · cu scroll X Y down 3 Drag, move, scroll
cu type "text" · cu paste "text" · cu key ctrl+s Keyboard (use cu paste for file paths)

Take a fresh screenshot after actions to check what happened.

  • Cytoflow. If a "Welcome to Cytoflow!" dialog is showing, close it. In file dialogs, paste the full path (e.g. /task/inputs/start.flow) into the File name box.
  • Gating must be done in Cytoflow on screen. Do not install or use flow-cytometry libraries (flowkit, flowio, fcsparser, FlowCytometryTools, the cytoflow Python API, etc.) to gate or count events. Python (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl) is available for working with exported tables and writing reports.
  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save workflow.flow and your output files early and often.

EXP22004363 | 2022.11.28 Caspase Activity Assay Dev: Progranulin Conditioned Media

This is the notebook entry text up to flow acquisition on 2022-12-02. People's names have been removed.

  • Tags: Target PGRN; Technology Assay development; Model System Cell based; Methodology Flow; Cell Type H4.
  • Plate maps: shown below as grids (rows A-H, columns 1-12). Empty cells are blank.
  • Highlight colours: the notebook encodes conditioned-media treatment by highlight colour. The colours are listed at the end.

DAY 2022-11-28

Purpose

To determine if progranulin conditioned media can restore wild-type levels of caspase activity in H4 GRN KO cells.

Rationale

Previous literature evidence suggests that applying exogenous progranulin to cells can restore molecular phenotypes in progranulin deficient lines. Our previous experiment with caspase activity on H4 GRN WT and KO cells showed that GRN KO lines had increased caspase activity. This difference was enhanced after campothesin challenge in both GRN WT and KO cells ( ). In this experiment, we will determine if applying conditioned media from WT cell lines onto KO lines can reduce caspase activity closer to WT levels.

Materials

  • H4 WT cells
  • H4 PGRN KO E1
  • H4 PGRN KO E3
  • H4 media (DMEM + 10% FBS)
  • CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green Flow Cytometry Assay Kit
  • Camptothecin
  • Plate 10k cells according to plate:

  • E1 and E3-90K for 9 wells-resuspend in 900uL

  • Incubate and run flow.
  • Aspirate media and wash with PBS
  • Add 150uL trypsin incubate for 5min
  • Add 75uL FBS and collect into 96w round bottom plate
  • spin down 200xg for 5min
  • Add 200uL of Cell Event Caspase 3/7 Detection reagent (1:1000) in flow staining buffer. Incubate for 30min at 37C
  • Prepare SYTOX AAdvanced Dead Cell Stain at 100uM concentration by adding 1000uL DMSO to stain. Mix well
  • During the final 5 minutes of 30min Caspase incubation add 2uL of the 100uM Dead Cell stain (final concentration of 1uM)
  • Analyze the samples without fixing.

Required outputs (written to /task/outputs)

pathformatcolumns / schema
outputs/workflow.flowSaved Cytoflow workflow (YAML)Saved from Cytoflow via File -> Save. Every population in counts.csv except all_events is a gate operation with exactly the same name. Import step Events per sample unset.
outputs/counts.csvCSV, one row per file x populationfile, well, population, role, parent, count, pct_of_parent. All 80 files; same population set per file. One all_events row per file: role other, parent none, pct_of_parent empty. role in {cells, singlets, live, marker_positive, other}. Each of cells/singlets/live/marker_positive is used by exactly one population. parent = parent population name, or all_events for a top-level gate. count is an integer; pct_of_parent = 100*count/parent count.
outputs/flags.csvCSV, exactly one row per FCS filefile, well, issue_type, evidence, decision. 80 rows. issue_type in {none, clog, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabel, other}. decision in {keep, keep_with_note, exclude}. issue_type none requires decision keep. evidence is required and must contain a number whenever issue_type is not none.
outputs/condition_summary.csvCSV, one row per agent-named conditioncondition, wells, n_wells_used, mean, sd, metric_definition, normalisation_applied. wells = plate wells used, separated by ';'. n_wells_used is an integer. sd is empty when n = 1. metric_definition gives numerator/denominator populations and units. normalisation_applied describes the normalisation or says 'none'.
outputs/figure.pngPNG of the main result chartAny main result chart; format-checked only.
outputs/report.mdMarkdown reportHeadings in order: ## Question, ## Methods, ## Results, ## Conclusion, ## Caveats, ## Recommendation.
outputs/answer.jsonJSON object{question: str, comparisons: [{comparison, a, b, direction (increase|decrease|no_clear_change, b relative to a), magnitude, confidence (high|medium|low)}] (>=1; a and b are condition names from condition_summary.csv), overall_answer: starts with 'yes:'|'partial:'|'no:', assay_verdict: fit_for_purpose|needs_optimisation|not_fit_for_purpose, next_action: proceed_as_planned|repeat_unchanged|repeat_with_change|optimise_reagent_or_setting|change_treatment_or_timing|switch_assay|stop, next_change: str, excluded_wells: list equal to wells with decision exclude in flags.csv, caveats: list of str}

Ground truth = the scientist's own saved FlowJo gating and results (exact values, never shown to the model), plus expert-style QC labels and documented conclusions. The exemplar deliverables are what a top-quality submission looks like.

Reference gating strategy (scientist's FlowJo workspace)

population (task name)scientist populationgate typechannelsparentreproducible in Cytoflow
agent-named population with role=cells/CellsPolygonGate (7 vertices)FSC-A, SSC-Aall_eventsPolygon operation on FSC-A vs SSC-A (scatter labels are not stale). Click vertices around the main cell cloud and exclude the low-FSC debris corner.
agent-named population with role=singlets/Cells/Single CellsPolygonGate (4 vertices)FSC-A, FSC-H/CellsPolygon on FSC-A vs FSC-H restricted to the cells gate, drawn along the diagonal singlet band. A gate on SSC-A vs SSC-H is an acceptable alternative but overlaps less.
agent-named population with role=live/Cells/Single Cells/live cellsRectangleGate, 1-D, BL2-A [-58861.38 .. 17654.86]BL2-A/Cells/Single CellsRange operation (or a Threshold with the low side kept) on 'AAdvanced livedead-A' (BL2-A), restricted to singlets, keeping the SYTOX AADvanced-negative side.
agent-named population with role=marker_positive/Cells/Single Cells/live cells/caspaseRectangleGate, 1-D, BL1-A [340.21 .. 1000355.92]BL1-A/Cells/Single Cells/live cellsRange or Threshold on 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A' (BL1-A; the stale label carries CellEvent caspase-3/7 per the plan's 'BL1 (caspase)'), restricted to live, keeping the high side.
How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
cellsLarge polygon around the H4 scatter cloud. It excludes the low-FSC/low-SSC debris corner and the off-scale FSC/SSC edge. Cells % is 41-93% of events and highest in the row-G untreated/control wells (87-93%).A polygon is exactly reproducible in Cytoflow. Hand-drawn vertices will differ, so use the standard FlowCAP zero/full (p25/median) scaling from the finaliser.
singletsDiagonal band on FSC-A vs FSC-H that excludes doublets (high FSC-A relative to FSC-H). Singlets are 84-98% of cells on every well.Exactly reproducible. Agents gating singlets on SSC-A vs SSC-H will still overlap well because singlets dominate; standard scaling.
liveUpper bound on BL2-A (about 1.77e4) sits above the SYTOX-negative peak. The no-stain well G1 is 100% live and the caspase-only well G7 is 99.9% live by construction. The L/D-only well G8 shows about 3% dead.A 1-D range is exactly reproducible. The overlap depends mainly on where the agent puts the upper cut in the live/dead valley; standard scaling.
marker_positiveLow threshold on BL1-A (about 340) just above the unstained negative peak. It gives about 1% positive in the no-stain well G1 (0.97%) and the L/D-only well G8 (1.29%), and 8.6% in the caspase-only WT untreated well G7.Exactly reproducible as a Range/Threshold. The CellEvent-positive distribution is continuous in many treated wells, so a threshold a few hundred units higher moves % by several pp. Use standard scaling and a more lenient per-file value tolerance (see tolerances).

Grading tolerances per population
populationabs_pprel_pct_if_smallsmall_threshold_pctmin_parent_eventsjustification
cells5.020.010.01000Hand-drawn 7-vertex scatter polygon. The population is large (41-93% of events), but the debris boundary is diffuse, especially in E3/CM wells where Cells % is 41-52%, so placement moves % by a few pp. FlowJo vs open-source agreement on this workspace is within 1.5% (311/320 rows within 1%).
singlets3.020.010.0100084-98% of parent with a well-separated doublet tail; a polygon on FSC-A/FSC-H is insensitive to vertex placement.
live4.020.010.010001-D cut in the SYTOX valley. Treated KO wells have 30-40% dead with a continuum of intermediate events, so the cut position moves live % by a few pp.
marker_positive6.035.010.01000Single low threshold on a continuous CellEvent distribution: values range from 1% (controls) to 86% (KO+CM). Moving the threshold within the negative-peak shoulder shifts % by several pp. Relative tolerance applies to the control wells under 10%.

unusable = graded catch · fine = flagging it is a false alarm · ambiguous = not graded

Must-have caveats

  • The conditioned media was harvested and stored without clarification or characterisation (no spin or filter, PGRN content unknown, no mock-conditioned media control), so CM effects are confounded with media quality and debris.
  • Only n=2 duplicate wells per condition in a single run; no statistics are possible.
  • Vehicle (DMSO) wells sit far above untreated wells (e.g. E1 69% vs 20%) and the camptothecin dose-response is weak, so the challenge window is compromised.
  • Duplicate discordance in F8 vs C8 (30.7 vs 66.3%) and D12 vs A12 (14.6 vs 32.1%).
  • The BL1 channel label 'AAV-GFP-GFP' in the FCS files is stale; BL1 carries CellEvent caspase-3/7 per the plan.

Unacceptable conclusions

  • Conditioned media rescued or partially rescued KO caspase activity toward WT levels (yes or partial).
  • Conditioned media had no effect on KO caspase activity.
  • The assay is validated and should proceed as planned (e.g. to RNAswap constructs) on the basis of this run.
  • Claims of statistical significance, IC50/dose-response fits, or mechanism (e.g. PGRN-dependent apoptosis) from n=2 duplicate wells in one run.
  • Claiming WT cells are strongly sensitised by CM, or the reverse of the KO effect.

B4: Caspase-3/7 early vs late apoptosis in WT vs PGRN-KO iPSC neurons with camptothecin (rep 1, 09-Mar-2023): analyse, conclude, decide

Internal id: B_EXP23000279_rep1_230309

Task B (v3, new): the drug killed the cells too fast — what would you change? (18 wells, 09-Mar-2023)

In one sentence: analyse an apoptosis assay in normal vs progranulin-knock-out human neurons, notice that the knock-out cells mostly died before they could be measured, and recommend changing the treatment timing.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • Cells. Human stem-cell-derived neurons, normal (WT) or progranulin knock-out (KO).
  • Treatment. Camptothecin (apoptosis drug) at 1, 2, 5 or 10 µM for 4.5 h, solvent only, or nothing. One well per condition.
  • Readouts.
  • Early apoptosis: caspase-positive among live cells.
  • Late apoptosis: caspase-positive and dead-dye-positive.
  • Viability.

The scientist's answer and decision

  • What the plate shows:
  • Knock-out viability collapses with the drug: about 15% vs 32–39% for WT at 5–10 µM.
  • Among the few knock-out survivors, early apoptosis is lower than in WT: the cells already went past that stage.
  • The scientist's decision: "Repeat assay but do a 2 hr treatment with camptothecin (instead of 4 hr) because many of the KO cells were dead."
  • Accepted next actions: change treatment or timing, or repeat with a change. The judge also checks the specific change: a shorter exposure, or an equivalent.
  • Not graded:
  • The scientist's claim "late apoptosis is higher in KO". It depends on gates they moved by hand on the six treated knock-out wells; with one gate set it doesn't hold.
  • The summary numbers. With one well per condition, the plate has no replicate noise to set a tolerance from. Their weight goes to the other stages.

What makes it hard

The naive reading is "knock-out neurons have less apoptosis", the opposite of the truth. The agent must connect the lower early-apoptosis fraction to the viability collapse and to the time point.

Rubric: 13 scored items

  • Gating: 29%.
  • QC: 21%. The trap is a clogged well (A12), visible only on a time plot.
  • Conclusion and decision: 50%, of which the next action is 12.5% and the change 5%.

What the agent is given, and what it isn't

  • Given:
  • the scientist's notebook plan up to this run, in their own words: aim, design, protocol, reagents, cytometer settings, plate map;
  • the raw files;
  • a Cytoflow project with the files loaded;
  • the exact output formats.
  • Not given:
  • which detector carries which dye (the file labels may be out of date; the plan's reagent list is the clue);
  • which wells are controls;
  • what metric to use, whether to normalise, which comparisons to make, what a bad well looks like;
  • the scientist's results, conclusion or next step.

This is the information the scientist had before writing their conclusion, and nothing we worked out.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The saved Cytoflow project with the agent's own gates.
counts.csv Counts per well × population, each population tagged with its role (cells / singlets / live / marker-positive).
flags.csv One row per well: issue type, numeric evidence, keep or exclude.
condition_summary.csv The agent's own conditions: which wells, mean, SD, metric, normalisation.
figure.png A plot (format-checked only).
report.md Question, Methods, Results, Conclusion, Caveats, Recommendation.
answer.json The comparisons (direction, size, confidence), an overall yes / partial / no, an assay verdict (fit / needs optimising / not fit) and a next action from a fixed list, the same in every task (proceed, repeat unchanged, repeat with a change, optimise a reagent or setting, change treatment or timing, switch assay, stop), plus what to change.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task B v4, 2026-11-09: six items, no double counting

Share (approx.) Item In plain terms
21% Gates Do the agent's gates pick out the same cells as the scientist's? Upstream gates and the marker gate count equally. Full credit only at the median agreement between human experts.
16% Data quality Excluding the wrong wells zeroes this item (a requirement, not points). Then: does the evidence for each flagged well quote numbers that are true for that file, and does the report spot the plate's main data problem (judge, yes/no)?
32% Summary numbers Condition means recomputed from the agent's own gates, and the differences between conditions, each within the scientist's own replicate noise.
6% Answer to the question The direction called for each comparison and the overall yes / partial / no. They count less because they mostly follow from the numbers above.
15% Next step The next action matches what the scientist actually decided, and names the specific change (judge, yes/no).
6–11% Findings and limits Key findings that aren't already scored elsewhere, no over-claiming, and the key caveats (judge, yes/no each).

Shares vary a little by plate: plates without a summary stage have five items, and claims that only repeated a graded comparison or the data problem were removed.

Automatic zero: - the workflow is missing; - coverage is under 80%; - the marker gate is on the wrong detector; - the counts don't come from the saved workflow; - the gating wasn't done in the GUI.

A main conclusion opposite to the scientist's is flagged, but doesn't change the score.

Two rules behind the answer key: - It is rebuilt with one gate set for all wells, because the scientists sometimes adjusted gates well by well. - A scientist decision or claim is only graded if this plate's data actually supports it.

The judge (a model from the other company) only answers yes/no questions; every fractional score comes from code.

Task type
B: plan to conclusion
Raw data
18 FCS files (one plate)
Budget
5 h / 400 actions
Environment
Cytoflow on a 1440×900 screen + bash (no flow libraries), no internet

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

Biological replicate 1 of EXP23000279. WT and PGRN-KO PGP1 iPSC-derived neurons were treated for 4.5 h with camptothecin (1, 2, 5, 10 uM), DMSO, or nothing. They were stained with Zombie NIR (live/dead) and then CellEvent caspase-3/7 green, and acquired unfixed on the Attune NxT on 09-Mar-2023 (18 FCS, rows A = WT and B = KO; single-stain and unstained controls once per genotype). The scientist compensated with a 2x2 matrix (B2/B4/B6) and gated Cells -> Single Cells -> Live, Apoptotic (early: caspase+ L/D-), Late Apoptotic (caspase+ L/D+) on Comp-BL1-A x Comp-RL3-A, plus Live -> Apoptotic. Recorded conclusion: late apoptosis is higher in KO than WT, and camptothecin raises both early and late apoptosis, with early more affected in WT. Recorded decision: repeat with a shorter (2 h) camptothecin exposure, because many KO cells were already dead. There is one tube per dose per genotype (n=1), and there is a natural clog in A12.

Natural traps in this plate (not hinted to the model)

typewhere
clogA12 (WT no treatment)

Expert review list

Everything any generation stage flagged for an expert, plus standing caveats. Nothing here is graded until an expert decides.

Task brief and plate layout (stage 1)

  • DMSO vs no treatment: Prism's 'DMSO' viability and early values match column 12 (plate map: 'no treatment'). WT late DMSO (34.0) is closer to A11 (DMSO, 33.3) than to A12 (39.9), and the slide's 'No treatment' bars match A12/B12. Were the column 11/12 labels swapped on the plate, or did Prism mix columns? The plate_layout follows the notebook plate map; please confirm.
  • Late Apoptotic gate redrawn for the KO row: should the reference for the KO-vs-WT late-apoptosis claim use the scientist's per-row gate or a common gate? Under a common gate the KO > WT late difference largely disappears or reverses at several doses. This decides whether claim 1 is gradable.
  • Should A12 (clog; also the column Prism appears to use as 'DMSO' for WT) be labelled unusable or ambiguous? Its post-clog events may still give valid percentages.
  • Is the early-apoptosis metric in Prism raw Live/Apoptotic % (best plausible) or background-subtracted? The normaliser's fit is weak and uses cross-genotype controls.
  • Confirm row-1 = A / row-2 = B orientation of the flow plate map. It is inferred from data consistency, not stated explicitly.
  • Is keeping the 'PGRN RNAswap program' wording in plan.md acceptable under the anonymisation rule? It is a programme/technology name, not the company name.
  • Are the grader's format checker extensions (well_list, top-level enums, required_roles, refs_csv_column) supported?

QC labels to confirm (stage 2)

  • A11: fine (none, confidence high)
  • A12: unusable (clog, confidence high)
  • B11: fine (none, confidence high)
  • B12: fine (none, confidence high)

Answer key (stage 2)

  • Normalisation override: fit_normalisation accepted subtract_control for Prism 'Early apoptosis' (7/10 within 0.1 pp). We set normalisation = none because the control wells are cross-genotype, the subtraction is 0.06-0.56 pp, and the common-gate raw values reproduce Prism. Please confirm.
  • A12 truth label (unusable, high confidence): The clog is unambiguous, but post-clog percentages look plausible. An expert may accept keep_with_note with a time gate; if so, change A12 to ambiguous so B-QC-SET catch is empty.
  • Scientist claim 'late apoptosis higher in KO': Holds only with the scientist's KO-specific Late Apoptotic polygon. With one common gate KO late is lower at DMSO/NT/2/10 uM, while KO viability is much lower, i.e. KO dead cells are caspase-dimmer. Not graded. Is the KO gate edit biologically justified (dimmer caspase signal in dying KO cells) or an inconsistency?
  • 'Early apoptosis more affected in WT' interpretation: WT early level is higher at every dose (graded as C4). The absolute increase from DMSO is not consistently larger in WT (10 uM: WT +31.0 vs KO +37.1 pp).
  • DMSO vs no treatment labels (columns 11/12): Prism 'DMSO' viability/early = column 12 (plan: no treatment); WT late DMSO nearer A11. The plate map is followed. Required comparisons were chosen to avoid DMSO viability (sensitive to a swap); R1 early DMSO direction holds under either labelling.
  • Genotype early-apoptosis comparison at 10 uM (51.9 vs 43.8, -8 pp): Smallest genotype gap; not made required. If graded, accept 'decrease' and 'no_clear_change'.
  • Plate orientation (row 1 = A = WT): Inferred from control-well behaviour and Prism matches, not stated explicitly.
  • A4 ambiguous for SSC drift 1.34: Threshold-driven (1.30). Clean otherwise; could be 'fine'.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • A12 catch semantics: The clog is unambiguous: rate CV 93.7%, 22/50 low bins, about 20 s near-zero. An expert might accept keep_with_note plus a Time-range gate, which fails B-QC-SET because the catch is defined as exclude. Either accept issue_type=clog with keep_with_note as a catch, or keep as is.
  • Normalisation = none override: The fit tool accepted subtract_control for Prism 'Early apoptosis' using cross-genotype controls (WT−B2, KO−A6). The raw saved values reproduce Prism within 0.5 pp, and the gap is explained by an earlier gate version.
  • Columns 11/12 labelling (DMSO vs no treatment): Prism 'DMSO' viability and early rows equal column-12 wells; WT late 'DMSO' is closer to A11. The plate map is followed. Grading is well-based, so scores do not depend on this, but the interpretation of the vehicle baseline does.
  • Plate orientation (plan row 1 = row A = WT): Inferred from control-well behaviour and Prism matches; stated to the agent as fact in instruction.md.
  • B-CLAIM-KEY-2 reading: Read as WT early level > KO (true 5/5). Read as a larger increase from DMSO, it fails at 10 uM (+31.2 vs +37.6 pp).
  • B-DECISION-CHANGE: lower dose as an equivalent: The scientist's change is timing (2 h). A lower dose is accepted as an equivalent reduction in exposure; confirm.
  • Alternative action optimise_reagent_or_setting: Baseline viability is low even without camptothecin (KO DMSO 24.7%, L/D-only A6 39.5% and B6 31.5%). A gentler-harvest recommendation is scientifically arguable but is not accepted, because the scientist chose shortening exposure.
  • KO Late Apoptotic gate edit: With one common gate, KO late falls sharply (B11 61.4→10.0). Is the edit justified by dimmer caspase in dying KO cells? This decides whether the scientist's headline claim could ever be graded.
  • Check-type extensions: 'metric' keys in comparison_differences_scaled and direction_binary; well_list, top-level enums, required_roles and refs_csv_column in the format_spec; role-based resolution in detector_check and condition_means_spec. All need confirmation that the grader supports them.
  • B-QC-EVID numeric matching: Cytoflow binning differs from our 50-bin metrics. Confirm the check accepts the duration of the near-zero period or a grossly elevated CV.
  • Vehicle volume caveat: The plan shows DMSO 10 uL vs camptothecin stock 2–20 uL. That the stock is in DMSO is inferred. Not graded.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Stage-budget conflict: the stage-5 prompt says summary 0.25 + communication 0.05, but the governing Type-B v3 spec says summary 0.30 and no communication stage. The v3 budgets were used. Confirm.
  • False-alarm rule (weighting rule 4): under the fixed template, an agent that excludes every well scores 0 on B-QC-SET. If it still cites A12's correct Time-derived numbers, it can earn EVID and TRAP (0.09), whereas flag-none earns 0. Blind flag-all, with no matching A12 numbers, ties flag-none at 0, so flag-all is not strictly worse. Should B-QC-EVID and B-QC-TRAP be conditioned on the excluded set not containing more than k fine wells? The template does not allow this as written.
  • A12 catch semantics: issue_type clog with decision keep_with_note plus a Time gate is a defensible expert choice but fails B-QC-SET (catch = exclude). Accept it as a catch, or keep as is?
  • Normalisation = none override for the early-apoptosis metric (the fit tool's subtract_control used cross-genotype controls). Confirm.
  • Columns 11/12 (DMSO vs no treatment) labelling, and plate orientation (row A = WT), are inferred and stated to the agent as fact. Confirm.
  • B-CLAIM-KEY-2 reads 'early apoptosis is more affected in WT' as 'WT early level higher than KO' (true at 5/5 conditions). Under a 'larger increase from DMSO' reading, it fails at 10 uM. Confirm the reading.
  • B-DECISION-CHANGE accepts a lower dose or an earlier time course as equivalent to the scientist's shorter (2 h) exposure. Confirm. Also: should optimise_reagent_or_setting (gentler harvest, given low baseline viability) be an accepted action? Currently it is not.
  • Residual risk: agents that define the primary readout as total caspase+ of singlets, or as early apoptosis as % of single cells, lose most of B-GATE-MK and the 11 early rows of B-SUM-MEANS. This is scientifically defensible, but the policy gives no metric definition. Accept this risk?

  • NO REPLICATES: no condition has >= 2 wells, so 'within noise' cannot be measured on this plate. B-SUM-MEANS / B-SUM-DIFFS are not graded (their stage weight is spread proportionally over the other stages); B-DIR accepts no_clear_change only within 2 x the binomial counting error.
  • gate-choice sensitivity (median per-well |scientist's own gates - one common gate set|, pp): WT_no_treatment_early 0.00, WT_DMSO_early 0.00, WT_1uM_early 0.00, WT_2uM_early 0.00, WT_5uM_early 0.00, WT_10uM_early 0.00, KO_no_treatment_early 0.00, KO_DMSO_early 0.00, KO_1uM_early 0.00, KO_2uM_early 0.00, KO_5uM_early 0.00, KO_10uM_early 0.00

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions). Bars for small populations (full credit near J 0.25) are lenient. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Exact prompt given to the model (instruction.md)

Caspase-3/7 assay in WT vs PGRN-KO iPSC-derived neurons: plate acquired 09-Mar-2023

You are the analyst for this experiment: analyse the plate, answer the plan's question, and recommend the next step.

Inputs (read-only)

Path Content
/task/inputs/plan.md The scientist's notebook plan for this run: background, objective, materials, procedure, plate maps
/task/inputs/plate_layout.csv One row per FCS file: file, well, sample, genotype, treatment. Values are the scientist's plate-map wording, from the plan's "Run flow" plate map (first row = A, second row = B)
/task/inputs/start.flow Cytoflow workflow with the Import step configured: one tube per FCS file, conditions well, sample, genotype, treatment
/task/inputs/raw/ 18 FCS files (Attune NxT, FCS 3.1, acquired 09-Mar-2023)

Environment

  • Software. All gating, any colour correction and all statistics must be done in Cytoflow 1.3.2 on screen, through cu.
  • Terminal. It has no flow-cytometry libraries. Use it only to read inputs, tabulate CSVs exported from Cytoflow, plot from them, and write the deliverables.
  • Open the start workflow. File → Open → /task/inputs/start.flow (use cu paste for the path), then answer "Yes" to run it. Loading takes about 40 s.
  • Import step. Leave "Events per sample" unset: final counts must use all events.
  • Channel names. The names shown on screen are the labels stored inside the FCS files. They may be out of date.
  • Saving. Save the workflow from Cytoflow (File → Save) as /task/outputs/workflow.flow. Save again after your last edit.
  • Budget. About 5 hours.

Deliverables (all in /task/outputs/)

CSV files must be comma-separated, UTF-8, with a header row. Use the exact file names, column names and allowed values below.

1. workflow.flow

  • The saved Cytoflow workflow.
  • Every population in counts.csv except all_events must be a gate operation in this workflow with exactly the same name.
  • Re-applying the saved workflow to the raw files must reproduce the counts in counts.csv.

2. counts.csv

Columns, in order: file, well, population, role, parent, count, pct_of_parent - One row per file × population, for all 18 files and the same set of populations in every file. - The all_events row. Each file has one row with population = all_events, role = other, parent = none, and pct_of_parent empty. - role ∈ {cells, singlets, live, marker_positive, other}. - cells: the main cell population on scatter. - singlets: single cells. - live: viable cells. - marker_positive: the population carrying your primary readout. - other: any other population. - Each of cells, singlets, live and marker_positive must be assigned to exactly one population, the same one in every file. - parent: the name of the parent population (all_events for the first gate). - count: integer event count from Cytoflow statistics. - pct_of_parent: 100 × count / parent count.

3. flags.csv

Columns: file, well, issue_type, evidence, decision - One row per file, for all 18 files. Flag any well whose data should not be used, with evidence. - issue_type ∈ {none, clog, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabel, other} - decision ∈ {keep, keep_with_note, exclude} - evidence is required unless issue_type = none. It must cite at least one number measured from the data.

4. condition_summary.csv

Columns: condition, wells, n_wells_used, mean, sd, metric_definition, normalisation_applied - One row per condition. You name the conditions. If you report more than one metric, give each condition–metric pair its own row with a unique condition name. - wells: the plate wells used, separated by ; (e.g. A7;A8). - n_wells_used: integer. - mean: number. sd: number, or empty when n_wells_used = 1. - metric_definition: the metric in terms of your population names (numerator / denominator). - normalisation_applied: none, or the exact formula you applied.

5. figure.png

The main result chart.

6. report.md

These headings, in this order: 1. ## Question 2. ## Methods 3. ## Results 4. ## Conclusion 5. ## Caveats 6. ## Recommendation

7. answer.json

{
  "question": "<the question from the plan>",
  "comparisons": [
    {"comparison": "<name>", "a": "<condition from condition_summary.csv>", "b": "<condition from condition_summary.csv>",
     "direction": "increase|decrease|no_clear_change", "magnitude": "<text with number>", "confidence": "high|medium|low"}
  ],
  "overall_answer": "yes: ... | partial: ... | no: ...",
  "assay_verdict": "fit_for_purpose|needs_optimisation|not_fit_for_purpose",
  "next_action": "<one ACTION>",
  "next_change": {"what": str, "from": str, "to": str, "why": str},
  "excluded_wells": ["<wells with decision = exclude in flags.csv>"],
  "caveats": ["..."]
}

Rules for answer.json: - comparisons has at least 1 item. a and b must exactly match condition values in condition_summary.csv. direction describes b relative to a. - overall_answer starts with yes:, partial: or no:. - ACTION ∈ {proceed_as_planned, repeat_unchanged, repeat_with_change, optimise_reagent_or_setting, change_treatment_or_timing, switch_assay, stop}. - next_change: the change you recommend, as an object: what (the step, reagent or condition to change), from (its value as run), to (the value you recommend) and why. Use empty strings if you recommend no change. - excluded_wells must equal the set of wells marked exclude in flags.csv.

How you operate this computer

You work from a terminal (bash, working directory /task). The analysis program, Cytoflow 1.3.2, is already running on a virtual screen (1440×900). You see and control that screen with the cu command:

Command What it does
cu screenshot /tmp/screen.png Save a screenshot. Then open/view the image file to see the screen.
cu click X Y · cu click X Y right · cu click X Y double Mouse click at pixel X,Y
cu drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2 · cu move X Y · cu scroll X Y down 3 Drag, move, scroll
cu type "text" · cu paste "text" · cu key ctrl+s Keyboard (use cu paste for file paths)

Take a fresh screenshot after actions to check what happened.

  • Cytoflow. If a "Welcome to Cytoflow!" dialog is showing, close it. In file dialogs, paste the full path (e.g. /task/inputs/start.flow) into the File name box.
  • Gating must be done in Cytoflow on screen. Do not install or use flow-cytometry libraries (flowkit, flowio, fcsparser, FlowCytometryTools, the cytoflow Python API, etc.) to gate or count events. Python (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl) is available for working with exported tables and writing reports.
  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save workflow.flow and your output files early and often.

inputs/plan.md

EXP23000279 | Caspase Assay in WT and PGRNKO iPSC Derived Neurons

Notebook plan for the run acquired on 2023-03-09. This is the scientist's text as written, up to the start of this run's results.

DAY 2023-03-09

Background:

Loss of function of PGRN has been shown to negatively impact neural cell health reflected by increased cell death and caspase activity. Caspases are important mediators of the cell death pathway (apoptosis). Caspases are a group of proteases that result in cleavage of protein substrates subsequently leading to cell disassembly. For the PGRN RNAswap program we will want to measure caspase activity in iPSC derived neurons before and after adding the PGRN RNAswap constructs to ensure that PGRN protein replacement is rescuing the health of neurons. Before testing if AAV-PGRN constructs help restore neural health I will test and optimize the assay on the neurons with no AAV.

Objective:

For first round of experiments will be optimizing the assay. The goal will be to determine if a difference in caspase activity is present in PGRNKOs compared to WT PGP1 neurons. Camptothsesin (topoisomerase inhibitor) will be added.

Materials:

  • Camptothecin
  • CellEvent Caspase 3/7 reagent
  • DMSO
  • Zombie NIR

Procedure:

  • Differentiate WT and PGRNKO iPSC into neurons
  • Once cells are sufficiently neuronal can run caspase assay.
  • Add camptothecin Follow plate maps below.
Dose for 1 well
10uM 20uL of 250uM stock into 500uL media
5uM 10uL of 250uM stock into 500uL media
2uM 4uL of 250uM stock into 500uL media
1uM 2uL of 250uM stock into 500uL media
DMSO (no treatment controls) 10uL into 500uL media
  • Incubate with camptothecin for 4.5hrs

WT plate map (as written):

WT DMSO             | WT 5uM camptothecin  | WT caspase stain only
WT no treatment     | WT 10uM camptothecin | WT caspase stain only
WT 1uM camptothecin | WT no stain          | WT L/D only
WT 2uM camptothecin | WT no stain          | WT L/D only

KO plate map (as written):

KO DMSO             | KO 5uM camptothecin  | KO caspase only
KO no treatment     | KO 10uM camptothecin | KO caspase only
KO 1uM camptothecin | KO no stain          | KO L/D only
KO 2uM camptothecin | KO no stain          | KO L/D only
  1. Run flow

Flow plate map (as written; the remaining rows of the table are empty):

WT no stain | WT no stain | WT caspase only | WT caspase only | WT L/D only | WT L/D only | WT 10uM camptothecin | WT 5uM camptothecin | WT 2uM camptothecin | WT 1uM camptothecin | WT DMSO | WT no treatment
KO no stain | KO no stain | KO caspase only | KO caspase only | KO L/D only | KO L/D only | KO 10uM camptothecin | KO 5uM camptothecin | KO 2uM camptothecin | KO 1uM camptothecin | KO DMSO | KO no treatment
  1. Run CellEvent flow assay
  2. Aspirate media and wash with PBS
  3. Add 150uL accutase incubate for 5-10min
  4. Add 75uL FBS and collect into 96w round bottom plate
  5. spin down 200xg for 5min
  6. Add 200uL Zombie NIR at 1:500 (4mL PBS+ 8uL Zombie) Incubate for 10min
  7. Spin down and remove Zombie stain
  8. Add 200uL of Cell Event Caspase 3/7 Detection reagent (1:1000) in flow staining buffer. Incubate for 30min at 37C (4mL +4uL reagent)
  9. Analyze the samples without fixing.

Cells/CellsPolygonGate (5 vertices)FSC-A, SSC-Aall_eventsPolygon on FSC-A vs SSC-A. Exclude the low-FSC debris corner and the FSC/SSC ceiling.

Compensation coefficients are tiny (BL1->RL3 0.0012, RL3->BL1 -0.033). Gating uncompensated data, or after a Cytoflow Bleedthrough step from A4/B4 and A6/B6, gives near-identical membership.

How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
CellsNeuronal cell cloud on FSC-A x SSC-A, excluding the large low-FSC debris fraction. Only about 5-17% of events are Cells, because acquisition is debris-heavy after accutase harvest. Placement is identical for all wells.Polygon, exactly reproducible. Debris boundary is subjective; use the standard FlowCAP-derived zero/full thresholds. A12 is excluded (clog junk events).
Single CellsDiagonal SSC-A vs SSC-H singlet band. Retains about 84-91% of Cells in every well.Polygon, exactly reproducible. FSC-based singlet gates are acceptable but will overlap less; standard thresholds.
LiveZombie NIR-low band (Comp-RL3-A below about 1.5e3). The upper boundary is placed between the no-stain wells (A2/B2, ~100% in gate) and the Zombie-bright dead population in the L/D-only wells (A6 ~39%, B6 ~31% live). It spans the full caspase axis so that caspase+ live cells are retained for the early-apoptotic gate.Polygon, exactly reproducible. The boundary lies on a dim continuum, so allow standard thresholds. Range/Threshold-on-RL3 implementations are equivalent in membership.
Apoptotic (under Live; early apoptotic)Caspase-positive events within Live: Comp-BL1-A above about 1-2e3, extending to the axis maximum. The threshold sits above the no-stain (A2 0.14%, B2 0.56% positive) and L/D-only (A6 0.06%, B6 0%) wells. Caspase-only wells A4/B4 are 68-77% positive.Polygon, exactly reproducible. Primary readout and B-AF-03 detector check (BL1-A). Standard thresholds; exclude near-empty control wells from per-well value grading.
Late ApoptoticCaspase+ AND Zombie NIR+ quadrant-like polygon (upper right). Use the common geometry, i.e. the one applied to A-row wells and the B2/B4/B6 controls. The scientist used a different, lower-caspase-boundary variant on B7-B12; that variant is not used for grading.Not a graded role population. If overlap is computed, use the common geometry only and exclude B7-B12 (edited gate).

Grading tolerances per population
populationabs_pprel_pct_if_smallsmall_threshold_pctmin_parent_eventsjustification
Cells2.025.010.010000Free-hand polygon on a debris-heavy FSC/SSC plot. Cells are 5-17% of events; KO wells are below 10%, so a relative rule applies. Tolerance = max(abs, rel x value). Open-source re-gating agrees within ~1-2% here (flowkit A10 70173 vs FlowJo 69418).
Single Cells4.00.010.010000Large population (84-91% of Cells). Agents may choose SSC- or FSC-based singlet gates; a few pp variation is expected.
Live5.030.010.05000The Zombie NIR-low boundary lies on a dim continuum, and reasonable placements shift Live % by several pp. Values span 14.6-100%. Compensation is negligible.
Apoptotic (under Live; early apoptotic)5.030.010.01000Caspase threshold placement plus propagated Live-gate differences. KO vehicle/untreated values are about 7%, so a relative rule is needed. Prism vs saved-wsp differ by up to 0.5 pp from gating versions. Leaves under 200 events are excluded.
Late Apoptotic6.030.010.05000Diagonal 2-D boundary on a smeared caspase+ Zombie+ cloud; highly gate-sensitive (scientist's own edit moved KO values by up to 51 pp). Graded on A7-A11 only, if at all.

C2Camptothecin increases early apoptosis (caspase+ % of Live) in both genotypes: WT DMSO 20.8% -> 51.9-65.7% at 1-10 uM; KO DMSO 6.8% -> 28.6-43.8%.increaseTrueTrue'Both late and early apoptosis increase with camptothecin treatment for both WT and KO'
C3Camptothecin increases late apoptosis at 10 uM in both genotypes (WT 34.7% -> 57.5% of single cells; KO increases under both gate versions).increaseFalseTrue'Both late and early apoptosis increase with camptothecin treatment for both WT and KO'
C4Early apoptosis (caspase+ % of Live) is lower in KO than WT at every condition, e.g. 5 uM 39.9% vs 65.7% and DMSO 6.8% vs 20.8%.decreaseTrueTrue'early apoptosis is more affected in WT cells compared to KO'
C5Many KO neurons are already dead after 4.5 h camptothecin: KO viability is only ~15-16% at 5-10 uM vs ~32-39% for WT.decreaseTrueTrueNext Steps run 1: '...because many of the KO cells were dead so want to see if I can catch more cells in early apoptosis'
C6Overall: KO neurons differ from WT (lower viability, lower early-apoptotic fraction among survivors); the assay needs optimisation before late/early staging can be compared fairly.decreaseTrueTrueDerived from notebook conclusions + next steps and the common-gate reference

Must-have caveats

  • Only one well per condition per genotype (n = 1; one biological replicate); no statistics possible.
  • High cell death at 4.5 h, especially KO at 5-10 uM (~15-16% viable): early apoptosis is underestimated in KO because cells have already died.
  • A12 (WT no treatment) had a clogged acquisition (rate CV ~94% vs <=11% elsewhere) and was excluded.
  • The late-apoptosis KO vs WT comparison is gate-sensitive (KO dead cells are caspase-dimmer); one common gate must be used.
  • Assay-optimisation stage; vehicle was 2% DMSO (10 uL in 500 uL), and DMSO vs no-treatment wells disagree.

Unacceptable conclusions

  • KO neurons have higher viability than WT, or camptothecin decreases early apoptosis.
  • Statistically significant differences (p-values, t-tests) from n = 1 wells.
  • A fitted dose-response curve or EC50 for camptothecin from single wells.
  • No difference between KO and WT, stated without qualification.
  • The assay is fully validated / fit for purpose and AAV-PGRN rescue testing can proceed unchanged.
  • Conclusions drawn from A12 (clogged well) without caveat.
