A1_flowkit: Gate one plate: CellEvent caspase-3/7 + Zombie NIR screen in GRN-KO iPSC neurons, biorep 2 (36 wells, 17-Apr-2023)

Internal id: A_base_screen_rep2_flowkit

FlowKit version. Same plate, answer key and scoring as A1, but the system works in a terminal with Python and FlowKit instead of drawing gates on screen in Cytoflow, and hands in its gates as a GatingML file (gates.xml). The check that gating was done in the GUI is removed.

Task A, base: gate a 36-well neuron screening plate

In one sentence: draw five gates in a GUI so that each of 36 wells is split into "cells → single cells → live → apoptotic", count each group, and say which wells are broken.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • Cells. Human stem-cell-derived neurons that lack the gene GRN (progranulin), a gene linked to dementia.
  • Treatment. Each well got one of 9 experimental gene-therapy viruses ("RNAswap constructs" meant to restore progranulin), a GFP control virus, or nothing. There are three wells per condition.
  • Dyes.
  • CellEvent caspase-3/7 glows green (detector BL1) in cells that are dying by apoptosis.
  • Zombie NIR glows far-red (RL3) in dead cells.
  • Data: 36 FCS files, about 9.4 million events in total.

What the agent has to do

  1. Open the prepared Cytoflow project and run it, which loads all 36 files.
  2. Draw 5 gates, one set applied to every well:
  3. Cells
  4. Single_Cells
  5. Live (Zombie-negative)
  6. Caspase_pos (caspase-bright among Live)
  7. Late_apoptosis (caspase-bright and Zombie-bright, a sibling branch next to Live)

It must use the written gating strategy and the control wells (no dye / one dye only) to place the lines. 3. Export the counts per well and per gate. 4. Inspect every well's event-rate-over-time trace for defects and flag the bad ones. 5. Write the deliverables.

Time: 2.5 hours.

What makes it tricky

  • Two wells are clogged (C1, C2): the event rate has gaps and bursts. The scientist kept them anyway, and our answer key says they should be flagged.
  • Several wells have mild, harmless end-of-run rate drops. Flagging them is a false alarm.
  • The caspase channel's label in the files says "AAV-GFP-Caspase", a leftover template name.
  • The GFP control wells (C4–C6) glow in the same detector as the caspase dye, so "caspase+" there isn't really caspase.
  • The scientist's Cells gate is very tight, keeping about 4% of events. Agents tend to keep about 60%, which inflates every downstream percentage.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The Cytoflow project with its gates, saved from the GUI. This is the agent's "classifier".
counts.csv For every well × population: how many events, and what % of the parent population that is.
flags.csv One row per well: usable yes/no, a reason category (clog, ran dry, too few events, ...) and numeric evidence.
notes.md One page explaining where each gate was drawn and why, the QC decisions, and any deviations. Required, but not scored.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task A v2, 2026-11-09

Share Item In plain terms
45% Gates For each gate, apply the agent's gate on its own to the cells the scientist kept at the step above, and compare it with the scientist's gate in every file: Jaccard = cells both selected / cells either selected. The scale comes from a public benchmark (FlowCAP-I) where 8 human experts gated the same data: zero credit at the overlap that 3 in 4 expert pairs beat (25th percentile), full credit at the median expert pair, linear in between. All gates count equally.
25% Read-out % For the populations the science uses (everything after cells and singlets): the share of wells whose % is within tolerance of the scientist's number. No credit outside the tolerance. Recomputed from the agent's gates, so it can't just type numbers.
15% Biology Do the control wells behave as expected, and do the wells rank in the same order as the scientist's?
10% Unusable wells Share of the truly bad wells caught × a penalty for each clean well flagged. No limit on flags; flagging everything scores 0.
5% QC evidence and reasons Judged by an LLM from the other model family: specific, numeric evidence, and the right reason for each caught well.

Populations whose reference can't be trusted are left out of grading and listed for expert review (e.g. the caspase gate on task A2).

Automatic zero:

  • the workflow is missing or broken;
  • fewer than 80% of the files are covered;
  • the key gates use the wrong detector;
  • the gating wasn't done in the Cytoflow GUI (the agent's command log shows it reading the raw files with code, or editing the saved workflow outside Cytoflow).

Strict format: a deliverable that breaks the specified format (wrong column names, wrong population names, ...) counts as missing.

Task type
A: gate one plate (gating + QC)

Budget

Environment

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

This is biological replicate 2 of the RNAswap V2.0 in-vitro screen (notebook EXP23000928, linked to biorep 1 EXP23000741). PGP1 GRN-KO iPSC-derived neurons were transduced with 9 AAV1 GRN RNAswap v2.0 constructs (SVEC 654-662), AAV1-GFP or no virus at 1e4 vg/cell. At D14 they were stained with Zombie NIR (RL3-A) and CellEvent caspase-3/7 Green (BL1-A) and acquired unfixed on the Attune NxT: 36 FCS files, wells A1-C12, triplicate wells per condition plus three dye controls. The scientist's FlowJo workspace (19-Apr-2023.wsp_caspase_RNAswap_rep2.wsp) uses one plate-wide gate set with no compensation: Cells (polygon FSC-A/SSC-A) -> Single Cells (polygon SSC-H/SSC-A) -> {Live (rectangle BL1/RL3) -> Caspase+ (rectangle BL1/RL3); Late apoptosis (polygon BL1/RL3)}. The Prism table 'Rep2' matches the saved gating 60/60 (Late apoptosis % of Single Cells; Caspase+ % of Live) with no normalisation. Well positions for the 10 Prism conditions come from matching Prism values to the per-well saved stats. C4-C6 (AAV1-GFP) and C10-C12 (unstained, Zombie-only, CellEvent-only) are inferred. The main natural QC trap is erratic, clog-like flow in C1 and C2, both of which the scientist kept in the answer key. Benign end-of-run gap/burst patterns occur in many wells.

Natural traps in this plate (not hinted to the model)

typewhere
clogC1 (3945_3503 replicate 1; kept in the scientist's Prism answer key)
clogC2 (3945_3503 replicate 2; kept in the scientist's Prism answer key)
otherEnd-of-run gap/burst or end-rate drop, benign and common: e.g. C8 (last10pct 0.41, 2 low bins, CV 23.4), C6 (0.53, CV 18.7), B11 (0.59, 1 low bin, CV 17.1), C5 (0.63, CV 17.5), B9 (0.67, CV 16.2), C11 (1 low bin, CV 18.8)
otherA7 and B8: non-monotonic Time column; B8 also max_bin_over_median 2.0, A7 1.65
stale_channel_labelBL1-A labelled 'AAV-GFP-Caspase-A' in every file
otherC4-C6 (AAV1-GFP, inferred): GFP shares BL1-A with CellEvent, so 'Caspase_pos' and 'Late_apoptosis' there are not caspase-specific. These wells also have low gated Live counts. They are excluded from the scientist's Prism table.
too_few_eventsC4-C6 gated Live populations are small (a few hundred events in C6), although total events per file are normal (>160k in every file)
saturationAll wells: SSC-A 1.2-4.4% and FSC-A ≤0.8% of events at detector maximum
mislabelNotebook flow-plate map in EXP23000928 (A1-A12 + B1-B3 controls) is a copy of the biorep-1 15-well map and does not describe the 36-well rep-2 plate. Controls are unlabeled in the data.
normalisation_stepNone applied by the scientist

Expert review list

Everything any generation stage flagged for an expert, plus standing caveats. Nothing here is graded until an expert decides.

Task brief and plate layout (stage 1)

  • Confirm the well positions of the 10 Prism conditions (A1-C3 and C7-C9), derived from Prism Rep2 row order matched to saved per-well FlowJo values (source 2). No plate map for rep 2 exists in the notebook.
  • Confirm C4-C6 = AAV1-GFP (fully stained), inferred from notebook design and file count, versus the investigation report's 'apoptosis-positive control'. Were these wells stained with both dyes?
  • Confirm C10 = unstained, C11 = Zombie NIR only, C12 = CellEvent only, all untransduced (NT). This is inferred from data plus the notebook's control order.
  • Construct ID discrepancy: '9421' (Prism) vs '9241' (notebook transduction map) vs '3421' (biorep-1 conclusion). Which is correct?
  • Is the EXP23000928 'Flow Plate' table indeed a stale copy of the biorep-1 map (not a description of this plate)?
  • Confirm the truth labels for C1 and C2 (erratic, clog-like flow) as 'unusable', given that the scientist kept both in the Prism answer key. Should Stage 5 propose a corrected reference that excludes them?
  • C8 end-of-run rate drop (last10pct 0.41, CV 23.4%): ambiguous or ran_dry?
  • Verify in the built image how Cytoflow 1.3.2 displays 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A' (space) and 'AAV-GFP-Caspase-A'. Is punctuation sanitised? Update the channel table if so.
  • Verify that Cytoflow accepts the op names Single_Cells, Caspase_pos and Late_apoptosis, and that make_import_flow treats construct values like '9523' as text (category), not integers.
  • Decide how to grade Caspase_pos given the scientist's finite upper BL1 bound (especially C4-C6 and C12).
  • Check whether the non-monotonic Time column in A7/B8 breaks Cytoflow's time-based views or FlowClean in this build.
  • Confirm the archive source path for the 36 FCS files (230417_flow under the EXP23000741 Caspase assay folder) before copying unchanged.
  • Confirm that 2.5 h / 180 actions is sufficient given rendering time for 9.4M events in Cytoflow views.

QC labels to confirm (stage 2)

  • A4: fine (ok, confidence medium)
  • A7: ambiguous (other, confidence medium)
  • A8: fine (ok, confidence medium)
  • B3: fine (ok, confidence medium)
  • B8: ambiguous (other, confidence medium)
  • C1: unusable (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence high)
  • C2: unusable (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence medium)
  • C4: ambiguous (mislabeled_or_unexpected, confidence low)
  • C5: ambiguous (other, confidence low)
  • C6: ambiguous (other, confidence low)
  • C8: ambiguous (ran_dry, confidence medium)
  • C10: fine (ok, confidence medium)
  • C12: fine (ok, confidence medium)

Answer key (stage 2)

  • C1 truth label = unusable (high) and C2 = unusable (medium): Both are in the scientist's Prism answer key. C2 is less extreme (rate CV 52.8%, settles after ~21 s). Decide whether A-QC-01 should require C2 or only C1.
  • Identity of C4-C6 (AAV1-GFP vs apoptosis-positive control): Unlabelled. The decision affects whether flagging them is reasonable (labelled ambiguous now) and whether BL1 populations there mean anything.
  • Identities of C10/C11/C12 (unstained / Zombie-only / CellEvent-only): Inferred from signal and notebook control order. They anchor control_bounds criteria.
  • Finite BL1 upper bounds in the scientist's Live and Caspase+ rectangles (and the Late polygon right edge): The brief describes Live as spanning the whole BL1 range and does not mention the Caspase+ upper edge. GFP wells are excluded, but C12 (47% Caspase+) could differ if many CellEvent-bright events lie above the upper edge. The pipeline should compute, per file, the % of Live events above the Caspase+ BL1 upper bound and exclude any file where it exceeds half the tolerance.
  • Scientist's Caspase+ cutoff leaves 8.8% of unstained C10 Live positive (vs 2.39% in C11): Any control_bounds max for C10 Caspase_pos must not be tighter than ~12%. Agents placing the cutoff strictly above C10 will read systematically lower Caspase_pos on samples. The odd C10 > C11 tail may reflect autofluorescent cells; check that the C10/C11 identities are correct.
  • Biex (FlowJo) vs logicle (Cytoflow) polygon-edge geometry for Late_apoptosis: Confirm that the overlap engine evaluates each polygon in its own display transform. The resulting systematic offset should be reflected in the threshold.
  • C8 (last10pct 0.41, CV 23.4%) labelled ambiguous rather than ran_dry: It is the strongest end-of-run drop on the plate and was used by the scientist (No-virus rep 2).
  • Near-threshold wells labelled fine (A4, B3; A8 SSC-A saturation 3.72%): They meet the fine bounds but sit close to them. Flagging any of them would be penalised as a false alarm, so the labels must be safe.
  • A7/B8 non-monotonic Time columns: Verify that Cytoflow Time views and FlowClean behave sensibly. If not, agents may be misled into flagging; they are labelled ambiguous.
  • Prism C7 Early 35.3 vs FlowJo 35.22: Minor transcription/rounding mismatch; irrelevant to grading (wsp authoritative) but recorded.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • Caspase+ BL1 upper edge (~4.8e3) vs CellEvent-bright live events: Have the pipeline compute, per graded file, the % of scientist-Live events with BL1 > 4834 and RL3 inside the Caspase+ interval. If this exceeds ~2.5 pp in many sample wells, the qualitative disclosure may not be enough, and A-FREQ-04/A-GATE-04 tolerance or exclusions need revisiting (C12 especially).
  • Identity of C4–C6 (AAV1-GFP vs apoptosis-positive control): Data (Cells 1.5–2.5%, Live 9–18%, Caspase+ 75–90% of Live inside a BL1 interval capped at ~4.8e3) fits an apoptosis-inducer control at least as well as bright GFP. The brief states AAV1-GFP as fact. If unresolved, relabel these wells in the brief as 'reference wells, identity uncertain; do not use for BL1 boundaries'.
  • C2 truth label (unusable, medium confidence): Rate CV 52.8%, 7 consecutive near-zero bins, BL1/RL3 band shift at ~21 s. If confirmed, add C2 to the A-QC-01 catch list and A-QC-04. The scientist kept both C1 and C2 in the Prism key.
  • C1 truth label: Strong metrics; confirm unusable before it serves as the only catch well.
  • C10/C11/C12 identities (unstained / Zombie-only / CellEvent-only): Inferred from signal and the notebook control order. Control bounds are value-based and remain valid, but the brief states the identities as fact.
  • Exclusion of C10 Caspase_pos: Fairness judgement: the scientist's cutoff leaves 8.8% of unstained live cells positive (vs 2.39% in Zombie-only C11). Confirm that C10/C11 are not swapped.
  • Fine labels A4, B3 (near CV/end-rate limits), A8 (SSC-A sat 3.72%), C10, C12: Excluded from A-QC-02 pending confirmation.
  • max_flagged = 10 in A-QC-01: The plate has 2 unusable + 13 ambiguous wells. Confirm the cap is not too strict for a cautious expert.
  • Biex (FlowJo) vs logicle (Cytoflow) polygon evaluation for Late_apoptosis and Cells: The overlap engine must evaluate each gate in its own transform. The finalise step must allow for the known +0.5–1.2 pp systematic offset.
  • Cells tolerance (20% relative, floor 0.5 pp): The debris/cell boundary is a continuum; the tolerance may be tight for hand-drawn polygons. Calibrate with a pilot run.
  • Cytoflow channel name display and op-name acceptance: Verify how 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A' and 'AAV-GFP-Caspase-A' render, that Single_Cells/Caspase_pos/Late_apoptosis are valid op names, and that construct values like '9523' import as categories.
  • Non-monotonic Time in A7/B8: Check that Cytoflow time views and FlowClean behave sensibly; both wells are labelled ambiguous.
  • Construct label 9421 vs 9241 vs 3421: Labelling only; not graded.
  • Regenerate 02_expected_values.csv: C10 Caspase_pos must be set use_for_grading=false (Caspase_pos graded 30).
  • Archive source path for the 36 FCS (230417_flow): Reconstructed path; verify before copying unchanged.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Accept the sanity ordering (c) 0.86 > (d) 0.72? It is unavoidable with the fixed type-A stage budgets (qc 0.15). The alternatives are to raise the qc budget template-wide or to accept that type A ranks gating quality above QC.
  • Confirm the A-QC-03 'max 1 when nothing is flagged' judge rule and the A-QC-04 x A-QC-01 dependency.
  • C2 truth label: if confirmed unusable, add it to the A-QC-01 catch list (score = fraction of 2 caught) and to A-QC-04. QC-01 weight can stay at 0.075.
  • Confirm C1 as unusable (the only catch well; the scientist kept it in the Prism key).
  • Caspase+ BL1 upper edge (~4.8e3): the pipeline should compute, per file, the % of scientist-Live events above it. If this exceeds ~2.5 pp widely (especially C12), revisit A-FREQ-04/A-GATE-04 tolerances or exclusions.
  • Identity of C4-C6 (AAV1-GFP vs apoptosis-positive control) and of C10/C11/C12; consider relabelling C4-C6 in the brief as 'identity uncertain'.
  • Fine labels for A4, B3, A8, C10 and C12 (currently excluded from A-QC-02); max_flagged = 10.
  • Pilot-calibrate the Cells relative tolerance (20%, floor 0.5 pp) and the finalise-step overlap curves, given the biex/logicle offset on Late_apoptosis (+0.5-1.2 pp already seen in FlowKit).
  • Verify Cytoflow channel display names, op-name acceptance, Time handling for A7/B8, and the archive source path of the 36 FCS files.

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Percentage tolerances were chosen by the model, not calibrated against data the way the gate thresholds are: Live: rel 20%, floor 1.0 pp, abs 5.0 pp; Caspase_pos: rel 30%, floor 1.5 pp, abs 5.0 pp; Late_apoptosis: rel 25%, floor 1.0 pp, abs 5.0 pp
  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions): zero credit at the expert 25th percentile, full credit at the expert median, by population size (Task A v2, 2026-11-09). Full credit therefore needs median expert agreement, which about half of real expert pairs miss. Population size is the share of the parent, so a scatter gate that keeps only a few % of events because of debris is binned as a small population. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Exact prompt given to the model (instruction.md)

Gate one plate: caspase-3/7 + Zombie NIR in GRN-KO iPSC neurons (36 wells)

Goal: with FlowKit (Python), gate all 36 wells with one gate set, report counts for five fixed populations per well, and flag every well whose data should not be used.

Experiment

Item Value
Cells PGP1 GRN-knockout iPSC-derived neurons
Treatment AAV1 transduction at 1e4 vg/cell: 9 GRN RNAswap v2.0 constructs, AAV1-GFP, or no virus; triplicate wells
Readout 14 days after transduction; acquired 17-Apr-2023, unfixed, Attune NxT
Staining Zombie NIR 1:500, 10 min on adherent cells → Accutase detachment → CellEvent Caspase-3/7 detection reagent 1:1000 in flow staining buffer, 30 min, 37 °C

Inputs

/task/inputs/raw/ 36 FCS 3.1 files Caspase_KO_RNAswap-rep2_caspase_Group_<well>.fcs, wells A1–C12
/task/inputs/plate_layout.csv file, well, construct, stain, replicate, is_control, control_type
/task/inputs/gating_strategy.md The scientist's gating strategy (description, no coordinates)

  • GFP wells. In the AAV1-GFP wells (C4–C6), GFP fluorescence is collected in the same detector, BL1-A.
  • No other fluorescence parameters were recorded.

Gate shapes and channels are given in gating_strategy.md.

Gating rules

  • One operation per population. Each population is one FlowKit gate (RectangleGate, PolygonGate or EllipsoidGate). Its name must be exactly the population name above.
  • Hierarchy.
  • A population's membership is its own gate AND all its ancestors' gates.
  • Compute counts with the full ancestor chain.
  • One gate set for all 36 wells. No per-well gates.
  • Raw (uncompensated) data only. Do not add Bleedthrough, Autofluorescence or any other operation that changes channel values.

Deliverables (all in /task/outputs/)

File Content
gates.xml Your gating strategy as GatingML 2.0, written with flowkit.export_gatingml (see Software). It must load with flowkit.parse_gating_xml. One gate per reported population, named exactly as the population.
counts.csv Columns file,well,population,count,parent_population,pct_of_parent. 180 rows: 36 files × 5 populations. file = exact FCS file name. count = integer events. pct_of_parent = 100 × count / parent count, a 0–100 float (0 if parent count is 0). The parent of Cells is All_events (all events in the file).
flags.csv Columns file,well,usable,reason_category,evidence. 36 rows, one per file. usable ∈ {yes, no}. reason_category ∈ {ok, clog_or_interrupted_flow, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabeled_or_unexpected, other}. usable=yes if and only if reason_category=ok. evidence = the observation behind the decision, quantified.
notes.md ≤ 1 page: how each gate was placed and why; any deviation from gating_strategy.md.

Flag any well whose data should not be used, with evidence.

Limits

  • Budget: about 2.5 h.
  • Save gates.xml early, and again after the last gate change.

Software (FlowKit version of this task)

  • Python 3 with FlowKit 1.2.3 (plus flowio, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, openpyxl) is installed. There is no graphical analysis program.
  • Load each file with flowkit.Sample(path). Build one flowkit.GatingStrategy for all wells, with flowkit.Dimension and flowkit.gates.RectangleGate, PolygonGate or EllipsoidGate (no quadrant or Boolean gates).
  • Gate names must be valid XML IDs: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (no spaces or +).
  • One gate per reported population, named exactly as the population and nested under its parent population (the first population's gate sits at the root). A population's events are its own gate within its parent.
  • Raw (uncompensated) data only. Every gate dimension uses compensation_ref="uncompensated"; apply no compensation or spillover correction.
  • Channels. FlowKit gate dimensions use the detector ID ($PnN, e.g. BL1-A), not the text label.
  • Transforms. You may draw gates on transformed axes (for example flowkit.transforms.LogicleTransform, added with add_transform and referenced by transformation_ref).
  • Save the strategy with flowkit.export_gatingml(strategy, open("/task/outputs/gates.xml", "wb")) and check that it reloads with flowkit.parse_gating_xml.
  • Counts. counts.csv must be the counts these saved gates give on each file (strategy.gate_sample(sample)), with no per-well changes.
  • Looking at data. Save plots as PNG files and open the image files to view them.

How you work

You work in a terminal (bash, working directory /task).

  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save gates.xml and your output files early and often.

Input files in /task/inputs (read-only)

inputs/gating_strategy.md

Gating strategy

This describes the scientist's original analysis of this plate: gate order, channels and gate shapes. Placing the boundaries is your job.

Hierarchy

  • All_events
  • Cells — polygon, FSC-A × SSC-A
    • Single_Cells — polygon, SSC-H × SSC-A
    • Live — rectangle, BL1-A × RL3-A
      • Caspase_pos — rectangle, BL1-A × RL3-A
    • Late_apoptosis — polygon, BL1-A × RL3-A

The scientist's original population names were Cells, Single Cells, Live, Caspase+ and Late apoptosis.

Global settings

  • One gate set applied to every well.
  • No compensation: BL1-A and RL3-A were gated as acquired.
  • Display BL1-A and RL3-A on a scale that shows values ≤ 0 (logicle).
  • Lower gate boundaries on these axes should sit below the negative population, so that negative-valued events are kept.

Gates

Population Drawn on Shape and axes Include
Cells all events polygon, FSC-A (x) × SSC-A (y) the cell cluster; exclude low-FSC-A debris
Single_Cells Cells polygon, SSC-H (x) × SSC-A (y) the diagonal singlet band; exclude events with SSC-A high relative to SSC-H
Live Single_Cells rectangle, BL1-A × RL3-A Zombie NIR-negative events (see note 1)
Caspase_pos Live rectangle, BL1-A × RL3-A CellEvent-positive events (see note 2)
Late_apoptosis Single_Cells (not Live) polygon, BL1-A × RL3-A events that are both Zombie NIR-bright and CellEvent-positive

Notes on the gates: 1. The Live rectangle spans the whole BL1-A range, so it selects on RL3-A only. A Range gate on RL3-A is an acceptable equivalent. 2. The Caspase_pos rectangle spans the RL3-A range of Live, so it selects on BL1-A only. A Range gate on BL1-A is an acceptable equivalent. 3. Live and Late_apoptosis are sibling gates, not complements. Events in neither are not reported, e.g.: - events with intermediate RL3-A; - events that are Zombie NIR-bright but CellEvent-negative.

Choosing boundaries (guidance)

  • Use the control wells to decide where negative ends on each fluorescence axis:
  • C10 (unstained): position of unstained cells on BL1-A and RL3-A.
  • C11 (Zombie NIR only): RL3-A boundary between Zombie-negative and Zombie-bright cells. This sets the Live upper edge and the Late_apoptosis lower edge.
  • C12 (CellEvent only): BL1-A boundary between caspase-negative and caspase-positive cells. This sets the Caspase_pos and Late_apoptosis left edges.
  • Check the boundaries on the fully stained no-virus wells C7–C9.
  • Do not set BL1-A boundaries on C4–C6: their BL1-A signal includes GFP.

FlowKit mapping

Population FlowKit gate Channels (detector IDs) Parent gate
Cells PolygonGate FSC-A, SSC-A root
Single_Cells PolygonGate SSC-H, SSC-A Cells
Live RectangleGate (or a 1-D RectangleGate on RL3-A) BL1-A, RL3-A Single_Cells
Caspase_pos RectangleGate (or a 1-D RectangleGate on BL1-A) BL1-A, RL3-A Live
Late_apoptosis PolygonGate BL1-A, RL3-A Single_Cells

outputs/flags.csvCSVfile,well,usable,reason_category,evidence. 36 rows. usable ∈ {yes,no}. reason_category ∈ {ok, clog_or_interrupted_flow, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabeled_or_unexpected, other}. usable=yes iff reason_category=ok. evidence = free text, quantified.
outputs/notes.mdMarkdown, ≤ 1 pageHow each gate was placed and why; any deviations from gating_strategy.md

Ground truth = the scientist's own saved FlowJo gating and results (exact values, never shown to the model), plus expert-style QC labels and documented conclusions. The exemplar deliverables are what a top-quality submission looks like.

Reference gating strategy (scientist's FlowJo workspace)

population (task name)scientist populationgate typechannelsparentreproducible in Cytoflow
Cells/CellsPolygonGate (5 vertices)FSC-A, SSC-AAll_eventsPolygon op 'Cells', xchannel FSC-A, ychannel SSC-A, no view subset. The pipeline evaluates it on all events of each file.
Single_Cells/Cells/Single CellsPolygonGate (4 vertices; x = SSC-H, y = SSC-A)SSC-H, SSC-ACellsPolygon op 'Single_Cells', xchannel SSC-H, ychannel SSC-A. Membership is Cells AND Single_Cells.
Live/Cells/Single Cells/LiveRectangleGateBL1-A, RL3-ASingle_CellsRectangle op 'Live' (tag range2d) on AAV-GFP-Caspase-A x LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A, or Range op on RL3-A. Membership is Cells AND Single_Cells AND Live. The scientist's rectangle selects on RL3-A. Its BL1-A bounds are a slightly negative lower edge and a finite upper edge of ~1.5e5, far below the detector maximum. These BL1 bounds only matter for very BL1-bright events, i.e. GFP wells.
Caspase_pos/Cells/Single Cells/Live/Caspase+RectangleGateBL1-A, RL3-ALiveRectangle op 'Caspase_pos' on BL1-A x RL3-A, or Range op on BL1-A. Membership is Cells AND Single_Cells AND Live AND Caspase_pos. The scientist's RL3-A interval covers the whole Live interval. The BL1-A interval is closed: lower edge in the low hundreds-to-~600 range, upper edge in the low thousands. An open-ended Range or Threshold therefore adds BL1-bright Live events that FlowJo excluded.
Late_apoptosis/Cells/Single Cells/Late apoptosisPolygonGate (4 vertices; x = BL1-A, y = RL3-A)BL1-A, RL3-ASingle_CellsPolygon op 'Late_apoptosis' on BL1-A x RL3-A, logicle scale, view subset Cells + Single_Cells. Membership is Cells AND Single_Cells AND Late_apoptosis, never restricted to Live. A polygon has straight edges in display space. FlowJo draws in biex space and Cytoflow in logicle space, so edges between the same raw-unit vertices curve differently in raw space. Expect small systematic boundary differences.
How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
CellsPolygon around the intact-cell cluster on FSC-A x SSC-A, excluding the very large low-FSC debris cloud. Only ~1.5-8.7% of events are Cells (iPSC-neuron prep after Accutase), so the lower-left edge sits in a debris/cell continuum and drives most of the between-analyst variation. There is no fluorescence control logic; placement is judged on scatter density.Small, debris-bordered population. Hand-drawn edges in a continuum make moderate overlap normal; set the threshold from the population-size calibration. The FlowJo axis transform for FSC/SSC must be read from the wsp.
Single_CellsDiagonal singlet band on SSC-H (x) vs SSC-A (y) within Cells. Events with SSC-A high for their SSC-H (doublets/aggregates) are excluded. 77-91% of Cells are retained across wells.Large population (>75% of parent); high overlap is expected from any reasonable band gate.
LiveRL3-A (Zombie NIR) upper edge placed just above the Zombie-negative population. C10 (unstained) and C12 (CellEvent-only) put 99.8-99.9% of singlets below it, and C11 (Zombie-only) shows the negative/bright split. The lower edge is below the negative population, keeping negative-valued events. The BL1 range is effectively open except for a finite upper edge.In stained sample wells the RL3 edge cuts through a continuum of intermediate-RL3 events (Live + Late account for only ~65-85% of singlets), so edge placement moves Live by several pp. GFP wells C4-C6 are excluded because of the finite BL1 upper bound and GFP in BL1.
Caspase_posBL1-A lower cutoff at the upper tail of the CellEvent-negative population. It is set relative to C12 (CellEvent-only, 47% positive of Live) and the dye-free wells. The scientist's cutoff still leaves 8.8% of C10 (unstained) Live and 2.4% of C11 (Zombie-only) Live above it, so it is NOT strictly above the unstained tail. The BL1 upper edge is finite (low thousands).Most placement-sensitive gate, a threshold in the shoulder of the negative peak. Agents who place the cutoff strictly above C10 will be systematically lower, and agents with an open upper bound will include BL1-bright Live events. Use the population-size calibration and do not tighten beyond it. GFP wells C4-C6 are excluded.
Late_apoptosisQuadrilateral covering the CellEvent+ / Zombie NIR-bright region within Single Cells. The lower RL3 edge is above the Live band and slants with BL1; the left BL1 edge is near the caspase cutoff. It is essentially empty in Zombie-free controls (C10: 0 events, C12: 1 event) and small in C11 (1.67%). It is a sibling of Live, so intermediate-RL3 and Zombie-bright/CellEvent-negative events fall in neither.Polygon in biex (FlowJo) vs logicle (Cytoflow) space: edges cannot match exactly. FlowKit re-gating of this wsp was already systematically +0.5-1.2 pp on this population. Use a moderate threshold. C10/C12 are excluded (empty reference) and graded via control bounds instead.

Grading tolerances per population
populationabs_pprel_pct_if_smallsmall_threshold_pctmin_parent_eventsjustification
Cells2.020.010.0200All reference values are 1.5-8.67% of all events, so the relative rule always applies (e.g. 5% ref gives ±1.0 pp; floor 0.5 pp). The polygon on FSC/SSC is reproducible in software, but the debris/cell boundary is a density continuum, and hand placement of the lower-left edge shifts Cells by a sizeable fraction of its value.
Single_Cells4.020.010.0200References are 77.7-90.8% of Cells. FlowKit-vs-FlowJo Single Cells differences on similar Attune workspaces were up to ~1-2 pp; add ~2 pp for hand-drawn band width.
Live5.020.010.0200References are 13.75-99.9% of Single Cells (graded wells). This is a 1-D RL3 cut through a continuum of intermediate-RL3 events in stained wells, so small edge shifts move several pp. FlowKit on this wsp differed by up to 1.19 pp, with Live among the >0.5 pp cases. Floor 1 pp for any value <10%.
Caspase_pos5.030.010.0200References are 2.39-47.08% of Live in graded wells (most 11-35%). The cutoff sits in the shoulder of the negative peak (8.8% of unstained C10 Live is 'positive'), which makes this the most placement-sensitive gate. The scientist's closed BL1 interval adds possible divergence for open-ended agent gates. C10 (8.8%) and C11 (2.39%) use the relative rule with floor 1.5 pp.
Late_apoptosis5.025.010.0200References are 1.67-49% of Single Cells in graded wells. Polygon in biex vs logicle space cannot be matched exactly, and FlowKit was already systematically +0.5-1.2 pp here. A double-positive region in a continuum adds placement variance. Floor 1 pp for C11 (1.67%).

notes_md

Gating notes (one gate set, all 36 wells; raw channels; full events; logicle on BL1-A and RL3-A)

  1. Cells: Polygon on FSC-A x SSC-A, no subset, drawn on pooled wells. Most events are low-FSC debris. The lower-left edge sits in the density trough between debris and the cell cluster, and was checked on C7 and C10.
  2. Single_Cells: Polygon on SSC-H x SSC-A, subset Cells. Encloses the diagonal singlet band and excludes events with SSC-A high relative to SSC-H.
  3. Live: Range on LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A (accepted equivalent of the rectangle), subset Cells + Single_Cells.
  4. Lower bound is below the negative population, so negative values are kept.
  5. Upper bound is just above the Zombie-negative peak, set on C11 (Zombie only).
  6. Checked that C10 (unstained) and C12 (CellEvent only) fall essentially entirely inside it.
  7. Caspase_pos: Range on AAV-GFP-Caspase-A (this is the CellEvent detector; the name is a stale template label), subset Cells + Single_Cells + Live.
  8. Lower edge is at the upper tail of the BL1-A negative population in C10/C11, where the C12 positive population separates.
  9. Upper edge is at the top of the C12 positive cluster.
  10. Checked on C7-C9. A small unstained tail remains above the cutoff in C10.
  11. Late_apoptosis: Polygon on BL1-A x RL3-A, subset Cells + Single_Cells (not Live).
  12. Covers events that are RL3-A bright (as in C11) and BL1-A above the caspase cutoff.
  13. Contains ~0 events in C10 and C12.

Boundaries. BL1-A boundaries were not set on C4-C6, where BL1-A includes GFP.

Counts. Channel Statistic (Count, by well) for each full ancestor chain; Table view exported to outputs/work/. The terminal computed pct_of_parent = 100 x count / parent count, with the parent of Cells = all events.

QC. Per-well Time histograms (event rate) and Time vs FSC-A/SSC-A/BL1-A/RL3-A plots. - C1 and C2 are flagged unusable (clog/interrupted flow). Their counts are still reported. - End-of-run gaps or slowdowns (B9, B11, C5, C6, C8) and single burst bins (A7, B8, C7) were judged benign and noted as caveats.

Deviations from gating_strategy.md. Live and Caspase_pos are Range gates instead of rectangles (allowed equivalents). No compensation or FlowClean filtering; FlowClean, if run, was for inspection only.

A2_flowkit: Gate a CellEvent caspase-3/7 + Zombie NIR plate: WT vs PGRN-KO mouse primary neurons treated with camptothecin (Attune NxT, 20-Mar-2023)

Internal id: A_EXP22004263_21_Mar_2023_flowkit

FlowKit version. Same plate, answer key and scoring as A2, but the system works in a terminal with Python and FlowKit instead of drawing gates on screen in Cytoflow, and hands in its gates as a GatingML file (gates.xml). The check that gating was done in the GUI is removed.

Task A: gate a 30-well mouse-neuron drug plate (21 Mar 2023)

In one sentence: draw four gates in a GUI to split each of 30 wells into "cells → single cells → live → apoptotic", count them, and flag broken wells.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • Cells. Mouse neurons grown in a dish, either normal (WT) or lacking progranulin (PGRN-KO).
  • Treatment. Camptothecin, a chemotherapy drug that triggers apoptosis, at 1, 5, 10 or 20 µM for 5 hours, plus DMSO (the solvent alone) and untreated wells.
  • Dyes. Caspase-3/7 (BL1, apoptotic cells) and Zombie NIR (RL3, dead cells).
  • Controls. Three staining-control wells per genotype: no dye, Zombie only, caspase dye only.
  • Data: 30 FCS files, about 1.9 million events.

What the agent has to do

  1. Open the prepared project and load all 30 files.
  2. Draw 4 gates, one set for every well: Cells, Single_Cells, Live, Caspase_pos. Use the control wells to decide where "negative" ends.
  3. Export counts.
  4. Inspect each well's flow over time and flag the defective ones.
  5. Write the deliverables.

Time: 2 hours.

What makes it tricky

  • Too few events. Some wells have very few events, e.g. B6 has only 8,000 in total. B6 should be marked unusable.
  • Side-scatter saturation. The side-scatter detector maxed out on 13–40% of events in every file, which squashes part of the Cells plot against the edge.
  • Swapped controls. The scientist's own analysis appears to have used two control wells the wrong way round.
  • Plate-map mismatches. Four wells in the files are not in the notebook's plate map, and four wells in the map were never run.
  • Stale channel label. The caspase channel is labelled "AAV-GFP-Caspase", but there is no virus in this experiment.

Not graded on this plate (since 2026-11-09): the caspase-positive gate and its percentage. The scientist's caspase gates were drawn after a colour-overlap correction that uses an impossible value (the dead-cell dye supposedly leaking into the caspase channel at 1.8×, although the two dyes are read by different lasers). The agent is not allowed to apply corrections, so the two would be compared on different data, and the plate's controls can't tell us the true correction. It is listed for expert review. The cells, singlets and live gates are still graded.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The Cytoflow project with its gates, saved from the GUI. This is the agent's "classifier".
counts.csv For every well × population: how many events, and what % of the parent population that is.
flags.csv One row per well: usable yes/no, a reason category (clog, ran dry, too few events, ...) and numeric evidence.
notes.md One page explaining where each gate was drawn and why, the QC decisions, and any deviations. Required, but not scored.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task A v2, 2026-11-09

Share Item In plain terms
45% Gates For each gate, apply the agent's gate on its own to the cells the scientist kept at the step above, and compare it with the scientist's gate in every file: Jaccard = cells both selected / cells either selected. The scale comes from a public benchmark (FlowCAP-I) where 8 human experts gated the same data: zero credit at the overlap that 3 in 4 expert pairs beat (25th percentile), full credit at the median expert pair, linear in between. All gates count equally.
25% Read-out % For the populations the science uses (everything after cells and singlets): the share of wells whose % is within tolerance of the scientist's number. No credit outside the tolerance. Recomputed from the agent's gates, so it can't just type numbers.
15% Biology Do the control wells behave as expected, and do the wells rank in the same order as the scientist's?
10% Unusable wells Share of the truly bad wells caught × a penalty for each clean well flagged. No limit on flags; flagging everything scores 0.
5% QC evidence and reasons Judged by an LLM from the other model family: specific, numeric evidence, and the right reason for each caught well.

Populations whose reference can't be trusted are left out of grading and listed for expert review (e.g. the caspase gate on task A2).

Automatic zero:

  • the workflow is missing or broken;
  • fewer than 80% of the files are covered;
  • the key gates use the wrong detector;
  • the gating wasn't done in the Cytoflow GUI (the agent's command log shows it reading the raw files with code, or editing the saved workflow outside Cytoflow).

Strict format: a deliverable that breaks the specified format (wrong column names, wrong population names, ...) counts as missing.

Task type
A: gate one plate (gating + QC)
Raw data
30 FCS files (one plate)
Budget
2 h / 150 actions
Environment
Python + FlowKit in a terminal (no GUI); gates handed in as GatingML

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

EXP22004263, WT vs PGRN-KO run of 20-Mar-2023. DIV8 mouse primary neurons, WT and PGRN-KO, were treated for 5 h with camptothecin (1/5/10/20 uM, two wells each), DMSO, or no treatment (NT). Cells were then stained with Zombie NIR (dead cells, RL3) and CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green (caspase-active cells, BL1) and acquired unfixed on the Attune NxT. Each genotype has three staining controls: no stain, Zombie only and caspase only. The flow plate map puts one genotype in rows A/B and the other in rows C/D. Thirty FCS files exist; A4/A6/C4/C6 (one DMSO and one NT position per genotype) were not acquired, and B5/B6/D5/D6 exist but are not in the notebook plate map. The scientist gated in FlowJo: Cells (ellipse FSC-A/SSC-A) -> Single Cells (polygon SSC-H/SSC-A) -> Live (rectangle Comp-RL3-A x SSC-A) -> Caspase+ (rectangle Comp-BL1-A x SSC-A), using an embedded 2x2 compensation matrix with an implausible RL3->BL1 coefficient of 1.875.

Natural traps in this plate (not hinted to the model)

typewhere
stale_channel_labelBL1-A labelled 'AAV-GFP-Caspase-A' in all 30 files; no AAV/GFP in this experiment
bad_controlCompensation group A1-A3: the workspace gates 'BL1-A+' on A2 and 'RL3-A+' on A3, i.e. A2 treated as the BL1 control and A3 as the RL3 control, the reverse of the notebook map (A2 = Zombie only, A3 = caspase only). The resulting RL3->BL1 spill of 1.875 is implausible and was applied to all samples.
saturationPlate-wide: SSC-A saturated in about 13-40% of events in every file (lowest B3 13.4%, B6 15.6%; highest C5 40.0%)
too_few_eventsB6 (8,004 total events), B3 (13,995), D5 (18,412). Tiny Live/Caspase+ counts in B5, B6, D5, D6 (Live a few hundred to ~1.2k events)
clogCandidates with elevated rate CV and/or low-rate bins: D3 (CV 33.3%, max bin 2.31x), D4 (CV 30.5%, 2 low bins, max 2.03x), B1 (CV 29.1%, 1 low bin, max 2.5x); weaker: C9, C10, C11, D5, D6
mislabelB5, B6, D5, D6 acquired but absent from the notebook plate map; A4/A6/C4/C6 in the plate map but not acquired
normalisation_stepPrism caspase values (WT end .x4, KO end .x8) are consistent with a per-genotype constant background subtraction; the values also differ from the saved gating (older gating?)

Expert review list

Everything any generation stage flagged for an expert, plus standing caveats. Nothing here is graded until an expert decides.

Task brief and plate layout (stage 1)

  • Confirm genotype assignment: rows A/B = WT, rows C/D = PGRN-KO. This was inferred from Prism viability values, not recorded in the notebook.
  • What are wells B5, B6, D5, D6? They are not in the plate map and their treatment is unknown. Should they be excluded from frequency grading or labelled 'mislabeled_or_unexpected' in QC?
  • Control identity conflict: the notebook map says A2/C2 = Zombie only and A3/C3 = caspase only, but the FlowJo compensation group treated A2 as the BL1 control and A3 as the RL3 control. The saved counts (A2 caspase+ ~3%, A3 caspase+ ~23%) support the notebook. Confirm, and decide whether A2/A3 should be labelled bad_control or the comp matrix treated as the defect.
  • Zombie-only controls A2 and C2 show essentially 100% Live in the saved gating while NT both-dye wells show ~8-14% dead. Is the Zombie-only control valid (possible bad_control)?
  • Ground truth for Live/Caspase+ uses the implausible compensation, while agents gate uncompensated. Should Live/Caspase_pos references be recomputed without compensation, or tolerances widened, especially for low-viability wells?
  • Should plate-wide SSC-A saturation (13-40% of events) be labelled ambiguous for all wells?
  • Prism values differ from the saved gating, with an apparent constant background subtraction (WT .x4, KO .x8) and an outlier at D4 caspase. They should not be used for grading; confirm.
  • Clog candidates (D3, D4, B1) and low-event wells (B6, B3, D5) need expert QC labels in stage 2.

QC labels to confirm (stage 2)

  • A2: ambiguous (bad_control, confidence low)
  • A3: ambiguous (bad_control, confidence low)
  • A7: ambiguous (mislabeled_or_unexpected, confidence low)
  • B1: ambiguous (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence medium)
  • B5: ambiguous (too_few_events, confidence medium)
  • B6: unusable (too_few_events, confidence high)
  • C2: ambiguous (bad_control, confidence low)
  • C3: ambiguous (bad_control, confidence low)
  • C7: ambiguous (mislabeled_or_unexpected, confidence low)
  • C9: ambiguous (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence low)
  • D3: ambiguous (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence medium)
  • D4: ambiguous (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence medium)
  • D5: unusable (too_few_events, confidence high)
  • D6: ambiguous (too_few_events, confidence low)

Answer key (stage 2)

  • B6 and D5 labelled unusable (too_few_events): The defect is low live-cell recovery (Live 382 and 380; Caspase_pos 65 and 25), not an instrument failure. An expert should confirm that a Live parent <500 events is the right cut and that B5 (513) stays ambiguous.
  • Clog candidates B1, D3, D4 (also C9, C10, C11, D2, D6) labelled ambiguous: Metrics show 1-2 isolated low-rate bins and 2-2.5x bursts with the full volume acquired. Whether these are mid-run interruptions or benign end-of-run gap/burst patterns needs a look at the Time plots.
  • SSC-A saturation policy (13-40% of events per well): Treated as a plate-wide caveat. Wells with >=35% saturation (C1, C3, C5, C8, C9) are ambiguous; the rest are fine on this metric. An expert should confirm that flagging plate-wide saturation should not count as a catch.
  • Zombie-only controls A2/C2 (100.0% Live) and caspase-only controls A3/C3 (~11-15% outside Live): Neither behaves as labelled for RL3. Possible control preparation error or mix-up; labelled ambiguous bad_control. Also decide whether the stage-1 gating guidance to use A3/C3 for the Live boundary should be revised.
  • Reference Live and Caspase+ come from compensated channels with an implausible matrix: Agents gate uncompensated data. Recommend recomputing Live and Caspase_pos references with identity compensation (the investigation has MN_21Mar_comp_effect.csv for Caspase+; the Live shift is unquantified). Also confirm which of the two embedded matrices ('Compensation' vs 'Compensation-1') was applied to samples; the investigation reports Compensation-1.
  • NT both-dye wells A7 (32.64%) and C7 (53.26%) Caspase+: Higher than DMSO and most treated wells, and excluded from Prism. Possible mislabel; labelled ambiguous.
  • Prism background subtraction and D4 caspase value: The offset is not recoverable and D4 Prism (29.98) vs saved (24.21) is unexplained. Prism is not used for grading.
  • Identity of B5, B6, D5, D6: Not in the plate map. Genotype assigned from row only. Low viability suggests a high-dose or other harsh condition.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • Uncompensated references for Live and Caspase_pos: The references use Comp-RL3/Comp-BL1 under an implausible matrix. Recompute with identity compensation (MN_21Mar_comp_effect.csv covers Caspase+). Also compute, per well, the fraction of Single Cells with Comp-RL3 < -11,012 to confirm or refute the bright-caspase exclusion artifact. If it is large in treated wells, widen A-FREQ-04 or switch to the uncompensated references.
  • Exclusion of A3/C3 from Live and Caspase_pos grading (stage-4 decision): Based on the geometric inference that their non-Live events are a compensation artifact. Reinstate them if the per-well check shows otherwise.
  • Which embedded matrix ('Compensation' vs 'Compensation-1') FlowJo applied to samples: Overlap re-application for A-GATE-03/04 assumes Compensation-1 (1.875), per the investigation.
  • B6 and D5 as unusable catches (D5 confidence lowered to medium): The call rests on a Live parent of about 380 events, which makes Caspase_pos unreliable. Live % itself is valid. Confirm that an expert would mark the whole well unusable, and that B5 (513 Live) stays ambiguous.
  • New gating_strategy.md sentence: leave events at the top of the SSC-A scale out of Cells: Inferred from saved counts (the ellipse excludes ≥74–87% of saturated events), not quoted from the scientist. Approve the wording.
  • A-RANK-01 Caspase_pos thresholds (0.9/0.5): Clustered treated-well values plus a systematic uncompensated shift may give a correct gate rho < 0.9.
  • Clog candidates B1, D3, D4 (and C9, C10, C11, D2, D6): Ambiguous on summary metrics only. Time plots should be inspected before any is promoted to a catch.
  • Zombie-only controls A2/C2 at 100% Live: Unexplained (possible missing Zombie). Ambiguous, ungraded; confirm.
  • Genotype row assignment (A/B = WT, C/D = PGRN-KO) and identity of B5/B6/D5/D6: Inferred from Prism viability ordering (strong match) and row grouping. Not recorded in the notebook.
  • Detector label mapping in the grader: 'AAV-GFP-Caspase-A' → BL1-A and 'LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A' (contains a space) → RL3-A must survive any Cytoflow label sanitisation.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Ordering conflict: under fixed stage budgets, a flag-everything agent (0.861) outscores a sloppy-gating agent (0.677). Accept this as inherent to type A (QC is only 15%), or authorise a template change (e.g. a qc-based cap) for future plates?
  • Uncompensated references: recompute Live and Caspase_pos references with identity compensation before finalising A-GATE-03/04, A-FREQ-03/04 and A-RANK-01. Also check per well the fraction of Single Cells with Comp-RL3 < -11,012 (the bright-caspase exclusion artifact).
  • Confirm the stage-4 exclusion of A3/C3 from Live/Caspase_pos grading, and update 02_expected_values.csv accordingly.
  • Confirm which embedded matrix ('Compensation' vs 'Compensation-1') FlowJo applied to samples.
  • Confirm B6/D5 as unusable catches (D5 confidence now medium) and B5 (513 Live events) as ambiguous.
  • Confirm A-QC-01 max_flagged = 15. A very conservative agent could flag up to ~21 caveat wells and lose all catch credit.
  • A-RANK-01 thresholds (0.9/0.5) may penalise a correct uncompensated Caspase_pos gate on clustered treated-well values. Verify by re-gating with the scientist's boundaries on raw data.
  • Approve the stage-4 gating_strategy.md sentence telling agents to leave saturated-SSC events out of Cells (inferred from counts, not quoted).
  • Clog candidates (B1, D3, D4, C9, C10, C11, D2, D6) remain ambiguous pending inspection of the Time plots.
  • Genotype row assignment (A/B = WT, C/D = PGRN-KO) and the identity of B5/B6/D5/D6 are inferred; confirm them.

Excluded from grading (grading_overrides.json)

  • Caspase_pos: The scientist's caspase gates were drawn on data compensated with an impossible bleed-through value (RL3 -> BL1 = 1.80 in the saved workspace; the dyes use different lasers, so the real leak is near 0, gap G2). Agents may not compensate in this task, so their caspase gates and the scientist's are drawn on different data. The control tubes cannot measure the true leak (dying cells glow green on their own), so no unique corrected reference exists. Expert review: decide the correct compensation and re-derive the caspase reference before grading it.

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Percentage tolerances were chosen by the model, not calibrated against data the way the gate thresholds are: Live: rel 30%, floor 2.0 pp, abs 6.0 pp
  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions): zero credit at the expert 25th percentile, full credit at the expert median, by population size (Task A v2, 2026-11-09). Full credit therefore needs median expert agreement, which about half of real expert pairs miss. Population size is the share of the parent, so a scatter gate that keeps only a few % of events because of debris is binned as a small population. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Exact prompt given to the model (instruction.md)

Gate a CellEvent caspase-3/7 + Zombie NIR plate (mouse primary neurons)

Goal: with FlowKit (Python), gate all 30 wells of one Attune NxT plate as Cells → Single_Cells → Live → Caspase_pos, export per-well counts, and flag every well whose data should not be used.

Experiment

  • Assay: CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green flow assay with Zombie NIR viability dye. Acquired 20-Mar-2023 on an Attune NxT, unfixed.
  • Cells: WT and PGRN-KO mouse primary neurons (DIV8).
  • Treatment: camptothecin 1, 5, 10 or 20 µM (two wells each), DMSO vehicle, or no treatment (NT), for 5 h.
  • Staining after treatment: Zombie NIR (1:500, 10 min), trypsin harvest, CellEvent Caspase-3/7 (1:1000, 30 min, 37 °C).
  • Per-well genotype, treatment and stain: /task/inputs/plate_layout.csv.
  • Wells with treatment = unrecorded have no entry in the notebook plate map. Gate and report them like every other well.
  • replicate = 0 means the replicate number is not recorded.

Inputs

Path Content
/task/inputs/raw/ 30 FCS files, one per well (Caspase_primaryneurons_caspase_Group_<well>.fcs)
/task/inputs/plate_layout.csv file, well, genotype, treatment, stain, replicate, is_control, control_type
/task/inputs/gating_strategy.md Written gating strategy: populations, channels, gate shapes

Channels

Each channel has a detector ID ($PnN) and a text label stored in the FCS file ($PnS).

Detector Name in the FCS file ($PnS) Real dye Marks
FSC-A / FSC-H FSC-A / FSC-H scatter size
SSC-A / SSC-H SSC-A / SSC-H scatter granularity; singlet discrimination
BL1-A AAV-GFP-Caspase-A CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green caspase-3/7-active cells
RL3-A LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A Zombie NIR dead cells (bright); live = Zombie-negative
Time Time n/a acquisition time

The AAV-GFP part of the BL1-A label is stale: there is no AAV or GFP in this experiment. BL1-A carries CellEvent caspase only.

Populations to report (exact names, in this order)

# Population Parent Channels Definition
1 Cells all_events FSC-A, SSC-A intact cells, debris excluded
2 Single_Cells Cells SSC-A, SSC-H singlets
3 Live Single_Cells RL3-A (+ SSC-A) Zombie NIR-negative
4 Caspase_pos Live BL1-A (+ SSC-A) CellEvent caspase-3/7-positive

Use these exact strings as the FlowKit gate names and in counts.csv.

Procedure and tool rules

  • Gating rules:
  • Use the full data (no subsampling).
  • Use one gate per population, applied to all wells.

Deliverables (all in /task/outputs/)

File Content
gates.xml Your gating strategy as GatingML 2.0, written with flowkit.export_gatingml (see Software). It must load with flowkit.parse_gating_xml. One gate per reported population, named exactly as the population.
counts.csv Columns file, well, population, count, parent_population, pct_of_parent
flags.csv Columns file, well, usable, reason_category, evidence
notes.md At most one page with headings ## Gates, ## Quality control, ## Deviations from the strategy, in that order

counts.csv rules - One row per file × population: 30 × 4 = 120 rows. - count: integer events in the population. - parent_population: all_events for Cells; otherwise the parent from the population table. - pct_of_parent: count / parent count × 100, as a 0–100 float.

flags.csv rules - One row per file (30 rows). - usable: yes or no. - reason_category: one of ok, clog_or_interrupted_flow, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabeled_or_unexpected, other. - usable = yes requires ok. - usable = no requires a category other than ok. - Flag any well whose data should not be used. - evidence on every usable = no row: - must give well-specific numbers, time-resolved where relevant (e.g. event counts, event-rate behaviour over Time, % events at scale maximum); - must include confidence=high, confidence=medium or confidence=low.

notes.md rules - ## Gates: how and why each gate was placed, including which control wells set each fluorescence boundary. - ## Quality control: how wells were judged. - ## Deviations from the strategy: every departure from gating_strategy.md, or "none".

Time budget

2 hours.

Software (FlowKit version of this task)

  • Python 3 with FlowKit 1.2.3 (plus flowio, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, openpyxl) is installed. There is no graphical analysis program.
  • Load each file with flowkit.Sample(path). Build one flowkit.GatingStrategy for all wells, with flowkit.Dimension and flowkit.gates.RectangleGate, PolygonGate or EllipsoidGate (no quadrant or Boolean gates).
  • Gate names must be valid XML IDs: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (no spaces or +).
  • One gate per reported population, named exactly as the population and nested under its parent population (the first population's gate sits at the root). A population's events are its own gate within its parent.
  • Raw (uncompensated) data only. Every gate dimension uses compensation_ref="uncompensated"; apply no compensation or spillover correction.
  • Channels. FlowKit gate dimensions use the detector ID ($PnN, e.g. BL1-A), not the text label.
  • Transforms. You may draw gates on transformed axes (for example flowkit.transforms.LogicleTransform, added with add_transform and referenced by transformation_ref).
  • Save the strategy with flowkit.export_gatingml(strategy, open("/task/outputs/gates.xml", "wb")) and check that it reloads with flowkit.parse_gating_xml.
  • Counts. counts.csv must be the counts these saved gates give on each file (strategy.gate_sample(sample)), with no per-well changes.
  • Looking at data. Save plots as PNG files and open the image files to view them.

How you work

You work in a terminal (bash, working directory /task).

  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save gates.xml and your output files early and often.

Input files in /task/inputs (read-only)

inputs/gating_strategy.md

Gating strategy: CellEvent caspase-3/7 + Zombie NIR, mouse primary neurons

Use a single gate set and apply it unchanged to all 30 wells. Gate on uncompensated channels; apply no bleedthrough correction.

Sequence

# Population Parent Plot (x vs y) Original gate shape FlowKit implementation
1 Cells all events FSC-A vs SSC-A ellipse around the main cell cloud, excluding low-FSC debris EllipsoidGate, or a PolygonGate approximating the ellipse
2 Single_Cells Cells SSC-H vs SSC-A 4-vertex polygon along the singlet diagonal PolygonGate
3 Live Single_Cells RL3-A (LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A) vs SSC-A rectangle around the Zombie NIR-negative events RectangleGate on RL3-A × SSC-A; a 1-D RectangleGate on RL3-A is also acceptable
4 Caspase_pos Live BL1-A (AAV-GFP-Caspase-A) vs SSC-A rectangle around the CellEvent-bright events RectangleGate on BL1-A × SSC-A; a 1-D RectangleGate on BL1-A is also acceptable

Placing the fluorescence boundaries

  • These are guidance, not a record of how the original cut-offs were chosen.
  • Live (RL3-A):
  • Use the no-stain wells (A1, C1) and the caspase-only wells (A3, C3) to see where Zombie NIR-negative events lie.
  • Use treated wells to confirm that a separate Zombie-bright population falls outside the gate.
  • Caspase_pos (BL1-A):
  • Use the no-stain wells (A1, C1) and the Zombie-only wells (A2, C2) to see where caspase-negative events end.
  • Place the lower boundary above that population.
  • SSC-A limits on the rectangles should keep the gated cells and exclude events at the scatter extremes. Record your reasoning in notes.md.

How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
CellsEllipse around the main FSC-A/SSC-A cell cloud, excluding the low-FSC/low-SSC debris corner. It keeps 36-64% of events per well (lowest in the high-event KO control/treated wells C1-C3, C5, C8, C9; highest in the low-event wells B3, B6). On this plate 13-40% of events sit at the SSC-A maximum, so the treatment of the saturated top edge is part of the gate's definition.A polygon can only approximate the ellipse, and agents may handle the saturated SSC-A band differently. Overlap thresholds should be on the lenient side of the size-based calibration. Saturated events are removed by Single_Cells in any case, so downstream populations are insensitive to this choice.
Single_Cells4-vertex polygon along the SSC-H vs SSC-A singlet diagonal. It excludes doublets (high SSC-A for a given SSC-H) and all events at the SSC-A maximum, and keeps 78-87% of Cells in every well.Reproducible exactly as a polygon in linear raw units. Use the standard size-based threshold for a large population.
LiveRectangle on Comp-RL3-A x SSC-A. It spans the Zombie-negative population from slightly below zero up to a boundary just above the no-stain distribution: A1 100.0%, C1 99.99% Live. The SSC-A range trims the lowest-SSC events and stays below the saturated top. Treated wells show a separate Zombie-bright population outside the gate (e.g. D4 8.95% Live, B3 17.95%).The agent gates raw RL3-A; the scientist gated Comp-RL3-A. Comp-RL3 = (RL3 - 0.0849*BL1)/0.841 under 'Compensation-1'. Caspase-bright events therefore shift toward lower Comp-RL3 and are more likely to be called Live in the original, and the 1/0.841 factor shifts the effective upper bound. Graders must apply the scientist's gate to data compensated with the workspace matrix and the agent's gate to raw data. Expect lower overlap in high-caspase and low-viability wells. Use the lenient end of the calibrated threshold.
Caspase_posRectangle on Comp-BL1-A x SSC-A. The lower BL1 bound sits in the extreme upper tail of the caspase-negative wells: no-stain A1 3.2% and C1 0.86% positive; Zombie-only A2 3.08% and C2 0.84% positive. The caspase-only wells show a distinct bright subset (A3 22.65%, C3 20.2%). The upper bound is at the top of scale. The SSC-A lower bound is higher than Live's, so low-SSC live events are excluded.The original used compensated BL1: Comp-BL1 = (BL1 - 1.875*RL3)/0.841, from an implausible coefficient. The investigation's identity-compensation re-run moved Caspase+ %Live by a median of 2.7 pp and a maximum of 14 pp, largest in low-viability wells. 1-D Range/Threshold variants also differ through the SSC-A lower bound. Use the lenient end of the calibrated threshold. Low-viability wells are excluded from grading (see grading_exclusions).

Grading tolerances per population
populationabs_pprel_pct_if_smallfloor_ppsmall_threshold_pctmin_parent_eventsjustification
Cells5.020.02.010.05000Hand-drawn polygon approximating a FlowJo ellipse. Open-source re-application agreed within a median of 1-1.6 pp and at most 2.7 pp on main populations, but a free-hand redraw adds placement variance. 13-40% of events pile up at the SSC-A maximum, so the treatment of the top edge can move Cells % by several points. All reference values are 36-64%, so the small-population rule never applies. All wells have at least 8,004 events.
Single_Cells3.020.01.510.02000Polygon, exactly reproducible in linear units. Reference values are a tight 78-87%. Remaining variance comes from vertex placement on a diagonal band; 3 pp is roughly the spread an expert redraw produces. The smallest parent is 5,107 Cells (B6).
Live6.030.02.010.02000Rectangle gate, but the reference is on Comp-RL3-A while agents must gate raw RL3-A. The comp subtracts 0.085*BL1 and rescales by 1/0.841, so caspase-bright events and the effective upper bound move. This shift was not quantified by the investigation, hence the wider abs_pp. Values span 3.6-100%; wells under 10% get 30% relative tolerance with a 2 pp floor.
Caspase_pos5.050.01.510.0500Leaf rectangle on Comp-BL1-A with an implausible RL3->BL1 coefficient (1.875). Turning compensation off moved Caspase+ by a median of 2.7 pp (max 14 pp, in excluded wells), so 5 pp covers the typical shift. Credit decays linearly to 10 pp. Small references (control wells 0.84-3.2%) get 50% relative tolerance with a 1.5 pp floor, because the boundary sits in the steep upper tail of the negative population. Wells with Live <10% of singlets are excluded.

Code-scored criteria re-apply the agent's saved gates to the raw FCS files. Numbers the agent typed are only checked for consistency. Judged criteria are scored by ONE LLM judge from the other model family than the agent (Anthropic agent → GPT-6 Luna; OpenAI agent → Claude Haiku 5.5); agent text is passed to it as untrusted data. A3_flowkit: Gate plate 230306: AAV serotype panel in WT PGP1 iPSC-derived neurons (GFP / Zombie NIR), 42 wells

Internal id: A_EXP23000352_09_Mar_2023_flowkit

FlowKit version. Same plate, answer key and scoring as A3, but the system works in a terminal with Python and FlowKit instead of drawing gates on screen in Cytoflow, and hands in its gates as a GatingML file (gates.xml). The check that gating was done in the GUI is removed.

Task A: gate a 42-well virus-serotype plate (9 Mar 2023), the big plate

In one sentence: draw four gates in a GUI to find, in each of 42 wells, the fraction of live single neurons that turned green (took up the virus), and flag broken wells.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • Cells. Human stem-cell-derived neurons.
  • Treatment. Seven different AAV serotypes, i.e. versions of a gene-delivery virus with different "shells", all carrying the same green-fluorescent-protein (GFP) gene, at three doses, in duplicate. A cell that the virus got into glows green.
  • Dyes. Zombie NIR (RL3, dead cells) and an NCAM neuron-surface marker (VL1, not used in this task).
  • Data: 42 FCS files, about 34 million events in total. That's large: loading takes minutes, and in our runs it ran an 8 GB sandbox out of memory.

What the agent has to do

  1. Open the prepared project and load all 42 files with the full data.
  2. Draw 4 gates, one set for every well: Cells, Singlets, Live, GFP_pos.
  3. Export counts.
  4. Inspect flow over time per well; flag defects.
  5. Write the deliverables.

Time: 3 hours.

What makes it tricky

  • No control wells at all. There is no unstained well and no "virus-free" well, so the agent has to decide where "GFP-negative" ends just from the shape of the clouds in the sample wells.
  • One well (D5) has almost no events. It must be flagged "too few events", the one clear QC catch.
  • Borderline wells. Possible clogs (B7, B8) and ran-dry wells (C3, C4) are judgement calls. The answer key treats them as ambiguous, so they're neither rewarded nor penalised.
  • Size and memory. The plate's size makes every redraw slow and memory-hungry.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The Cytoflow project with its gates, saved from the GUI. This is the agent's "classifier".
counts.csv For every well × population: how many events, and what % of the parent population that is.
flags.csv One row per well: usable yes/no, a reason category (clog, ran dry, too few events, ...) and numeric evidence.
notes.md One page explaining where each gate was drawn and why, the QC decisions, and any deviations. Required, but not scored.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task A v2, 2026-11-09

Share Item In plain terms
45% Gates For each gate, apply the agent's gate on its own to the cells the scientist kept at the step above, and compare it with the scientist's gate in every file: Jaccard = cells both selected / cells either selected. The scale comes from a public benchmark (FlowCAP-I) where 8 human experts gated the same data: zero credit at the overlap that 3 in 4 expert pairs beat (25th percentile), full credit at the median expert pair, linear in between. All gates count equally.
25% Read-out % For the populations the science uses (everything after cells and singlets): the share of wells whose % is within tolerance of the scientist's number. No credit outside the tolerance. Recomputed from the agent's gates, so it can't just type numbers.
15% Biology Do the control wells behave as expected, and do the wells rank in the same order as the scientist's?
10% Unusable wells Share of the truly bad wells caught × a penalty for each clean well flagged. No limit on flags; flagging everything scores 0.
5% QC evidence and reasons Judged by an LLM from the other model family: specific, numeric evidence, and the right reason for each caught well.

Populations whose reference can't be trusted are left out of grading and listed for expert review (e.g. the caspase gate on task A2).

Automatic zero:

  • the workflow is missing or broken;
  • fewer than 80% of the files are covered;
  • the key gates use the wrong detector;
  • the gating wasn't done in the Cytoflow GUI (the agent's command log shows it reading the raw files with code, or editing the saved workflow outside Cytoflow).

Strict format: a deliverable that breaks the specified format (wrong column names, wrong population names, ...) counts as missing.

Task type
A: gate one plate (gating + QC)
Raw data
42 FCS files (one plate)
Budget
3 h / 200 actions
Environment
Python + FlowKit in a terminal (no GUI); gates handed in as GatingML

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

EXP23000352 biological replicate 2. WT PGP1 iPSC-derived neurons were transduced with seven self-complementary AAV serotypes (AAV1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, DJ), all carrying the same STX1025 hU1-Rab7a / CMV-GFP construct, at 5e3, 1e4 and 5e4 vg/cell in duplicate wells. Cells were harvested 72 h later, stained live with Zombie NIR and anti-NCAM-BV421, trypsinised, and acquired on the Attune NxT on 06-Mar-2023 as 42 wells (A1-A12, B1-B12, C1-C12, D1-D6). The scientist's FlowJo workspace 09-Mar-2023.wsp applies a single 4-gate tree to all 42 samples: Cells (polygon FSC-A x SSC-A) -> Single Cells (polygon SSC-H x SSC-A) -> Live (rectangle RL3-A x SSC-A) -> GFP+ (rectangle BL1-A x SSC-A). There is no compensation, no NCAM gate in this workspace, and no answer table (Prism/CSV) for this run. The plate has no negative, unstained or single-stain control wells. QC candidates are one very-low-event well (D5), two wells with event-rate irregularities (B7, B8), and A1, which was acquired at a different flow rate.
