Expert review list

Everything any generation stage flagged for an expert, plus standing caveats. Nothing here is graded until an expert decides.

Task brief and plate layout (stage 1)

  • Serotype per well is not recorded in the 06-Mar flow plate map. Confirm whether the 6-well-block / notebook-order inference (A1-A6 AAV1 ... D1-D6 AAVDJ) is correct, if serotype is ever needed (e.g. a type-B variant). It is currently omitted from plate_layout.csv.
  • Confirm that '5e3-1/5e3-2' etc. mean dose (vg/cell) and duplicate number, and that the 03-06 flow plate map (not the 02-16 map, which has NT in A1) applies to 230306_flow.
  • Confirm that the NT and Count wells of culture plate 2 were never acquired on this run. Without them there is no GFP-negative or viability control, so the GFP_pos and Live cut-offs are judgement calls. Consider whether gate-overlap tolerances for Live and GFP_pos should be looser than usual.
  • Feasibility: start.flow will import ~33.9 M events (16 parameters). Verify Cytoflow load time and container memory (roughly 4+ GB as float64) before release. If it is infeasible, consider allowing documented subsampling only for display, which would conflict with A-PROC-01 as currently written.
  • QC label for D5: 153,195 events, Live ~641, GFP+ ~50 (saved counts) vs thousands in other wells. Proposed unusable (too_few_events), medium confidence. Confirm.
  • QC labels for B7 and B8: rate CV ~25-27% with 2 low-rate bins and max-bin bursts 1.46-1.70x, not at the end of the run. Inspect when the low-rate bins occur and whether scatter shifts. Decide unusable (clog_or_interrupted_flow) vs ambiguous.
  • QC label for A1: acquired at about twice the flow rate in 46 s (vol 155 µL). Proposed ambiguous. Confirm it should not be graded.
  • C3/C4 show mild end-of-run rate decline (0.72-0.73 of median). Proposed ambiguous or fine. Confirm.
  • The notebook's Serotype Panel Info table has '#VALUE!' in the 5e3 vg/cell volume column for AAV9 and AAVDJ, suggesting a possible dosing-calculation issue at 5e3 for those vectors. This is irrelevant for type A, but matters for any biology-level task built on this plate.
  • Should the A-WF-01 accepted forms include polygon gates for Live/GFP_pos (not offered in the brief), and should either axis order be accepted for the Singlets polygon (SSC-H x SSC-A vs SSC-A x SSC-H)?

QC labels to confirm (stage 2)

  • A1: ambiguous (other, confidence medium)
  • B7: ambiguous (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence medium)
  • B8: ambiguous (clog_or_interrupted_flow, confidence medium)
  • D5: unusable (too_few_events, confidence high)

Answer key (stage 2)

  • Live gate tightness: Saved Live is only 8-24% of singlets in every well, although the notebook says the cells looked healthy. The RL3-A cut-off may sit inside, rather than above, the Zombie-dim peak. An agent following the 'valley' guidance could then get systematically higher Live % and fail frequency and overlap. An expert should view RL3-A histograms against the reference upper edge before tolerances are finalised; if needed, adjust the gating_strategy guidance wording, without coordinates.
  • GFP_pos cut-off without a negative control: There is no untransduced or unstained well, so the reference cut-off cannot be validated against a control. Consider looser overlap calibration for GFP_pos.
  • D5 unusable label: The scientist kept D5 in the workspace and never labelled wells. The data defect is clear (10x fewer cells, 50 GFP+ events), but exclusion is a judgement.
  • B7/B8 labelled ambiguous: Rate CV 27.1/24.6% (plate median ~6%), 2 low-rate bins, bursts 1.70/1.46x, not at end of run. Our metrics do not record when the dips occur. If an expert sees a clear clog with scatter disruption, promote both to unusable (clog_or_interrupted_flow) and add them to the A-QC-01 catch list.
  • A1 faster acquisition: 46 s at ~21k ev/s (200 uL/min per investigation notes) vs ~98 s elsewhere. Atypical Cells/Singlets %. Kept ambiguous.
  • C7 scatter drift and C3/C4/C10 end-of-run decline: Labelled ambiguous by stated thresholds; confirm these are benign.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • Live reference cut-off (RL3-A upper edge < 1,000 raw units; Live 8-24% of singlets plate-wide): May sit inside the Zombie-dim peak rather than at a valley. The agent-facing 'valley' guidance could produce systematically higher Live %, depressing A-GATE-03/A-FREQ-03 and propagating to GFP_pos. An expert should view RL3-A histograms against the reference edge. Then either loosen the Live calibration and the A-FREQ-03 tolerance, or reword the gating_strategy guidance (no coordinates).
  • GFP_pos reference cut-off (BL1-A lower edge ~369 raw) with no negative control: Cannot be validated against a control. Decide whether finalise should use looser-than-standard overlap calibration, and confirm the A-FREQ-04 tolerance (3 pp / 30% relative, floor 1.0 pp).
  • D5 unusable (too_few_events), confidence high: It is the only catch well, and the scientist kept it in the workspace. If an expert rejects it, A-QC-01 and A-QC-04 have no target and must be re-specified.
  • B7/B8 ambiguous: Rate CV 27.1/24.6%, 2 low-rate bins, mid-run bursts 1.70x/1.46x. If an expert sees a clear clog, promote them to unusable, add them to the A-QC-01 wells, and add them to the A-QC-04 items.
  • B4/C2 relabelled ambiguous; A10/A12 remain fine (CV 8.6%, end-of-run 0.82/0.81): The fine/ambiguous line for mild end-of-run decline is arbitrary. Confirm that the fine wells nearest the boundary would not reasonably be flagged by an expert.
  • A1 ambiguous (46 s run at ~2x flow rate): Confirm it should not be graded for QC. It remains graded for gate overlap and frequency because the scientist's gates apply to the same events.
  • Feasibility of full-data import (~33.9 M events, subsampling forbidden by A-PROC-01): About 3.6x the tested load. Verify Cytoflow load time, plotting responsiveness and memory within the 3 h budget before release.
  • Plate-layout interpretation: The dose/duplicate meaning of the '5e3-1' labels and the absence of NT/Count wells from the 06-Mar flow run are inferred from the notebook flow plate map. Already listed by stage 1.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Sanity ordering conflict (structural): the required ordering (a) > (b) > (d) > (c) cannot be met for type A under the fixed stage budgets. A flag-everything agent with perfect gates loses at most the whole qc budget (0.15), so (c) >= 0.85. An agent with ~30%-too-loose gates loses roughly 0.25-0.30 across gate_overlap and frequency. This rubric therefore gives (a) 1.00 > (b) 0.90 > (c) 0.88 > (d) ~0.72. Achieving d > c would need a template change (larger qc budget, or a cap triggered by mass false alarms), which the stage rules forbid. Please confirm this is acceptable, or amend the type-A template.
  • Live reference cut-off (RL3-A upper edge < 1,000 raw; Live 8-24% of singlets plate-wide) may sit inside the Zombie-dim peak rather than at a valley. An expert should view RL3-A histograms before release. A-GATE-03 (0.185) and A-FREQ-03 depend on it, and errors cascade into A-GATE-04 (0.185).
  • GFP_pos has no negative control (reference BL1-A lower edge ~369 raw). Confirm looser overlap calibration in finalise and the A-FREQ-04 tolerance (3 pp / 30% relative, floor 1.0 pp).
  • D5 is the only catch well (A-QC-01 0.075 + A-QC-04 0.0175). If an expert rejects the unusable label, these weights must be re-specified.
  • B7/B8 are ambiguous (mid-run rate dips, CV 27.1/24.6%). If promoted to unusable, add them to A-QC-01 and A-QC-04, rescale per-catch credit, and revisit max_flagged.
  • B4/C2 were moved to ambiguous; A10/A12 remain fine near the end-of-run boundary (0.82/0.81). Confirm.
  • Feasibility: about 33.9 M events with subsampling forbidden (A-PROC-01). Verify Cytoflow load time and memory within 3 h before release.

Dropped by the finalise step

  • dropped A-WF-01: removed from the template (2026-11-05: Task A process/format stage removed (every attempt scored full))
  • dropped A-CNT-01: removed from the template (2026-11-05: Task A process/format stage removed (every attempt scored full))
  • dropped A-PROC-01: removed from the template (2026-11-05: Task A process/format stage removed (every attempt scored full))
  • dropped A-NOTE-01: removed from the template (2026-11-05: Task A process/format stage removed (every attempt scored full))
  • dropped A-NOTE-02: removed from the template (2026-11-05: Task A process/format stage removed (every attempt scored full))
  • Task A v2 (2026-11-09): A-GATES <- ['A-GATE-01', 'A-GATE-02', 'A-GATE-03', 'A-GATE-04'], A-READOUT <- ['A-FREQ-03', 'A-FREQ-04'], A-BIOLOGY <- ['A-RANK-01'], A-QC-CATCH <- ['A-QC-01', 'A-QC-02']
  • pre-flight format check: passed

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Percentage tolerances were chosen by the model, not calibrated against data the way the gate thresholds are: Live: rel 25%, floor 1.5 pp, abs 3.0 pp; GFP_pos: rel 30%, floor 1.0 pp, abs 3.0 pp
  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions): zero credit at the expert 25th percentile, full credit at the expert median, by population size (Task A v2, 2026-11-09). Full credit therefore needs median expert agreement, which about half of real expert pairs miss. Population size is the share of the parent, so a scatter gate that keeps only a few % of events because of debris is binned as a small population. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Exact prompt given to the model (instruction.md)

Gate plate 230306 (AAV serotype panel, iPSC-derived neurons) in FlowKit

Goal: gate all 42 wells of this plate down to GFP+ live single cells with FlowKit (Python), report event counts per population, and flag every well whose data should not be used.

Experiment

  • Cells: WT PGP1 iPSC-derived neurons in a 24-well culture format. This plate is biological replicate 2 of an AAV serotype panel.
  • Treatment:
  • self-complementary AAV1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9 or DJ, all carrying the same CMV-GFP construct;
  • doses 5e3, 1e4 or 5e4 vg/cell, each dose in duplicate wells;
  • harvested 72 h after transduction.
  • Staining, on live adherent cells before trypsinisation:
  • Zombie NIR 1:500, 15 min;
  • anti-NCAM-BV421 1:200, 30 min;
  • resuspended in PBS + 2% FBS.
  • Acquisition: Attune NxT, 06-Mar-2023, one FCS file per well. Notebook voltages: FSC 30, SSC 300, BL1 250, VL1 300, RL3 300.
  • Plate layout:
  • plate_layout.csv gives the dose and duplicate number of each well, taken from the notebook flow plate map.
  • The serotype of each well is not recorded in that map and is not needed for this task.
  • No biological conclusion is requested.

Channels

Channel names come from the labels stored in the FCS files. On this plate they match the dyes actually used. -H and -W versions of each channel are also present.

Detector ($PnN) Name in the FCS file ($PnS) Dye Marks Used for

SSC-A, SSC-H SSC-A, SSC-H none (scatter) granularity Cells, Singlets; y-axis of Live and GFP_pos
RL3-A LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A Zombie NIR (fixable amine-reactive viability dye) dead cells (bright); live cells are negative Live

Populations (report exactly these, in this order)

# population parent_population definition
1 Cells all_events intact cells on FSC-A vs SSC-A
2 Singlets Cells single cells on SSC-H vs SSC-A

4 GFP_pos Live GFP (BL1-A) positive

Use these names as the names of the gate operations in FlowKit.

Controls

  • This plate has no control wells. No untransduced, unstained, Zombie-only or NCAM-only wells were acquired. The notebook's non-transduced and cell-count culture wells are absent from the flow plate map and from raw/.
  • All 42 wells are transduced samples. In plate_layout.csv, is_control is false and control_type is none for every row.
  • Set the Live and GFP_pos boundaries from the populations visible in the sample wells, as described in gating_strategy.md. Use one boundary per gate for the whole plate.

Deliverables

Write everything to /task/outputs/.

Path Content
/task/outputs/counts.csv Columns file, well, population, count, parent_population, pct_of_parent.
/task/outputs/flags.csv Columns file, well, usable, reason_category, evidence.
/task/outputs/notes.md One page at most, with the headings ## Gates, ## Quality control, ## Deviations, in that order.

counts.csv

  • One row per file x population: 42 x 4 = 168 rows. population is one of Cells, Singlets, Live, GFP_pos.
  • file and well are exactly as in plate_layout.csv.
  • count is an integer: the number of events inside the population's own gate and all of its ancestor gates.
  • parent_population is all_events for Cells, Cells for Singlets, Singlets for Live, and Live for GFP_pos.
  • pct_of_parent is 100 x count / parent count, a float from 0 to 100. For Cells, the parent count is the file's total event count.

flags.csv

  • One row per file (42 rows).
  • usable is yes or no.
  • reason_category is one of ok, clog_or_interrupted_flow, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabeled_or_unexpected, other. Use ok if and only if usable = yes.
  • evidence gives numbers from that well, for example:
  • total events and gated population counts;
  • event rate over Time;
  • low-rate intervals or bursts, with their time position;
  • end-of-run rate;
  • % events at the scale maximum.
  • Rows with usable = no must end with confidence: high, confidence: medium or confidence: low.

notes.md

  • ## Gates: how each gate was placed and why, including which wells and plots set each fluorescence boundary.
  • ## Quality control: how wells were screened.
  • ## Deviations: every departure from gating_strategy.md, or None.

Constraints

  • Gate uncompensated data. Do not add bleedthrough, autofluorescence or bead-calibration operations, and do not subsample.
  • Use exactly one gate operation per reported population.
  • Time budget: 3 hours.

Software (FlowKit version of this task)

  • Python 3 with FlowKit 1.2.3 (plus flowio, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, openpyxl) is installed. There is no graphical analysis program.
  • Load each file with flowkit.Sample(path). Build one flowkit.GatingStrategy for all wells, with flowkit.Dimension and flowkit.gates.RectangleGate, PolygonGate or EllipsoidGate (no quadrant or Boolean gates).
  • Gate names must be valid XML IDs: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (no spaces or +).
  • One gate per reported population, named exactly as the population and nested under its parent population (the first population's gate sits at the root). A population's events are its own gate within its parent.
  • Raw (uncompensated) data only. Every gate dimension uses compensation_ref="uncompensated"; apply no compensation or spillover correction.
  • Channels. FlowKit gate dimensions use the detector ID ($PnN, e.g. BL1-A), not the text label.
  • Transforms. You may draw gates on transformed axes (for example flowkit.transforms.LogicleTransform, added with add_transform and referenced by transformation_ref).
  • Save the strategy with flowkit.export_gatingml(strategy, open("/task/outputs/gates.xml", "wb")) and check that it reloads with flowkit.parse_gating_xml.
  • Counts. counts.csv must be the counts these saved gates give on each file (strategy.gate_sample(sample)), with no per-well changes.
  • Looking at data. Save plots as PNG files and open the image files to view them.

How you work

You work in a terminal (bash, working directory /task).

  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save gates.xml and your output files early and often.

Input files in /task/inputs (read-only)

inputs/gating_strategy.md

Gating strategy: plate 230306 (AAV serotype panel, iPSC-derived neurons)

  • Sequence: Cells -> Singlets -> Live -> GFP_pos.
  • One gate tree, applied identically to all 42 wells.
  • Uncompensated data. No compensation was used.
  • NCAM (VL1-A) is not gated.

Gates

Population Parent Axes (x vs y) Scientist's gate shape Accepted FlowKit gates
Cells all events FSC-A vs SSC-A polygon PolygonGate
Singlets Cells SSC-H vs SSC-A polygon PolygonGate
Live Singlets RL3-A (Zombie NIR) vs SSC-A rectangle RectangleGate on RL3-A x SSC-A, or a 1-D RectangleGate on RL3-A
GFP_pos Live BL1-A (GFP) vs SSC-A rectangle RectangleGate on BL1-A x SSC-A, or a 1-D RectangleGate on BL1-A

Gate descriptions

  • Cells: polygon around the main cell cloud. It excludes low-FSC-A / low-SSC-A debris and events piled at the scale maximum.
  • Singlets: narrow polygon along the diagonal of SSC-H vs SSC-A. It excludes events whose SSC-A is too high for their SSC-H (doublets and aggregates).
  • Live:
  • The rectangle's RL3-A range runs from the lowest values up to the Zombie NIR cut-off. Its SSC-A range spans almost the whole axis.
  • The RL3-A upper edge is the boundary that matters.
  • GFP_pos:
  • The rectangle runs from the GFP cut-off to the top of the BL1-A axis, with a wide SSC-A range.
  • The BL1-A lower edge is the boundary that matters.

Choosing the fluorescence cut-offs (guidance, not a record of the scientist's choice)

The notebook does not record how the Live and GFP cut-offs were chosen, and the plate has no unstained, single-stain or untransduced well.

  • Live: on Singlets, put the RL3-A cut-off in the valley between the Zombie NIR-dim (live) and Zombie NIR-bright (dead) populations. Check that the valley sits in the same place across wells.
  • GFP_pos:
  • Put the BL1-A cut-off just above the upper edge of the GFP-negative Live population.
  • Judge that edge on the wells with the fewest GFP-bright events.
  • Apply the same cut-off to every well.

FlowKit notes

  • A 1-D RectangleGate with only a maximum (or only a minimum) selects events below (or above) the cut-off.
  • Draw fluorescence gates on a logicle axis (flowkit.transforms.LogicleTransform) so the negative populations are visible, or give raw-unit bounds.
  • A population's events are those inside its own gate and all its ancestor gates (nest each gate under its parent).

population (task name)scientist populationgate typechannelsparentreproducible in Cytoflow
Cells/CellsPolygonGate (4 vertices)FSC-A, SSC-Aall_events (FlowJo root)Polygon operation on FSC-A x SSC-A, applied to all events.
Singlets/Cells/Single CellsPolygonGate (4 vertices)SSC-H, SSC-ACellsPolygon operation on SSC-H x SSC-A (either axis order), restricted to Cells == True.
Live/Cells/Single Cells/LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A, SSC-A subsetRectangleGateRL3-A, SSC-ASingletsRange2D (rectangle) on RL3-A x SSC-A, or a 1-D Range on RL3-A. The reference rectangle spans almost the whole SSC-A axis, so a 1-D Range is nearly equivalent. A Threshold cannot express it because Threshold selects events above the cut-off.
GFP_pos/Cells/Single Cells/LiveDead-Zombie NIR-A, SSC-A subset/AAV-GFP-GFP-A, SSC-A subsetRectangleGateBL1-A, SSC-ALiveRange2D on BL1-A x SSC-A reproduces it exactly. A Threshold or Range on BL1-A is accepted but omits the rectangle's SSC-A limits and its finite upper BL1-A edge.
How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
CellsPolygon around the main FSC-A/SSC-A cell cloud. It excludes the very large low-scatter debris fraction (only about 7-16% of events fall in the gate in normal wells) and the events piled at the scale maximum. No control is involved; the gate is placed by morphology.Polygon, so exactly reproducible. The population is a minority of events and its lower-left edge cuts through dense debris, so small vertex shifts change counts noticeably. Use standard calibration for a medium-sized population. Gate coordinates are linear raw units in both FlowJo and Cytoflow, so no transform conversion is needed.
SingletsNarrow polygon along the SSC-H vs SSC-A diagonal. It excludes events with excess SSC-A for their SSC-H (doublets and aggregates). Placed by morphology; no control is involved.Polygon, exactly reproducible. The population is large (about 62-92% of Cells), so overlap should be high. Accept either axis order.
LiveRectangle on RL3-A x SSC-A running from below zero to a low Zombie NIR cut-off, with an SSC-A extent covering nearly the full axis. Only the upper RL3-A edge matters. The plate has no unstained or Zombie-only well, so the cut-off was a judgement on the sample wells. The notebook does not record how it was chosen. One cut-off is used for all 42 wells.Rectangle, exactly reproducible. The reference Live population is only about 8-24% of singlets, so overlap is very sensitive to where the RL3-A cut-off sits relative to the Zombie-dim peak. Without a viability control, expect more inter-analyst spread than usual; calibrate as a small, control-free population. Expert check recommended (see needs_expert_review).
GFP_posRectangle on BL1-A x SSC-A from the GFP cut-off up to a high BL1-A value, with wide SSC-A limits that trim only low- and very-high-SSC slivers. Only the lower BL1-A edge matters. There is no untransduced or unstained well on this plate, so the cut-off had to be set above the GFP-negative Live population as seen in the transduced wells. One cut-off is used for all wells.Rectangle, exactly reproducible with Range2D. 1-D Threshold/Range forms will include the trimmed SSC slivers and any events above the upper BL1-A edge, so they may slightly exceed the reference counts. Leaf counts are 207-1955 events per well (excluding D5), and most wells are below 10% of parent. Use a lenient small-population calibration because there is no negative control.

Grading tolerances per population
populationabs_pprel_pct_if_smallsmall_threshold_pctmin_parent_eventsjustification
Cells2.020.010.010000Hand-drawn polygon whose edge cuts dense debris. Reference values are about 7-16% of all events, many below 10%. For such values, 20% relative (floor 1.0 pp) is about 1.5-2 pp. Open-source re-gating of this workspace agreed within 2.0% at most (133/168 rows within 1%), so the tolerance is dominated by gate-drawing variability, not software.
Singlets5.020.010.05000Large population (62-92% of Cells, excluding D5). SSC-H/SSC-A singlet polygons vary between analysts by a few points. 5 pp absolute is standard for a large morphological gate.
Live3.025.010.05000Rectangle with a single operative RL3-A edge and no viability control. Values are 8-24% of singlets, so a small cut-off shift moves the percentage substantially. 3 pp above 10%, and 25% relative (floor 1.5 pp) below 10% (six wells are just under 10%). Credit decays linearly to 2x tolerance.
GFP_pos3.030.010.01000Leaf population of 207-1955 events (D5 excluded). Values are 1.4-31% of Live, mostly below 10%. There is no untransduced or unstained well, so the cut-off is a judgement. 30% relative (floor 1.0 pp) below 10%, 3 pp above. Threshold/Range forms ignore the reference SSC limits, which adds a small positive bias that this tolerance absorbs.

Code-scored criteria re-apply the agent's saved gates to the raw FCS files. Numbers the agent typed are only checked for consistency. Judged criteria are scored by ONE LLM judge from the other model family than the agent (Anthropic agent → GPT-6 Luna; OpenAI agent → Claude Haiku 5.5); agent text is passed to it as untrusted data. B1_flowkit: PGRN-conditioned media vs camptothecin-induced caspase activation in H4 WT / PGRN-KO lines (plate of 16-Dec-2022): analyse, conclude, decide

Internal id: B_base_conditioned_media_flowkit

FlowKit version. Same plate, answer key and scoring as B1, but the system works in a terminal with Python and FlowKit instead of drawing gates on screen in Cytoflow, and hands in its gates as a GatingML file (gates.xml). The check that gating was done in the GUI is removed.

Task B (v3), base: does "conditioned media" rescue progranulin-deficient cells? (78 wells, 16-Dec-2022)

In one sentence: analyse the plate, answer whether medium from normal cells lowers apoptosis in progranulin-knock-out cells, and decide what the lab should do next.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • Cells. H4 brain-tumour cells: normal (WT) and two progranulin knock-out clones (E1, E3).
  • Treatment. A day in medium taken from WT cells ("conditioned media", collected after 24 h or 48 h), which should contain progranulin, or in plain medium. Then camptothecin (an apoptosis-inducing drug) at 2, 5 or 10 µM, or solvent only.
  • Readout. % of live cells with active caspase-3/7 (dying by apoptosis), from two dyes.
  • Data: 78 wells, duplicates. This is the scientist's second run; the first one failed.

What the agent must decide (nothing is pre-decided for it)

  • Detectors: which detector carries which dye (the files carry stale labels).
  • Wells: which wells are controls.
  • Gates: where to draw them.
  • Metric: which readout and whether to normalise.
  • Comparisons: which ones answer the question.
  • Conclusion: the overall answer (yes / partial / no).
  • Assay verdict and next action, chosen from a fixed list of seven.

Time: 5 hours.

The scientist's answer, rebuilt with one gate set

  • What stands:
  • the knock-outs have clearly more apoptosis than WT (+14 to +18 points at 10 µM);
  • the assay is usable;
  • the scientist's next step, proceed (apply it to cells treated with the RNAswap constructs), is supported by the plate.
  • What doesn't: the scientist's "partial rescue" claims depend on dead-cell cutoffs they tuned well by well (61 of 78 wells). With one gate set, most rescue comparisons are small or flip, so those claims are not graded. Expert review is needed on whether those per-well cutoffs were justified.
  • Graded overall answer: "partial" or "no".

Rubric: 14 scored items

  • Gating (20%): upstream gates, plus the marker gate at double weight.
  • QC (15%): exclusion set, evidence fact-check, the main QC problem (low cell yield in the 10 µM knock-out wells).
  • Summary (30%): condition means and differences within the plate's replicate noise, about 2.8 points per well.
  • Conclusion (35%):
  • directions;
  • the overall answer;
  • the next action (12% of the score);
  • 2 scientist claims;
  • no over-claiming;
  • 2 caveats.

What the agent is given, and what it isn't

  • Given:
  • the scientist's notebook plan up to this run, in their own words: aim, design, protocol, reagents, cytometer settings, plate map;
  • the raw files;
  • a Cytoflow project with the files loaded;
  • the exact output formats.
  • Not given:
  • which detector carries which dye (the file labels may be out of date; the plan's reagent list is the clue);
  • which wells are controls;
  • what metric to use, whether to normalise, which comparisons to make, what a bad well looks like;
  • the scientist's results, conclusion or next step.

This is the information the scientist had before writing their conclusion, and nothing we worked out.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The saved Cytoflow project with the agent's own gates.
counts.csv Counts per well × population, each population tagged with its role (cells / singlets / live / marker-positive).
flags.csv One row per well: issue type, numeric evidence, keep or exclude.
condition_summary.csv The agent's own conditions: which wells, mean, SD, metric, normalisation.
figure.png A plot (format-checked only).
report.md Question, Methods, Results, Conclusion, Caveats, Recommendation.
answer.json The comparisons (direction, size, confidence), an overall yes / partial / no, an assay verdict (fit / needs optimising / not fit) and a next action from a fixed list, the same in every task (proceed, repeat unchanged, repeat with a change, optimise a reagent or setting, change treatment or timing, switch assay, stop), plus what to change.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task B v4, 2026-11-09: six items, no double counting

Share (approx.) Item In plain terms
21% Gates Do the agent's gates pick out the same cells as the scientist's? Upstream gates and the marker gate count equally. Full credit only at the median agreement between human experts.
16% Data quality Excluding the wrong wells zeroes this item (a requirement, not points). Then: does the evidence for each flagged well quote numbers that are true for that file, and does the report spot the plate's main data problem (judge, yes/no)?
32% Summary numbers Condition means recomputed from the agent's own gates, and the differences between conditions, each within the scientist's own replicate noise.
6% Answer to the question The direction called for each comparison and the overall yes / partial / no. They count less because they mostly follow from the numbers above.
15% Next step The next action matches what the scientist actually decided, and names the specific change (judge, yes/no).
6–11% Findings and limits Key findings that aren't already scored elsewhere, no over-claiming, and the key caveats (judge, yes/no each).

Shares vary a little by plate: plates without a summary stage have five items, and claims that only repeated a graded comparison or the data problem were removed.

Automatic zero: - the workflow is missing; - coverage is under 80%; - the marker gate is on the wrong detector; - the counts don't come from the saved workflow; - the gating wasn't done in the GUI.

A main conclusion opposite to the scientist's is flagged, but doesn't change the score.

Two rules behind the answer key: - It is rebuilt with one gate set for all wells, because the scientists sometimes adjusted gates well by well. - A scientist decision or claim is only graded if this plate's data actually supports it.

The judge (a model from the other company) only answers yes/no questions; every fractional score comes from code.

Task type
B: plan to conclusion
Raw data
78 FCS files (one plate)
Budget
5 h / 400 actions
Environment
Python + FlowKit in a terminal (no GUI); gates handed in as GatingML

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

The plate is the second run (acquired 16-Dec-2022, folder 221216, 78 FCS files) of notebook entry EXP22004363. The entry asks whether conditioned media from WT H4 cells, which contains progranulin, lowers caspase-3/7 activation in the H4 PGRN-KO clones E1 and E3. Design: rows A–C and D–F are duplicate sets of WT / E1 / E3. Columns form blocks of four (24 h conditioned media | 48 h conditioned media | no conditioned media), and within each block the treatments are camptothecin 10 / 5 / 2 µM and DMSO. Row G holds the controls: no stain, L/D only, caspase only, and untreated wells per line. Cells were stained with CellEvent caspase-3/7 Green (BL1) and SYTOX AAdvanced dead-cell stain (BL2) and acquired unfixed on the Attune NxT. The scientist gated Cells (ellipse FSC-A/SSC-A) → Single Cells (polygon SSC-A/SSC-H) → Live (BL2-A range) → caspase+ (BL1-A range), and reported raw caspase+ % of Live with no background subtraction. The recorded conclusion was a partial rescue: CM lowered caspase+ % in the KO lines, mainly at 10 µM. The recorded decision was to apply the assay to GRN RNAswap-treated cells. The first run (02-Dec) failed and is excluded from scope and from every agent-facing text.

Natural traps in this plate (not hinted to the model)

typewhere
stale_channel_labelBL1-A is labelled 'AAV-GFP-GFP' in all 78 files but measures CellEvent caspase-3/7 Green
normalisation_stepPlate-wide. The scientist reported raw caspase+ % of Live with no background subtraction. Prism matched raw FlowJo values in 63/72 cells (normalisation.json rule 'none'). Agents may wrongly subtract the G1/G3 control values.
too_few_eventsC5 (3151 events), F5 (3184), B9 (3505), F9 (3608), C9 (4067), E9 (4147), E5 (4437). These are mostly 10 µM KO wells with low cell yield (C5 has ~609 Live events). Most likely biological (cytotoxicity / KO growth), not an acquisition fault.
ran_dryPlate-wide end-of-well depletion at 500 µL/min: C12, D1, D7, G6 (last10pct_rate_over_median 0.35–0.39, 3 low-rate bins), F12 and D6 (0.43), D5 (0.47). Our report calls this systematic and plate-wide, not a single bad tube. Treat as benign/ambiguous.
otherE10 has SSC-A median last/first quarter = 3.51 and FSC-A = 1.48, a scatter drift within the run. All other wells are <=1.47 on SSC. The cause is unconfirmed; ambiguous.
otherThe scientist used per-well versions of the Live gate (25 versions) and of the caspase+ gate (4 versions: C4, D1, D9, E9). Re-gating with one common gate moves several condition means by >3 pp and flips the sign of E1 24h-CM vs unconditioned at 10 µM (−12.1 pp with own gates vs +2.8 pp with a common gate).
otherPrism transcription errors relative to the saved gating: A4/D4 values swapped (WT 24h DMSO); D1 17.5 vs FlowJo 19.1; D5 12.2 vs 13.0; D6 10.7 vs 11.6; F1 29.6 vs 31.6; F4 24.9 vs 25.5. Grading must use FlowJo-saved values.
otherThe scientist's Cells gate is an ellipse; Cytoflow needs a polygon approximation

Expert review list

Everything any generation stage flagged for an expert, plus standing caveats. Nothing here is graded until an expert decides.

Task brief and plate layout (stage 1)

  • Row G (G1–G6): the conditioned-media status is not stated in the plan (uncoloured cells). Confirm 'not stated' vs 'No conditioned media'.
  • Confirm that the run-1 staining/acquisition protocol and cytometer settings (FSC-20; SSC-290; BL1-225; BL2-350) applied unchanged to the 16-Dec-2022 run.
  • Confirm that a detector-ID → on-screen-label table (without dyes) is acceptable under the type-B v3 policy. Without it the agent can still infer BL1/BL2 from the labels, but less directly.
  • The scientist's per-well Live/caspase+ gate edits make the reference conclusion gate-dependent (E1 24h CM at 10 µM flips under a common gate). Decide whether the answer key should use the scientist's own-gate values, require robustness to uniform gating, or drop the affected comparisons.
  • QC labels for low-event wells (C5, F5, B9, F9, C9, E9, E5) and end-of-run depletion wells (C12, D1, D7, G6, F12, D6, D5): we propose 'ambiguous'. Expert confirmation needed.
  • E10 SSC-A drift (last/first quarter median 3.51): an expert should check whether this well is usable.
  • FCS files contain the operator's real name in $OP (gap G16). Strip it from task copies?
  • Should the EXP number and the 'previous experiment' sentence in the rationale be kept? They are pre-run background, but they point to a related entry.

QC labels to confirm (stage 2)

  • B1: ambiguous (gate_sensitive_live_dead, confidence low)
  • B9: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • C5: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • C9: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • C12: ambiguous (ran_dry_plate_wide, confidence medium)
  • D1: ambiguous (ran_dry_plate_wide, confidence medium)
  • D7: ambiguous (ran_dry_plate_wide, confidence medium)
  • E5: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • E9: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • E10: ambiguous (scatter_drift, confidence low)
  • F5: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • F9: ambiguous (too_few_events_biological, confidence medium)
  • G6: ambiguous (ran_dry_plate_wide, confidence medium)

Answer key (stage 2)

  • Scale of uniform_gate.json gates: The common Live gate is reported as BL2-A [0, 1170] and caspase+ as BL1-A [1158, 4096], but the workspace base gates are BL2-A [-44580, 2477] and BL1-A [310.7, ...]. The tool apparently works on a different (channel/transformed) scale. The 'common' per-well values used for the reference should be re-verified in raw space before finalising tolerances.
  • B1 under the common gate: Live jumps from 69.4% to 98.6% and caspase+ from 29.8% to 42.2%. This single well drives E1_CM24h_10uM to 35.8% and reverses the scientist's main E1 24h result. The comparison was excluded from grading; confirm whether B1's BL2 distribution is anomalous.
  • Scientist's 10 uM 'about 10% reduction' claim: Holds only with the scientist's per-well gates (E1 -12 pp, E3 -7 pp). Under one gate set the reductions are 3.7-4.7 pp and E1 24h reverses. Not graded.
  • Accepting overall 'no': The scientist said partial. Under a uniform gate the CM effects are within n=2 noise, so 'no clear rescue' is defensible. Both labels are currently accepted; 'yes' is rejected.
  • Accept repeat_with_change?: Adding biological replicates and a KO-conditioned-media specificity control is a reasonable next step. It is not accepted because the scientist proceeded and no specific change is derivable from agent-visible text.
  • QC labels for low-event 10 uM KO wells and end-of-well depletion wells: Labelled ambiguous (not graded). An expert should confirm that none is unusable.
  • E10 SSC-A drift (3.51x first to last quarter): Unique on the plate; cause unknown; labelled ambiguous.
  • Prism values that differ from the saved gating (A4/D4 swap, D1, D5, D6, F1, F4, F8, A5): Some may come from an older gating; the workspace is used as truth.
  • normalisation.json by-value matching: It assigned some Prism values to wells outside their condition (e.g. E1 24h DMSO rep0 -> F4; WT 48h 2 uM rep1 -> A5). The per-condition layout from the notebook map and CM_2_prism_layout.csv is used instead; the conclusion 'no normalisation' is unaffected.
  • Row G conditioned-media status: Not stated in the plan; G wells are not used in reference conditions.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • Gate-sensitive 10 µM KO values: The scientist's per-well Live edits make the 10 µM unconditioned and 24 h CM KO values depend on where the cutoff is placed (3–9 pp). These are now graded only for direction (B-DIR). Confirm this narrowing of the summary key is acceptable.
  • Live base geometry for overlap: Confirm the overlap checker uses the workspace's raw-space Live gate (BL2-A [-44579.7, 2476.96], the version A1 uses), not uniform_gate.json's [0, 1170] representation or a per-well version.
  • B-QC-EVID vacuous_score = 0: An agent that marks all 78 wells 'none' (defensible, since no well must be excluded) gets 0 on 0.5 of the QC stage. Alternative: move the remainder share to B-QC-TRAP.
  • B-DECISION accepted actions: repeat_with_change (add biological replicates and a KO-conditioned media control) is scientifically reasonable but scores 0 on a 0.35 share. If accepted, B-DECISION-CHANGE would need a specific change, and none is notebook-derivable.
  • B-ANS accepting 'no': The scientist wrote partial; 'no' is defensible under one gate set. Confirm.
  • QC ambiguous labels (40 wells): Low-event 10 µM KO wells, plate-wide end-of-well depletion (C12, D1, D7, G6; last10 ratio 0.35–0.39), E10 SSC drift 3.51× and B1's gate sensitivity: an expert should confirm that none is unusable.
  • $OP operator name and 'mlk' initials in the FCS files: Personal data visible to the agent. Strip $OP in the task copies; decide whether to rename the files (counts.csv keys on file names).
  • plan.md provenance: The staining protocol and cytometer settings come from the 2022-12-02 day block and are assumed unchanged for 16-Dec. SYTOX was added to the Materials list. Row G conditioned_media is 'not stated'.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Stage budgets: the v3 spec (summary 0.30, no communication stage) was used rather than the generic stage-5 text (summary 0.25, communication 0.05). Confirm.
  • B-QC-EVID carries 0.075 (half the QC stage) with vacuous_score = 0. An agent that defensibly flags no well loses it. Consider moving part of this share to B-QC-TRAP.
  • B-DECISION (0.1225) does not accept repeat_with_change (replicates plus a KO-conditioned media specificity control), which is scientifically reasonable. Confirm the exclusion.
  • B-ANS accepts 'no' in addition to the scientist's 'partial'. Confirm.
  • Confirm that the 40 ambiguous QC wells (low-yield 10 µM KO wells, end-of-well depletion wells, E10 SSC drift, B1) contain no unusable well.
  • Strip $OP (operator name) from the task FCS copies; decide on the 'mlk' initials in file names.

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions). Bars for small populations (full credit near J 0.25) are lenient. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Exact prompt given to the model (instruction.md)

Conditioned-media caspase plate (16-Dec-2022): analyse, conclude, decide

You are the analyst for this experiment: analyse the plate, answer the plan's question, and recommend the next step.

Inputs (read-only)

path content
/task/inputs/plan.md Notebook plan for this run: purpose, rationale, reagents, protocol, plate maps, cytometer settings
/task/inputs/plate_layout.csv One row per FCS file: file, well, sample, cell_line, camptothecin, conditioned_media (plate-map wording)
/task/inputs/raw/ 78 FCS 3.1 files (Thermo Attune NxT, acquired 16-Dec-2022), wells A1–F12 and G1–G6

Environment

  • Network. None.

Channels

Channel names are the labels stored inside the FCS files ($PnS). They may be out of date. Use the plan's reagent list and cytometer settings to decide what each detector measured.

detector Name in the FCS file ($PnS)
FSC-A / FSC-H / FSC-W FSC-A / FSC-H / FSC-W
SSC-A / SSC-H / SSC-W SSC-A / SSC-H / SSC-W
BL1-A / BL1-H / BL1-W AAV-GFP-GFP-A / AAV-GFP-GFP-H / AAV-GFP-GFP-W

Time Time

Deliverables (all in /task/outputs/)

1. gates.xml

  • Your gating strategy as GatingML 2.0, written with flowkit.export_gatingml (see Software). It must load with flowkit.parse_gating_xml("/task/outputs/gates.xml").
  • Every population in counts.csv except all_events must be a gate in this file with exactly the same name.
  • These gates must be the ones that produced counts.csv.

2. counts.csv

Columns, in order: file, well, population, role, parent, count, pct_of_parent.

Rows - One row per FCS file × population, covering all 78 files. - Every file has the same population set.

Columns - file: exact FCS file name. well: as in plate_layout.csv. - population: your gate names (no commas). Each file also has one row with population = all_events, role = other, parent = none, count = total events and pct_of_parent empty. - role ∈ {cells, singlets, live, marker_positive, other}. - Each of cells, singlets, live and marker_positive is used by exactly one population, the same population in every file. - other may be used by any number of populations. - parent: the parent population's name (another population of the same file, or all_events). Use none only for all_events. - count: integer number of events in the population. - pct_of_parent: 100 × count / parent count.

3. flags.csv

Columns, in order: file, well, issue_type, evidence, decision. Exactly one row per FCS file (78 rows).

  • Flag any well whose data should not be used, with evidence.
  • issue_type ∈ {none, clog, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabel, other}. If a well has several issues, give the main one here and describe the rest in evidence.
  • evidence: required unless issue_type = none. It must cite at least one number taken from the data.
  • decision ∈ {keep, keep_with_note, exclude}.
  • Wells marked exclude must appear in answer.json → excluded_wells and must not be used in condition_summary.csv.

4. condition_summary.csv

Columns, in order: condition, wells, n_wells_used, mean, sd, metric_definition, normalisation_applied. One row per condition you define.

  • condition: your name for the condition. Names must be unique and contain no commas.
  • wells: the plate wells used, separated by ; (e.g. X1;X2).
  • n_wells_used: integer, equal to the number of wells listed.
  • mean, sd: computed across the listed wells, in the units of your metric. Leave sd empty when n_wells_used = 1.
  • metric_definition: which population counts form the numerator and the denominator, or another exact definition.
  • normalisation_applied: none, or the exact formula used.

5. figure.png

The main result chart.

6. report.md

These headings, in this order: ## Question, ## Methods, ## Results, ## Conclusion, ## Caveats, ## Recommendation.

7. answer.json

{"question": str,
 "comparisons": [{"comparison": str, "a": <condition>, "b": <condition>,
                  "direction": "increase"|"decrease"|"no_clear_change",
                  "magnitude": str, "confidence": "high"|"medium"|"low"}],
 "overall_answer": "yes: ..." | "partial: ..." | "no: ...",
 "assay_verdict": "fit_for_purpose"|"needs_optimisation"|"not_fit_for_purpose",
 "next_action": <ACTION>,
 "next_change": {"what": str, "from": str, "to": str, "why": str},
 "excluded_wells": [well IDs],
 "caveats": [str]}
  • comparisons: at least one comparison.
  • a and b must be condition values from condition_summary.csv.
  • direction describes a relative to b (increase = a higher than b).
  • magnitude states the size of the difference, with a number.
  • overall_answer must start with yes:, partial: or no:.
  • next_action ∈ {proceed_as_planned, repeat_unchanged, repeat_with_change, optimise_reagent_or_setting, change_treatment_or_timing, switch_assay, stop}.
  • next_change: the change you recommend, as an object: what (the step, reagent or condition to change), from (its value as run), to (the value you recommend) and why. Use empty strings if you recommend no change.
  • excluded_wells: well IDs (e.g. G1) that have decision = exclude in flags.csv. Use [] if there are none.

Constraints

  • Time budget: 5 hours.
  • Do not modify anything in /task/inputs/.

Software (FlowKit version of this task)

  • Python 3 with FlowKit 1.2.3 (plus flowio, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, openpyxl) is installed. There is no graphical analysis program.
  • Load each file with flowkit.Sample(path). Build one flowkit.GatingStrategy for all wells, with flowkit.Dimension and flowkit.gates.RectangleGate, PolygonGate or EllipsoidGate (no quadrant or Boolean gates).
  • Gate names must be valid XML IDs: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (no spaces or +).
  • One gate per reported population, named exactly as the population and nested under its parent population (the first population's gate sits at the root). A population's events are its own gate within its parent.
  • Compensation. Your choice. Every gate dimension must state its compensation_ref ("uncompensated", "FCS" for the file's own spillover matrix, or the id of a matrix you add to the strategy).
  • Channels. FlowKit gate dimensions use the detector ID ($PnN, e.g. BL1-A), not the text label.
  • Transforms. You may draw gates on transformed axes (for example flowkit.transforms.LogicleTransform, added with add_transform and referenced by transformation_ref).
  • Save the strategy with flowkit.export_gatingml(strategy, open("/task/outputs/gates.xml", "wb")) and check that it reloads with flowkit.parse_gating_xml.
  • Counts. counts.csv must be the counts these saved gates give on each file (strategy.gate_sample(sample)), with no per-well changes.
  • Looking at data. Save plots as PNG files and open the image files to view them.

How you work

You work in a terminal (bash, working directory /task).

  • Inputs are in /task/inputs/ (read-only). Write every deliverable to /task/outputs/. Only that folder is collected for grading.
  • Limits. There is no limit on the number of actions; the only limit is the time budget above. Save gates.xml and your output files early and often.

Input files in /task/inputs (read-only)

inputs/plan.md

Plan: Caspase activity assay development with progranulin conditioned media (H4 cells)

Source: lab notebook entry (target PGRN; assay development; cell-based; flow; cell type H4). This plan covers the plate acquired on 16-Dec-2022. People's names, and all text written after acquisition, have been removed.

Purpose

To determine if progranulin conditioned media can restore wild-type levels of caspase activity in H4 GRN KO cells.

Rationale

Previous literature evidence suggests that applying exogenous progranulin to cells can restore molecular phenotypes in progranulin deficient lines. Our previous experiment with caspase activity on H4 GRN WT and KO cells showed that GRN KO lines had increased caspase activity. This difference was enhanced after campothesin challenge in both GRN WT and KO cells. In this experiment, we will determine if applying conditioned media from WT cell lines onto KO lines can reduce caspase activity closer to WT levels.

Materials

  • H4 WT cells
  • H4 PGRN KO E1
  • H4 PGRN KO E3
  • H4 media (DMEM + 10% FBS)
  • CellEvent Caspase-3/7 Green Flow Cytometry Assay Kit
  • SYTOX AAdvanced Dead Cell Stain
  • Camptothecin

Protocol

2022-12-12: conditioned-media donor plate

  • Passage WT H4 cells into 96 well plate (10K/well). This plate is the one the media is collected from.

Staining and acquisition (assay protocol as written in this entry)

  • Aspirate media and wash with PBS
  • Add 150uL trypsin incubate for 5min
  • Add 75uL FBS and collect into 96w round bottom plate
  • spin down 200xg for 5min
  • Add 200uL of Cell Event Caspase 3/7 Detection reagent (1:1000) in flow staining buffer. Incubate for 30min at 37C
  • Prepare SYTOX AAdvanced Dead Cell Stain at 100uM concentration by adding 1000uL DMSO to stain. Mix well
  • During the final 5 minutes of 30min Caspase incubation add 2uL of the 100uM Dead Cell stain (final concentration of 1uM)
  • Analyze the samples without fixing.

Flow cytometer settings: FSC-20; SSC-290; BL1 (caspase)-225, BL2 (AAddvanced Dead Cell Stain)-350

Acquisition

  • Instrument: Thermo Attune NxT.
  • Date: 16-Dec-2022.
  • Files: 78 FCS files, one per well (A1–F12 and G1–G6).

Required outputs (written to /task/outputs)

pathformatcolumns / schema
outputs/gates.xmlCytoflow workflow saved from the GUIGatingML 2.0 written with flowkit.export_gatingml; loads with flowkit.parse_gating_xml; one gate per reported population, same names
outputs/counts.csvper-file x per-population countsColumns file, well, population, role, parent, count, pct_of_parent. One row per FCS file x population; same population set for all 78 files. One all_events row per file (role other, parent none, count = total events, pct_of_parent empty). role in {cells, singlets, live, marker_positive, other}; each of cells/singlets/live/marker_positive used by exactly one population (the same in every file). parent = a population of the same file or all_events; none only for all_events. count integer; pct_of_parent = 100 x count / parent count.
outputs/flags.csvper-well QC flagsColumns file, well, issue_type, evidence, decision. Exactly one row per FCS file (78). issue_type in {none, clog, ran_dry, too_few_events, saturation, bad_control, mislabel, other}; decision in {keep, keep_with_note, exclude}; evidence required unless issue_type = none and must cite at least one number. Wells with decision exclude must equal answer.json excluded_wells.
outputs/condition_summary.csvper-condition summaryColumns condition, wells, n_wells_used, mean, sd, metric_definition, normalisation_applied. One row per agent-defined condition (unique names, no commas). wells = plate wells used separated by ';'. n_wells_used integer = number of wells listed. mean/sd across wells in metric units; sd empty when n_wells_used = 1. metric_definition = numerator/denominator populations or exact definition. normalisation_applied = 'none' or the exact formula.
outputs/figure.pngmain result chart (PNG)PNG image of the main result chart.
outputs/report.mdmarkdown reportHeadings in order: ## Question, ## Methods, ## Results, ## Conclusion, ## Caveats, ## Recommendation.
outputs/answer.jsonstructured answer{question: str, comparisons: [{comparison: str, a: <condition>, b: <condition>, direction: increase|decrease|no_clear_change (a relative to b), magnitude: str, confidence: high|medium|low}] (>=1 item; a and b are condition values from condition_summary.csv), overall_answer: str starting 'yes:'|'partial:'|'no:', assay_verdict: fit_for_purpose|needs_optimisation|not_fit_for_purpose, next_action: proceed_as_planned|repeat_unchanged|repeat_with_change|optimise_reagent_or_setting|change_treatment_or_timing|switch_assay|stop, next_change: str, excluded_wells: [well IDs with decision exclude in flags.csv], caveats: [str]}

Withheld from the model

itemwhy
Scientist's gating strategy, gate hierarchy, gate shapes and coordinates (Conditoned media-2.wsp)Type-B information policy: no gating strategy or workspace
Which detector carries which dye, and the explanation that the BL1 label is staleType-B policy: the agent must infer this from the plan's reagent list and cytometer settings
FlowJo counts/percentages, Prism tables (Caspase_conditioned media.pzfx) and linked result imagesAnswer-key material
This run's Results, Conclusion and Next StepsGraded conclusion and decision
Run 1 (02-Dec-2022) protocol, plate maps, results, conclusion and its failure explanationOut of scope; would leak the history of the assay and the reason for the spin-down step
Our per-file QC metrics and investigation notes on end-of-well depletion and low-event wellsDerived QC material; the agent must find issues itself
Normalisation used (none) and the metric definition (caspase+ % of Live)Type-B policy: the plan does not state them
Notebook author names, ELN folder path, operator namePersonal data / anonymisation

Ground truth = the scientist's own saved FlowJo gating and results (exact values, never shown to the model), plus expert-style QC labels and documented conclusions. The exemplar deliverables are what a top-quality submission looks like.

Reference gating strategy (scientist's FlowJo workspace)

population (task name)scientist populationgate typechannelsparentreproducible in Cytoflow
Cells/CellsEllipsoidGateFSC-A, SSC-Aall_eventsPolygon gate on FSC-A vs SSC-A approximating the ellipse around the main cell cloud. Cytoflow has no ellipse gate.
Single Cells/Cells/Single CellsPolygonGate (4 vertices)SSC-A, SSC-HCellsPolygon gate on SSC-A vs SSC-H along the singlet diagonal, applied to Cells.
Live/Cells/Single Cells/LiveRectangleGate 1-DBL2-ASingle CellsThreshold or Range on 'AAdvanced livedead-A' (BL2-A) keeping SYTOX AAdvanced-negative events. G1 (no stain) and G2 (L/D only) set the cutoff.
caspase+/Cells/Single Cells/Live/caspase+RectangleGate 1-DBL1-ALiveThreshold on 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A' (BL1-A; stale label, actually CellEvent caspase-3/7 Green) above the negative peak. G1 (no stain) and G2 (L/D only) set the background; G3 (caspase only) is the positive reference.
How each gate was placed (rationale)
populationplacement rationaleoverlap note
CellsEllipse around the main FSC-A/SSC-A cell cloud, excluding low-FSC debris. Debris is heavy in camptothecin-treated KO wells, where Cells is 27-45% of events, compared with >90% in DMSO WT and control wells.Agents can only approximate an ellipse with a polygon. Use the finaliser's FlowCAP-derived zero/full, and expect lower overlap than for polygon or rectangle gates.
Single CellsDiagonal polygon on SSC-A vs SSC-H that keeps about 90-97% of Cells in every well.Standard polygon. High overlap is expected because almost all of Cells is inside.
Live1-D gate on BL2-A covering the SYTOX AAdvanced-negative peak. G1 (no stain) is 100% inside. G2 (L/D only) shows the dead-cell tail above the cutoff.The scientist edited this gate per well (25 versions). Grade overlap against the base (most common) geometry only. The live/dead boundary is shallow in camptothecin-treated KO wells, so small cutoff shifts move Live % by 5-30 pp (uniform_gate.json). Use the finaliser defaults; do not tighten.
caspase+1-D gate on BL1-A above the CellEvent-negative peak. About 4.8% of G1 (no stain) and 5.5% of G2 (L/D only) fall above the cutoff (autofluorescence background); G3 (caspase only) is 11.2%.4 per-well versions (C4, D1, D9, E9); grade against the base geometry. Exact reproduction is possible with a Threshold. The marker gate must sit on BL1-A (B-AF-03).

Grading tolerances per population
populationabs_pprel_pct_if_smallsmall_threshold_pctmin_parent_eventsjustification
Cells6.020.010.01000The ellipse must be approximated by a polygon. Ellipse gates drift 1-20% in open-source re-gating. Cells % spans 27-94% across wells and depends on how much debris is cut.
Single Cells2.510.010.01000Polygon on a tight diagonal with 90-97% of Cells inside. Flowkit vs FlowJo agreed within 0.3 pp.
Live6.025.010.05001-D cutoff on a shallow live/dead boundary in camptothecin-treated KO wells. The scientist's per-well edits move Live by up to 29 pp, and a uniform cutoff moves KO wells by 5-30 pp. Only a wide tolerance is fair to a single agent gate.
caspase+3.025.010.05001-D threshold. Most wells are 7-45%. Background in unstained G1 is about 4.8%. Common vs per-well gates differ by 0-12 pp in KO wells, mostly through the Live parent; 3 pp covers reasonable threshold placement. Leaves under 200 events are excluded.

Must-have caveats

  • Only 2 duplicate wells per condition from one plate (one biological run). CM effects of about 3-5 pp are comparable to duplicate spread (e.g. E1 unconditioned 10 uM 36.5 vs 29.5; E1 24h CM 10 uM 42.2 vs 29.4). No statistics are possible.
  • There is no specificity control (KO-conditioned or PGRN-depleted media) and PGRN in the CM was not measured. CM also lowers caspase+ without camptothecin in E1 (48h DMSO -5.8 pp), so the effect may not be PGRN-specific.
  • Results depend on live/dead gate placement in camptothecin-treated KO wells, where the SYTOX AAdvanced boundary is shallow. A single gate set shifts KO values by several pp.
  • Low cell yield in several 10 uM KO wells (C5 3151 events with about 600 live; F5, B9, F9, C9, E9, E5 <4500 events).
  • Caspase+ % is raw and includes about 5% background seen in the unstained control (G1); no background subtraction.
  • The BL1 channel is stored as 'AAV-GFP-GFP' but measures CellEvent caspase-3/7.

Unacceptable conclusions

  • WT conditioned media increases caspase activation in KO cells (opposite direction; this was the failed earlier run's pattern, not this plate's).
  • Conditioned media fully restores KO caspase activity to WT levels.
  • KO and WT do not differ in caspase activation.
  • Statistically significant rescue, or a fitted dose-response / EC50, from n=2 duplicate wells.
  • Mechanistic claims that progranulin in the media causes the reduction (PGRN was not measured, and there is no specificity control).
  • Excluding the low-event 10 uM KO wells (C5, F5, B9, F9, C9, E9, E5) and then drawing conclusions about 10 uM without those duplicates.

B2_flowkit: H4 WT vs PGRN-KO cleaved-caspase-3 ICFC antibody test (26-Oct-2022): analyse, conclude, decide

Internal id: B_EXP22004082_26_Oct_2022_flowkit

FlowKit version. Same plate, answer key and scoring as B2, but the system works in a terminal with Python and FlowKit instead of drawing gates on screen in Cytoflow, and hands in its gates as a GatingML file (gates.xml). The check that gating was done in the GUI is removed.

Task B (v3): is this antibody apoptosis assay good enough? (18 wells, 26-Oct-2022)

In one sentence: analyse a small plate testing a new antibody-based apoptosis assay in normal vs progranulin-knock-out cells, and decide whether the lab should keep using it.

The experiment, in plain terms

  • Cells. H4 cells: WT and two progranulin knock-out clones (E1, E3).
  • Staining. Cells are fixed and stained with an antibody against active caspase-3, which marks apoptotic cells, at two dilutions. A dead-cell dye (Zombie NIR) is added too.
  • Controls. Per cell line: unstained, antibody only, dead-cell dye only.

What the agent must decide

  • detectors, gates and the metric;
  • whether to subtract each line's background: the scientist did, but the plan doesn't say so;
  • the comparisons;
  • the conclusion;
  • the assay verdict and the next action.

Time: 4 hours.

The scientist's answer

  • The signal is tiny. After background subtraction, caspase-positive cells are at most about 5% everywhere: WT 1.1%, E1 0.3%, E3 3.4%.
  • E3's apparent increase is mostly background. Its dye-only control, with no antibody at all, shows about 8% "positive".
  • The scientist's decision: "much less sensitive… possibly needs optimisation of antibody concentration… we will stick to [the other assay]".
  • Accepted next actions: switch assay, optimise a reagent, or repeat with a change. The judge also checks that the change named matches.
  • In the old version (v2), 0 of 10 agent attempts made this call.
  • One more finding: the scientist's workspace has a broken live gate on well A11, which the one-gate-set rebuild fixes.

Rubric: 15 scored items

  • Gating: 20%.
  • QC: 15%. The trap is the E3 background control.
  • Summary: 30%, background-subtracted as the scientist did.
  • Conclusion and decision: 35%, including the next action (9%) and the specific change (3.5%).

What the agent is given, and what it isn't

  • Given:
  • the scientist's notebook plan up to this run, in their own words: aim, design, protocol, reagents, cytometer settings, plate map;
  • the raw files;
  • a Cytoflow project with the files loaded;
  • the exact output formats.
  • Not given:
  • which detector carries which dye (the file labels may be out of date; the plan's reagent list is the clue);
  • which wells are controls;
  • what metric to use, whether to normalise, which comparisons to make, what a bad well looks like;
  • the scientist's results, conclusion or next step.

This is the information the scientist had before writing their conclusion, and nothing we worked out.

What the agent hands in

File What it is
workflow.flow The saved Cytoflow project with the agent's own gates.
counts.csv Counts per well × population, each population tagged with its role (cells / singlets / live / marker-positive).
flags.csv One row per well: issue type, numeric evidence, keep or exclude.
condition_summary.csv The agent's own conditions: which wells, mean, SD, metric, normalisation.
figure.png A plot (format-checked only).
report.md Question, Methods, Results, Conclusion, Caveats, Recommendation.
answer.json The comparisons (direction, size, confidence), an overall yes / partial / no, an assay verdict (fit / needs optimising / not fit) and a next action from a fixed list, the same in every task (proceed, repeat unchanged, repeat with a change, optimise a reagent or setting, change treatment or timing, switch assay, stop), plus what to change.

How it's scored (0–1) — Task B v4, 2026-11-09: six items, no double counting

Share (approx.) Item In plain terms
21% Gates Do the agent's gates pick out the same cells as the scientist's? Upstream gates and the marker gate count equally. Full credit only at the median agreement between human experts.
16% Data quality Excluding the wrong wells zeroes this item (a requirement, not points). Then: does the evidence for each flagged well quote numbers that are true for that file, and does the report spot the plate's main data problem (judge, yes/no)?
32% Summary numbers Condition means recomputed from the agent's own gates, and the differences between conditions, each within the scientist's own replicate noise.
6% Answer to the question The direction called for each comparison and the overall yes / partial / no. They count less because they mostly follow from the numbers above.
15% Next step The next action matches what the scientist actually decided, and names the specific change (judge, yes/no).
6–11% Findings and limits Key findings that aren't already scored elsewhere, no over-claiming, and the key caveats (judge, yes/no each).

Shares vary a little by plate: plates without a summary stage have five items, and claims that only repeated a graded comparison or the data problem were removed.

Automatic zero: - the workflow is missing; - coverage is under 80%; - the marker gate is on the wrong detector; - the counts don't come from the saved workflow; - the gating wasn't done in the GUI.

A main conclusion opposite to the scientist's is flagged, but doesn't change the score.

Two rules behind the answer key: - It is rebuilt with one gate set for all wells, because the scientists sometimes adjusted gates well by well. - A scientist decision or claim is only graded if this plate's data actually supports it.

The judge (a model from the other company) only answers yes/no questions; every fractional score comes from code.

Summary (for maintainers, not shown to the model)

Second run of notebook entry EXP22004082. The scientist tested an intracellular-flow (ICFC) assay using a cleaved caspase-3 (Asp175) Alexa Fluor 488 antibody in H4 WT and two PGRN-KO clones (E1, E3). One 24-well plate was seeded on 25-Oct, and the cells were harvested and stained on 26-Oct: Zombie NIR fixable viability dye, then fix/perm, then antibody at 1:100 (replicate -1) or 1:50 (replicates -2, -3). Each line also has no-stain, caspase-only (1:100) and zombie-only control wells. All 18 tubes were acquired on the Attune NxT (96-well plate rows A and B; BL1 = caspase antibody, RL3 = Zombie NIR) and gated in FlowJo as Cells, then Single Cells, then a Zombie-dim/live polygon (FSC-A vs RL3-A), then caspase+ (BL1-A threshold). The Prism values are caspase+ % of live minus the same line's zombie-only well. The scientist concluded that caspase+ cells were very low in all lines and that the assay was much less sensitive than the CellEvent kit tested a week earlier, with a similar trend of E3 being higher. The scientist noted that antibody concentration might need optimising, but decided to stick with the CellEvent assay.

Natural traps in this plate (not hinted to the model)

typewhere
stale_channel_labelBL1-A in all 18 files is labelled 'AAV-GFP-GFP-A' but carries the cleaved caspase-3 AF488 antibody
normalisation_stepPrism values = caspase+ % of live minus the same line's zombie-only well (A3/A9/B3); 7/9 within 0.1 pp
otherThe scientist's live gate is a Zombie-dim band whose lower edge sits above the unstained level. The no-stain and caspase-only wells (A1, A2, A7, A8, B1, B2) therefore have about 0 events in the live gate and cannot be read through the full hierarchy. The agent must decide how to use the controls.
otherHigh BL1 background in E3. The E3 zombie-only well B3 (no antibody) has 8.04% of live in the caspase+ gate, versus 0.16% (A3) and 0.32% (A9). The E3 stained wells (6.55–12.8%) are close to that background, and B4 falls below it after subtraction.
too_few_eventsWT control wells are low: A2 3,149 events (32 ev/s), A3 5,742, A1 6,969, versus 13k–59k in other wells. A2 is a control that cannot be gated past the live gate anyway.
saturationAll E3 wells (B1–B6): FSC-A 2.86–3.87% and SSC-A 3.40–4.11% saturated, versus ≤0.38% in row A. This is moderate and probably biological (cell size/clumping) or a scatter-setting matter.
otherEnd-of-run rate drop is mild only: A1 0.59, A2 0.63, A8 0.69, A5 0.70 last-10% rate over median. There is no clog signature (max_bin_over_median ≤1.6; low_rate_bins ≤1).

Expert review list

Everything any generation stage flagged for an expert, plus standing caveats. Nothing here is graded until an expert decides.

Task brief and plate layout (stage 1)

  • Run-1 context removed. plan.md omits run 1 (CellEvent caspase-3/7 kit on the same lines, 20-Oct) per the 'remove earlier runs entirely' rule. The scientist's conclusion compares sensitivity with that assay and decides to stick with it. Only the Materials list hints that the CellEvent kit exists, so claims or decisions phrased as 'less sensitive than the previous assay' are not derivable from agent inputs. Should a neutral line be added (e.g. 'the CellEvent kit was run on these lines on 20-Oct-2022; results not provided'), or should stage 3 restrict accepted decisions and claims accordingly?
  • Scientist decision to action mapping. The decision combines 'possibly needs further optimization of antibody concentration' with 'we will stick to using [the CellEvent] assay'. The candidate actions are switch_assay (scientist's actual call) and optimise_reagent_or_setting. Please confirm in stage 3.
  • A4/B4 reference values. Prism A4/B4 appear to come from the pre-edit common Cells gate (inferred, see generator_notes). Should the summary reference use the saved per-well-edited counts, the common-gate counts that a Cytoflow user will reproduce, or exclude B4 from strict numeric grading?
  • E3 BL1 background. E3 zombie-only background is 8% caspase+ with no antibody, so E3 'elevation' after background subtraction is small and inconsistent (B4 is negative with saved gating). Does the data support the scientist's 'similar trend with E3 higher'? With background subtraction, E3 > WT holds for B5/B6 but not B4 (saved gating); without subtraction, E3 is clearly higher. Expert review is needed before B-DIR acceptance sets are fixed.
  • Low event counts. Are the WT control wells (A1 6,969; A2 3,149; A3 5,742 events) to be labelled ambiguous rather than unusable? A2 is a caspase-only control with few events, and A3 is the WT background well used for subtraction.
  • E3 saturation. Is the E3-row scatter saturation (~3–4% FSC-A/SSC-A) benign (ambiguous), or should it be treated as a saturation flag?
  • Caspase-only controls. Can the caspase-only wells (A2, A8, B2) be used to judge antibody specificity at all, given the scientist's Zombie-dim live gate excludes them? Graders should accept agent approaches that evaluate them at the singlet level.

QC labels to confirm (stage 2)

  • A1: ambiguous (too_few_events / end-of-run rate drop, confidence medium)
  • A2: ambiguous (too_few_events / end-of-run rate drop, confidence medium)
  • A3: ambiguous (too_few_events, confidence medium)
  • B1: ambiguous (saturation (moderate, row-wide) / scatter drift, confidence medium)
  • B2: ambiguous (saturation (moderate, row-wide) / scatter drift, confidence medium)
  • B3: ambiguous (saturation (moderate) plus high BL1 background in a no-antibody control, confidence medium)
  • B4: ambiguous (saturation (moderate, row-wide) / scatter drift, confidence medium)
  • B5: ambiguous (saturation (moderate) / one low-rate bin, confidence medium)
  • B6: ambiguous (saturation (moderate, row-wide) / scatter drift, confidence medium)

Answer key (stage 2)

  • Derivability of switch_assay / 'less sensitive than previous assay': Run-1 (CellEvent) results were removed from plan.md. The agent sees only that the CellEvent kit is in Materials. The sensitivity comparison (C4) is not graded, but the switch_assay decision rests partly on it.
  • E1_vs_WT accepted directions ['decrease','no_clear_change']: The reference difference (−0.76 pp) exceeds the replicate SD (0.14–0.20), so strictly only 'decrease' qualifies. Both values are at the assay floor (<1.5%), and the scientist did not distinguish E1 from WT, so no_clear_change is also accepted. Please confirm.
  • E3_vs_WT accepted only 'increase': Increase holds with the common gate (all E3 > all WT) and without normalisation. With the scientist's saved, edited gating, B4 is −1.49 and the difference is within noise. An agent arguing no_clear_change because of E3's 8% background would be marked wrong. Confirm whether no_clear_change should also be accepted.
  • Tool-reported direction flips (E1_vs_WT, E3_vs_E1): These are artefacts of A11's duplicate nested gate name in the 'own' evaluation (live = 214). With FlowJo-saved counts there is no flip. E1_vs_WT is kept as a required comparison on that basis.
  • Normalisation grading: Background subtraction is not stated in the plan. Agents reporting raw caspase+ % of live (WT 1.25, E1 0.66, E3 11.54) are scientifically defensible. Decide whether B-SUM accepts the raw version when normalisation_applied = none.
  • Uniform reference is from open-source re-evaluation: The 'common' values carry the known ~4% singlet-count offset versus FlowJo. Caspase+ % of live is barely affected (A10 0.538 vs saved 0.54), but absolute counts are.
  • repeat_with_change accepted: Adding a camptothecin positive control is good practice and supported by the plate's lack of one, but it was not the scientist's call. Confirm whether it should be accepted for B-DECISION.
  • Low-event WT controls and E3 saturation labelled ambiguous: A1/A2/A3 (3.1k–7.0k events) and the B1–B6 scatter saturation (2.9–4.1%) are borderline and not graded either way. An expert should confirm that none is unusable.
  • Cause of the E3 BL1 background in B3: Possibilities are autofluorescence of larger or clumped E3 cells, or nonspecific Zombie spill. It cannot be resolved from the scientist's gating because the E3 unstained and caspase-only wells are excluded by the live gate.

Criteria held out of the rubric (stages 3-4)

  • Normalisation acceptance (B-SUM-MEANS/DIFFS): Subtraction is the scientist's method but is not in the plan. If raw is to be accepted when an agent declares normalisation_applied = none, use these unnormalised common-gate references: WT 1.2547, E1 0.6610, E3 11.5436. Diffs (a−b): E1_vs_WT +0.5937, E3_vs_WT −10.2889. 1:50 subsets: WT 1.3592, E1 0.7224, E3 12.4260.
  • Diff sign convention: B-SUM-DIFFS now uses mean(a) − mean(b), following stage 2's citation of the spec. Confirm the comparison_differences_scaled implementation; if it uses b − a, negate ref_diff (E1 −0.7613, E3 +2.3349; alternatives −0.8044, +3.1128).
  • Checker support for 'alternatives', 'swap_handling' and 'stat_by_issue_type': These parameters were added for fairness. If the checkers cannot use them, drop them and record dilution-split analyses and 'other'-type QC flags as residual risks.
  • E3_vs_WT accepted direction: Only 'increase' is accepted. Under the common gate, +2.33 pp is ≈2.5× the pooled SE with n=3 per side (Welch df ≈2, not formally significant), and all E3 wells exceed all WT wells. Under saved gating, +1.36 pp is within noise. Decide whether no_clear_change (e.g. from an agent emphasising the B3 background) should also be accepted.
  • E1_vs_WT accepted direction: Only 'decrease' is accepted (≈5× SE). Both lines are at the assay floor and the scientist did not distinguish them; confirm.
  • Restore run-1 notebook text to plan.md: The scientist had run 1's protocol, conclusions and next steps before writing this run's conclusion; the B policy supports including them. They frame the question (is the antibody 'an even more robust flow assay' than CellEvent?) and strengthen the derivability of switch_assay. If restored, keep the result-file links out and re-run the leakage scan; the criteria stay valid.
  • repeat_with_change in B-DECISION: Plate-supported (no positive control) but not the scientist's call; confirm acceptance.
  • A7 in the fine set: A7 is an unstained control with clean acquisition metrics. An agent may exclude it for having an empty Zombie-dim gate, which fails QC-SET; confirm this should count as a false alarm.
  • Ambiguous labels: Low-event WT controls (A1 6969, A2 3149, A3 5742) and the E3-row scatter saturation (FSC-A 2.86–3.87%, SSC-A 3.40–4.11%) are ungraded; an expert should confirm none is unusable.
  • Cause of the B3 BL1 background: Possibly autofluorescence of larger or clumped E3 cells (consistent with the E3 scatter saturation) or Zombie spillover. It does not affect grading, but it affects how strongly the trap should be emphasised.
  • Regenerate 02_expected_values.csv exclusions: The table excludes only A4/A11/B4. It should also exclude Live and caspase+ in A1, A2, A7, A8, B1 and B2, and caspase+ in A3, A4 (common <200), A5 and A9 for overlap grading, and it must reference the common Cells geometry.

Weights and rules (stage 5)

  • Stage-weight conflict: the stage-5 prompt lists summary 0.25 + communication 0.05, but the v3 type-B task_type_spec lists summary 0.30 and no communication stage. The v3 values are used here; confirm.
  • Normalisation acceptance: should B-SUM-MEANS and B-SUM-DIFFS also accept the unnormalised references (WT 1.2547, E1 0.6610, E3 11.5436; diffs a−b: E1_vs_WT +0.5937, E3_vs_WT −10.2889) when the agent declares normalisation_applied = none?

  • B-DIR E1_vs_WT: only 'decrease' is accepted (≈5× pooled SE). Both lines are at the assay floor; confirm.
  • B-DECISION: confirm that repeat_with_change is accepted alongside switch_assay and optimise_reagent_or_setting.
  • Restore run-1 notebook text (protocol, conclusions, next steps; no result links) to plan.md? This would strengthen the derivability of switch_assay and of the CellEvent arm of B-DECISION-CHANGE.

  • Confirm the ambiguous labels: the low-event WT controls A1, A2, A3 and the E3-row scatter saturation (B1–B6).

Standing caveats (always review)

  • Gate thresholds come from FlowCAP-I expert agreement (blood immune cells, eight analysts without shared instructions). Bars for small populations (full credit near J 0.25) are lenient. Re-gating 3-4 files by a local expert would give a better anchor (notes/05_overlap_threshold_provenance.md).

Analyse the 26-Oct-2022 H4 caspase ICFC plate, answer the plan's question, recommend the next step

You are the analyst for this experiment: analyse the plate, answer the plan's question, and recommend the next step.

Inputs (read-only)

Path Content

/task/inputs/plate_layout.csv One row per FCS file: file, well, sample, cell_line (sample = plate-map label as written in the notebook)
